Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 37, verse 1–23:

Meccan; it has three thousand, eight hundred and twenty-six letters, eight hundred and sixty words, and one hundred and eighty-two verses.

Kamil ibn Ahmad al-Mufid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Warraq informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus told us, saying: Salam ibn Salim told us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir al-Amili told us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Saffat will be given the reward of ten good deeds for every jinn and devil, the rebellious devils will keep far away from him, he will be free from shirk, and his two guardian angels will testify for him on the Day of Resurrection that he was a believer in the messengers." [85] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/293.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By those who range in ranks,﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Masruq, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: it means the ranks of the angels in the heavens, like the ranks of people in the world for prayer. It was also said: they are the angels who line up their wings in the air, standing in it until He commands them with what He wills. It was also said: they are the birds, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿And the birds in ranks﴾

and His saying:

﴿Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading their wings in ranks?﴾ [[Surah al-Mulk: 19.]]

And al-saff (the rank): the arrangement of a group in a line, like the rows in prayer and in battle.

﴿And those who drive with a driving,﴾ meaning the angels drive the clouds and push them along. Qatadah said: they are the admonitions of the Qur'an.

﴿And those who recite the remembrance,﴾ meaning Jibril and the angels recite the books of Allah; this is from Mujahid and al-Suddi. It was also said: they are the group of Qur'an reciters. All of these are plurals of plurals: al-saffah is the plural of al-saff, and al-saffat is the plural of al-saffah, and likewise their two companions. It was also said: it is an oath by Allah, the Exalted, with the implied meaning: "And by the Lord of the ranks."

﴿Indeed, your God is One.﴾ This is the object of the oath. Muqatil said: because the disbelievers of Makkah said: ﴿Has he made the gods into one god?﴾ So Allah swore by these: ﴿Indeed, your God is One.﴾ Al-A'mash, Abu 'Amr and Hamzah all read it with idgham (assimilation), and the rest read it with bayan (clear pronunciation).

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the easts.﴾ That is, the places where the sun rises. Allah created for the sun three hundred and sixty openings in the east and three hundred and sixty openings in the west, according to the number of the days of the year; it rises each day from one of them and sets in one of them, so these are the easts and the wests.

Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Makhladi informed us by dictation, saying: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Thaqafi informed us by dictation, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Umar ibn Mani' (truthful and trustworthy) told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, from 'Amarah ibn Abi Hafsah, from 'Ikrimah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said:

"The sun rises every year from three hundred and sixty openings; it rises each day from one opening and does not return to that opening except on that day of the following year. And it rises only while unwilling, so it says: 'My Lord, do not make me rise upon Your servants, for I see them disobeying You and doing Your disobedience.'" He said: "Have you not heard what Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said:

... until it is dragged and [whipped]?

I said: 'O my master, is the sun whipped?' He said: 'May your father's teeth be damaged! The rhyme forced him to say "jald" (whipped).'"

It was also said: every place upon which the sun has shone is a "mashriq" (east), and every place upon which it has set is a "maghrib" (west), as though he meant the Lord of all that the sun has risen upon. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 29/109.]]

﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment, the stars,﴾ Asim, in the narration of Abu Bakr, read (bi-zinatin) with tanwin and (al-kawakiba) in the accusative, meaning: by Our adorning the stars; it was also said: "I mean the stars." Hamzah and Asim in the other narrations read (bi-zinatin) with tanwin and (al-kawakibi) in the genitive, as a substitution (badal), meaning: with the adornment of the stars. The rest read (bi-zinati al-kawakib) with idafah (construct). Ibn 'Abbas said: it means by the light of the stars.

﴿And as a protection﴾ meaning: We protected it with protection, or We also made it a protection; this is common in the language. ﴿From every rebellious devil.﴾ A wicked one devoid of good.

﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly.﴾ As if He said: "So they cannot hear." The people of Kufa read (yassamma'una) with tashdid (doubling), meaning: they seek to listen. Mujahid said: "They used to seek to listen, but they did not hear." This is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd. The others read it with takhfif (lightening), which is the choice of Abu Hatim. ﴿To the exalted assembly﴾ means the recording angels in the heaven. ﴿And they are pelted﴾ meaning: they are struck ﴿from every side﴾ from the horizons of the heaven.

﴿Repulsed;﴾ they are kept away from the gatherings of the angels. Al-dahr and al-dahur mean: driving away and banishing. ﴿And theirs is a constant punishment,﴾ meaning: lasting. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And to Him belongs religion, constantly﴾ [[Surah al-Nahl: 52.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: severe. Al-Kalbi said: painful. It was also said: pure.

﴿Except one who snatches away a snatch,﴾ meaning one who steals and hears a word. ﴿So there follows him a piercing flame,﴾ meaning: a bright, powerful star pursues and reaches him, which does not miss; it kills, burns, or disables him. They return to eavesdropping despite knowing they will not reach it, out of hope for safety and attainment of their aim, like the rider of the sea.

﴿So ask them﴾ meaning: ask them, that is, the people of Makkah. ﴿Are they more difficult in creation, or those whom We created?﴾ meaning: from the earlier nations, whom We destroyed for their sins. It was also said: meaning the heavens, the earth, and what is between them.

It was revealed concerning Abu al-Asad ibn Kaldah; it was also said: Ubayy ibn Asad, and he was called "al-Asadayn" (the two lions) for the severity of his strength and power. Its parallel: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ [[Surah Ghafir: 57.]] and His saying: ﴿Are you more difficult in creation, or the heaven?﴾ [[Surah al-Nazi'at: 27.]]

﴿Indeed, We created them from clay, sticky.﴾ That is, good, pure clay that adheres and clings to the hand; its meaning is "lazim," with the mim substituted, as if it clings to the hand. Al-Suddi said: pure. Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: [al-Ramal] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/40; it is reported from Mujahid that he said: "al-lazib: al-lazim" (sticking).]]

﴿Rather, you wonder﴾ Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read (ʿajibtu) with a damma on the taa', which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas, in the sense that they have taken the place of those at whom one wonders. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: wonder from Allah means denial of a thing and its magnification, and this is the usage of the Arabs. It has come in a report: "Your Lord wonders at your despair and your despairing," and another report: "Allah wonders at the young man who has no youthful inclination," and similar. I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Nisaburi say: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baghdadi say:

Al-Junayd was asked about this verse and said: "Allah does not wonder at anything, but Allah agreed with His Messenger when His Messenger wondered, and so He said: ﴿And if you wonder, then wondrous is their saying﴾ [[Surah al-Ra'd: 5.]]." That is, He is according to what he says.

The others read it with a fatha on the taa', addressing the Prophet (ﷺ); this is the reading of Shurayh al-Qadi. He said: "Only one who does not know wonders, and Allah has knowledge of everything." Its meaning: "Rather, you wonder at their denial of you."

﴿And they mock﴾ they mock your wonder.

﴿And when they are reminded, they do not remember﴾ and when they are admonished, they do not heed.

﴿And when they see a sign﴾ meaning the splitting of the moon, ﴿they mock﴾ they ridicule. It was also said: some of them call on others to mock.

﴿And they say: "This is nothing but evident magic."﴾ ﴿"When we die and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?"﴾ ﴿"And our forefathers, the earlier ones?"﴾ meaning: "And our forefathers," or with the meaning of "and." ﴿Say: "Yes, and you will be humbled."﴾ humbled: abased. ﴿It will be but a single shout,﴾ meaning: the blast and the Resurrection, a single cry, ﴿and behold, they will be looking,﴾ alive. ﴿And they will say: "Woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense."﴾ ﴿"This is the Day of Judgment which you used to deny."﴾ ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions,﴾

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Madani informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Hasan al-Sufi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah told us, saying: My paternal uncle Abu Bakr told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say regarding ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions﴾: "Their counterparts." [86] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 23/56.]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: their likenesses. Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: their companions among the devils; every disbeliever with his devil in a chain. Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: everyone who did the same deeds as they did, so the people of wine with the people of wine, and the people of fornication with the people of fornication. Al-Hasan said: "and their wives" means the polytheistic women. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/73.]]

﴿And what they used to worship besides Allah﴾ in the world, ﴿so guide them﴾ meaning: call them; this was said by al-Dahhak. Ibn 'Abbas said: lead them. Ibn Kaysan said: so direct them. The Arabs call the driver "hadi" (guide), and from this it is said: "The charm is the guide of the driver." Imru' al-Qays said:

"As if the blood of the hastening ones upon its neck were the sap of henna mixed with grey hair." [[al-Sihah: 6/2534.]]

﴿To the path of Hellfire﴾ meaning: the road to the Fire.

[85] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/293.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

and His saying:

﴿Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading their wings in ranks?﴾ [[Surah al-Mulk: 19.]]

And al-saff (the rank): the arrangement of a group in a line, like the rows in prayer and in battle.

﴿And those who drive with a driving,﴾ meaning the angels drive the clouds and push them along. Qatadah said: they are the admonitions of the Qur'an.

﴿And those who recite the remembrance,﴾ meaning Jibril and the angels recite the books of Allah; this is from Mujahid and al-Suddi. It was also said: they are the group of Qur'an reciters. All of these are plurals of plurals: al-saffah is the plural of al-saff, and al-saffat is the plural of al-saffah, and likewise their two companions. It was also said: it is an oath by Allah, the Exalted, with the implied meaning: "And by the Lord of the ranks."

﴿Indeed, your God is One.﴾ This is the object of the oath. Muqatil said: because the disbelievers of Makkah said: ﴿Has he made the gods into one god?﴾ So Allah swore by these: ﴿Indeed, your God is One.﴾ Al-A'mash, Abu 'Amr and Hamzah all read it with idgham (assimilation), and the rest read it with bayan (clear pronunciation).

Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Makhladi informed us by dictation, saying: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Thaqafi informed us by dictation, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Umar ibn Mani' (truthful and trustworthy) told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, from 'Amarah ibn Abi Hafsah, from 'Ikrimah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said:

"The sun rises every year from three hundred and sixty openings; it rises each day from one opening and does not return to that opening except on that day of the following year. And it rises only while unwilling, so it says: 'My Lord, do not make me rise upon Your servants, for I see them disobeying You and doing Your disobedience.'" He said: "Have you not heard what Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said:

... until it is dragged and [whipped]?

I said: 'O my master, is the sun whipped?' He said: 'May your father's teeth be damaged! The rhyme forced him to say "jald" (whipped).'"

It was also said: every place upon which the sun has shone is a "mashriq" (east), and every place upon which it has set is a "maghrib" (west), as though he meant the Lord of all that the sun has risen upon. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 29/109.]]

﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment, the stars,﴾ Asim, in the narration of Abu Bakr, read (bi-zinatin) with tanwin and (al-kawakiba) in the accusative, meaning: by Our adorning the stars; it was also said: "I mean the stars." Hamzah and Asim in the other narrations read (bi-zinatin) with tanwin and (al-kawakibi) in the genitive, as a substitution (badal), meaning: with the adornment of the stars. The rest read (bi-zinati al-kawakib) with idafah (construct). Ibn 'Abbas said: it means by the light of the stars.

﴿And as a protection﴾ meaning: We protected it with protection, or We also made it a protection; this is common in the language. ﴿From every rebellious devil.﴾ A wicked one devoid of good.

﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly.﴾ As if He said: "So they cannot hear." The people of Kufa read (yassamma'una) with tashdid (doubling), meaning: they seek to listen. ﴿Repulsed;﴾ they are kept away from the gatherings of the angels. Al-dahr and al-dahur mean: driving away and banishing. ﴿And theirs is a constant punishment,﴾ meaning: lasting. ﴿Except one who snatches away a snatch,﴾ meaning one who steals and hears a word. ﴿So there follows him a piercing flame,﴾ meaning: a bright, powerful star pursues and reaches him, which does not miss; it kills, burns, or disables him. ﴿So ask them﴾ meaning: ask them, that is, the people of Makkah. ﴿Are they more difficult in creation, or those whom We created?﴾ meaning: from the earlier nations, whom We destroyed for their sins. It was also said: meaning the heavens, the earth, and what is between them.

﴿Indeed, We created them from clay, sticky.﴾ That is, good, pure clay that adheres and clings to the hand; its meaning is "lazim," with the mim substituted, as if it clings to the hand. Al-Suddi said: pure. Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: [al-Ramal] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/40; it is reported from Mujahid that he said: "al-lazib: al-lazim" (sticking).]]

It was also said: it is an oath by Allah, the Exalted, with the implied meaning: "And by the Lord of the ranks."

﴿Indeed, your God is One.﴾ This is the object of the oath. Muqatil said: because the disbelievers of Makkah said: ﴿Has he made the gods into one god?﴾ So Allah swore by these: ﴿Indeed, your God is One.﴾ Al-A'mash, Abu 'Amr and Hamzah all read it with idgham (assimilation), and the rest read it with bayan (clear pronunciation).

... until it is dragged and [whipped]?

[85] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/293.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

and His saying:

﴿Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading their wings in ranks?﴾ [[Surah al-Mulk: 19.]]

And al-saff (the rank): the arrangement of a group in a line, like the rows in prayer and in battle.

﴿And those who drive with a driving,﴾ meaning the angels drive the clouds and push them along. Qatadah said: they are the admonitions of the Qur'an.

﴿And those who recite the remembrance,﴾ meaning Jibril and the angels recite the books of Allah; this is from Mujahid and al-Suddi. It was also said: they are the group of Qur'an reciters. All of these are plurals of plurals: al-saffah is the plural of al-saff, and al-saffat is the plural of al-saffah, and likewise their two companions. It was also said: it is an oath by Allah, the Exalted, with the implied meaning: "And by the Lord of the ranks."

﴿Indeed, your God is One.﴾ This is the object of the oath. Muqatil said: because the disbelievers of Makkah said: ﴿Has he made the gods into one god?﴾ So Allah swore by these: ﴿Indeed, your God is One.﴾ Al-A'mash, Abu 'Amr and Hamzah all read it with idgham (assimilation), and the rest read it with bayan (clear pronunciation).

Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Makhladi informed us by dictation, saying: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Thaqafi informed us by dictation, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Umar ibn Mani' (truthful and trustworthy) told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, from 'Amarah ibn Abi Hafsah, from 'Ikrimah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said:

"The sun rises every year from three hundred and sixty openings; it rises each day from one opening and does not return to that opening except on that day of the following year. And it rises only while unwilling, so it says: 'My Lord, do not make me rise upon Your servants, for I see them disobeying You and doing Your disobedience.'" He said: "Have you not heard what Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said:

... until it is dragged and [whipped]?

I said: 'O my master, is the sun whipped?' He said: 'May your father's teeth be damaged! The rhyme forced him to say "jald" (whipped).'"

It was also said: every place upon which the sun has shone is a "mashriq" (east), and every place upon which it has set is a "maghrib" (west), as though he meant the Lord of all that the sun has risen upon. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 29/109.]]

﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment, the stars,﴾ Asim, in the narration of Abu Bakr, read (bi-zinatin) with tanwin and (al-kawakiba) in the accusative, meaning: by Our adorning the stars; it was also said: "I mean the stars." Hamzah and Asim in the other narrations read (bi-zinatin) with tanwin and (al-kawakibi) in the genitive, as a substitution (badal), meaning: with the adornment of the stars. The rest read (bi-zinati al-kawakib) with idafah (construct). Ibn 'Abbas said: it means by the light of the stars.

﴿And as a protection﴾ meaning: We protected it with protection, or We also made it a protection; this is common in the language. ﴿From every rebellious devil.﴾ A wicked one devoid of good.

﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly.﴾ As if He said: "So they cannot hear." The people of Kufa read (yassamma'una) with tashdid (doubling), meaning: they seek to listen. ﴿Repulsed;﴾ they are kept away from the gatherings of the angels. Al-dahr and al-dahur mean: driving away and banishing. ﴿And theirs is a constant punishment,﴾ meaning: lasting. ﴿Except one who snatches away a snatch,﴾ meaning one who steals and hears a word. ﴿So there follows him a piercing flame,﴾ meaning: a bright, powerful star pursues and reaches him, which does not miss; it kills, burns, or disables him. ﴿So ask them﴾ meaning: ask them, that is, the people of Makkah. ﴿Are they more difficult in creation, or those whom We created?﴾ meaning: from the earlier nations, whom We destroyed for their sins. It was also said: meaning the heavens, the earth, and what is between them.

﴿Indeed, We created them from clay, sticky.﴾ That is, good, pure clay that adheres and clings to the hand; its meaning is "lazim," with the mim substituted, as if it clings to the hand. Al-Suddi said: pure. Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: [al-Ramal] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/40; it is reported from Mujahid that he said: "al-lazib: al-lazim" (sticking).]]

﴿Rather, you wonder﴾ Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read (ʿajibtu) with a damma on the taa', which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas, in the sense that they have taken the place of those at whom one wonders. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: wonder from Allah means denial of a thing and its magnification, and this is the usage of the Arabs. It has come in a report: "Your Lord wonders at your despair and your despairing," and another report: "Allah wonders at the young man who has no youthful inclination," and similar. I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Nisaburi say: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baghdadi say:

Al-Junayd was asked about this verse and said: "Allah does not wonder at anything, but Allah agreed with His Messenger when His Messenger wondered, and so He said: ﴿And if you wonder, then wondrous is their saying﴾ [[Surah al-Ra'd: 5.]]." That is, He is according to what he says.

The others read it with a fatha on the taa', addressing the Prophet (ﷺ); this is the reading of Shurayh al-Qadi. He said: "Only one who does not know wonders, and Allah has knowledge of everything." Its meaning: "Rather, you wonder at their denial of you."

﴿And they mock﴾ they mock your wonder.

﴿And when they are reminded, they do not remember﴾ and when they are admonished, they do not heed.

﴿And when they see a sign﴾ meaning the splitting of the moon, ﴿they mock﴾ they ridicule. It was also said: some of them call on others to mock.

﴿And they say: "This is nothing but evident magic."﴾ ﴿"When we die and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?"﴾ ﴿"And our forefathers, the earlier ones?"﴾ meaning: "And our forefathers," or with the meaning of "and." ﴿Say: "Yes, and you will be humbled."﴾ humbled: abased. ﴿It will be but a single shout,﴾ meaning: the blast and the Resurrection, a single cry, ﴿and behold, they will be looking,﴾ alive. ﴿And they will say: "Woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense."﴾ ﴿"This is the Day of Judgment which you used to deny."﴾ ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions,﴾

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Madani informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Hasan al-Sufi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah told us, saying: My paternal uncle Abu Bakr told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say regarding ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions﴾: "Their counterparts." [86] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 23/56.]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: their likenesses. Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: their companions among the devils; every disbeliever with his devil in a chain. Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: everyone who did the same deeds as they did, so the people of wine with the people of wine, and the people of fornication with the people of fornication. Al-Hasan said: "and their wives" means the polytheistic women. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/73.]]

﴿And what they used to worship besides Allah﴾ in the world, ﴿so guide them﴾ meaning: call them; this was said by al-Dahhak. Ibn 'Abbas said: lead them. Ibn Kaysan said: so direct them. The Arabs call the driver "hadi" (guide), and from this it is said: "The charm is the guide of the driver." Imru' al-Qays said:

"As if the blood of the hastening ones upon its neck were the sap of henna mixed with grey hair." [[al-Sihah: 6/2534.]]

﴿To the path of Hellfire﴾ meaning: the road to the Fire.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 37, verse 1–23:

Meccan; it has three thousand, eight hundred and twenty-six letters, eight hundred and sixty words, and one hundred and eighty-two verses.

Kamil ibn Ahmad al-Mufid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Warraq informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus told us, saying: Salam ibn Salim told us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir al-Amili told us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Saffat will be given the reward of ten good deeds for every jinn and devil, the rebellious devils will keep far away from him, he will be free from shirk, and his two guardian angels will testify for him on the Day of Resurrection that he was a believer in the messengers." [85] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/293.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By those who range in ranks,﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Masruq, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: it means the ranks of the angels in the heavens, like the ranks of people in the world for prayer. It was also said: they are the angels who line up their wings in the air, standing in it until He commands them with what He wills. It was also said: they are the birds, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿And the birds in ranks﴾

and His saying:

﴿Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading their wings in ranks?﴾ [[Surah al-Mulk: 19.]]

And al-saff (the rank): the arrangement of a group in a line, like the rows in prayer and in battle.

﴿And those who drive with a driving,﴾ meaning the angels drive the clouds and push them along. Qatadah said: they are the admonitions of the Qur'an.

﴿And those who recite the remembrance,﴾ meaning Jibril and the angels recite the books of Allah; this is from Mujahid and al-Suddi. It was also said: they are the group of Qur'an reciters. All of these are plurals of plurals: al-saffah is the plural of al-saff, and al-saffat is the plural of al-saffah, and likewise their two companions. It was also said: it is an oath by Allah, the Exalted, with the implied meaning: "And by the Lord of the ranks."

﴿Indeed, your God is One.﴾ This is the object of the oath. Muqatil said: because the disbelievers of Makkah said: ﴿Has he made the gods into one god?﴾ So Allah swore by these: ﴿Indeed, your God is One.﴾ Al-A'mash, Abu 'Amr and Hamzah all read it with idgham (assimilation), and the rest read it with bayan (clear pronunciation).

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the easts.﴾ That is, the places where the sun rises. Allah created for the sun three hundred and sixty openings in the east and three hundred and sixty openings in the west, according to the number of the days of the year; it rises each day from one of them and sets in one of them, so these are the easts and the wests.

Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Makhladi informed us by dictation, saying: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Thaqafi informed us by dictation, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Umar ibn Mani' (truthful and trustworthy) told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, from 'Amarah ibn Abi Hafsah, from 'Ikrimah, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said:

"The sun rises every year from three hundred and sixty openings; it rises each day from one opening and does not return to that opening except on that day of the following year. And it rises only while unwilling, so it says: 'My Lord, do not make me rise upon Your servants, for I see them disobeying You and doing Your disobedience.'" He said: "Have you not heard what Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said:

... until it is dragged and [whipped]?

I said: 'O my master, is the sun whipped?' He said: 'May your father's teeth be damaged! The rhyme forced him to say "jald" (whipped).'"

It was also said: every place upon which the sun has shone is a "mashriq" (east), and every place upon which it has set is a "maghrib" (west), as though he meant the Lord of all that the sun has risen upon. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 29/109.]]

﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment, the stars,﴾ Asim, in the narration of Abu Bakr, read (bi-zinatin) with tanwin and (al-kawakiba) in the accusative, meaning: by Our adorning the stars; it was also said: "I mean the stars." Hamzah and Asim in the other narrations read (bi-zinatin) with tanwin and (al-kawakibi) in the genitive, as a substitution (badal), meaning: with the adornment of the stars. The rest read (bi-zinati al-kawakib) with idafah (construct). Ibn 'Abbas said: it means by the light of the stars.

﴿And as a protection﴾ meaning: We protected it with protection, or We also made it a protection; this is common in the language. ﴿From every rebellious devil.﴾ A wicked one devoid of good.

﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly.﴾ As if He said: "So they cannot hear." The people of Kufa read (yassamma'una) with tashdid (doubling), meaning: they seek to listen. Mujahid said: "They used to seek to listen, but they did not hear." This is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd. The others read it with takhfif (lightening), which is the choice of Abu Hatim. ﴿To the exalted assembly﴾ means the recording angels in the heaven. ﴿And they are pelted﴾ meaning: they are struck ﴿from every side﴾ from the horizons of the heaven.

﴿Repulsed;﴾ they are kept away from the gatherings of the angels. Al-dahr and al-dahur mean: driving away and banishing. ﴿And theirs is a constant punishment,﴾ meaning: lasting. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And to Him belongs religion, constantly﴾ [[Surah al-Nahl: 52.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: severe. Al-Kalbi said: painful. It was also said: pure.

﴿Except one who snatches away a snatch,﴾ meaning one who steals and hears a word. ﴿So there follows him a piercing flame,﴾ meaning: a bright, powerful star pursues and reaches him, which does not miss; it kills, burns, or disables him. They return to eavesdropping despite knowing they will not reach it, out of hope for safety and attainment of their aim, like the rider of the sea.

﴿So ask them﴾ meaning: ask them, that is, the people of Makkah. ﴿Are they more difficult in creation, or those whom We created?﴾ meaning: from the earlier nations, whom We destroyed for their sins. It was also said: meaning the heavens, the earth, and what is between them.

It was revealed concerning Abu al-Asad ibn Kaldah; it was also said: Ubayy ibn Asad, and he was called "al-Asadayn" (the two lions) for the severity of his strength and power. Its parallel: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ [[Surah Ghafir: 57.]] and His saying: ﴿Are you more difficult in creation, or the heaven?﴾ [[Surah al-Nazi'at: 27.]]

﴿Indeed, We created them from clay, sticky.﴾ That is, good, pure clay that adheres and clings to the hand; its meaning is "lazim," with the mim substituted, as if it clings to the hand. Al-Suddi said: pure. Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: [al-Ramal] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/40; it is reported from Mujahid that he said: "al-lazib: al-lazim" (sticking).]]

This is the Day of Recompense."﴾ ﴿"This is the Day of Judgment which you used to deny."﴾ ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions,﴾

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Madani informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Hasan al-Sufi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah told us, saying: My paternal uncle Abu Bakr told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say regarding ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions﴾: "Their counterparts." [86] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 23/56.]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: their likenesses. Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: their companions among the devils; every disbeliever with his devil in a chain. Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: everyone who did the same deeds as they did, so the people of wine with the people of wine, and the people of fornication with the people of fornication. Al-Hasan said: "and their wives" means the polytheistic women. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/73.]]

﴿And what they used to worship besides Allah﴾ in the world, ﴿so guide them﴾ meaning: call them; this was said by al-Dahhak. Ibn 'Abbas said: lead them. Ibn Kaysan said: so direct them. The Arabs call the driver "hadi" (guide), and from this it is said: "The charm is the guide of the driver." Imru' al-Qays said:

"As if the blood of the hastening ones upon its neck were the sap of henna mixed with grey hair." [[al-Sihah: 6/2534.]]

﴿To the path of Hellfire﴾ meaning: the road to the Fire.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 37, verses 24–61:

**Stop them and hold them** (waqafa, meaning "to make someone stand"). It is said: "I made him stand (waqaftuhu waqfan), so he stood (waqafa) and stood (wuquf)." **Indeed they will be questioned.** Ibn Abbas said: about "there is no god but Allah." Al-Dahhak said: about their sins. Al-Qurazi said: about all their words and deeds.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dinawari informed me, saying: Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Uqba informed us, saying: Abu Husayn ibn Numayr al-Hamdani related to us, saying:

Husayn ibn Qays al-Rahabi related to us (and he claimed that he was a truthful shaykh), saying: Ata related to us, from Abu Amr, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "The feet of the son of Adam will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is questioned about five things: about his youth, how he spent it; about his life, how he consumed it; about his wealth, from where he earned it and how he spent it; and what he did with what he knew." [87] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/35.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Saqlab related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman at Tarsus related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Khulayd related to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Yunus al-Akhtaf al-Aqtas related to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Bilal related to us, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, glorified is He, will summon one of His servants, make him stand before Him, and question him about his standing (jah) just as He questions him about his wealth." [88] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/346.]]

**What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?** That is, you do not take revenge, and they do not help one another. The guardians of the Fire say this to the disbelievers. This was the reply of Abu Jahl when he said on the day of Badr: "We are a united company that will be victorious."

Allah, the Exalted, said: **Rather, on that day they will submit.** Ibn Abbas said: "they will be humbled." Al-Hasan said: "they will be compliant." Al-Akhfash said: "they will throw down their hands" (i.e., surrender). The scholars of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "they will be yielding to what they cannot resist or avoid, like one who seeks safety in the place of conflict."

**And some of them will turn to others, questioning one another.** "They" means the leaders and the followers, "questioning one another" means disputing with one another.

They said: that is, the followers said to the leaders: **You used to come to us from the right.** That is, from the direction of the right, so that you led us astray from it. This is what al-Dahhak said. Mujahid said: "from the true path." The scholars of meaning said: "that is, from the side of sincere counsel, blessing, and the work by which one seeks blessing." The Arabs regard what comes from the right as auspicious. Some said: "that is, from strength and power," as in the verse of al-Shammakh:

*When a banner is raised for glory,*
*Gharaba meets it with the right hand.* [[Lisan al-Arab: 1/593.]]

That is, with strength. Gharaba is the name of a king of Yemen.

They (that is, the leaders) said: **Rather, you were not believers. We had no authority over you; rather, you were a transgressing people. So the word of our Lord has come true against us; we will surely taste (the punishment).** They mean His saying, glorified is He: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and humankind, all together." [[Surah al-Sajda: 13.]]

**Indeed, we will all surely taste the punishment.**

**So we led you astray**: that is, we misguided you, **because we were ourselves astray**, that is, wrongdoers. Allah, the Exalted, said: **Indeed, on that Day they will share in the punishment. Thus do We deal with the criminals.** **Indeed, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," they were arrogant. And they said: "Shall we abandon our gods for a mad poet?"** That refers to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family). Allah, the Exalted, replied to them: **Rather, he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers. Indeed, you will taste the painful punishment. And you will be repaid only for what you used to do.**

**Except the sincere servants of Allah. For them is a known provision**, meaning morning and evening, as in His saying: **"And for them is their provision therein, morning and evening."** [[Surah Maryam: 62.]]

**Fruits** is the plural of *fakiha*, which is any food eaten for pleasure, not for sustenance that preserves health. It is said: "So-and-so enjoys (yatafakkahu) this food." **And they will be honoured in the Gardens of Bliss, on couches facing one another. A cup will be circulated among them** (*ka's*: a vessel containing drink; it is not called a cup (*ka's*) unless it contains drink, otherwise it is merely a vessel). Al-Akhfash said: "every cup (*ka's*) in the Qur'an is wine." **From a flowing spring**: wine flowing in rivers with pure springs. It may be that *ma'in* is of the form *fa'il* from *al-ma'n*, which means speed and intensity, from *amama fi al-amr* when one enters deeply into a matter. The meaning is: wine flowing intensely and swiftly.

**White**, that is, pure, in the utmost delicacy. **Delicious to the drinkers. No harm (ghawl) is in it**, that is, no sin, according to al-Kalbi, and its parallel is: **"No idle talk is in it, nor any sinfulness."** [[Surah al-Tur: 23.]] Qatada said: "a pain in the stomach." Al-Hasan said: "a headache." Mujahid said: "a disease." Ibn Kaysan said: "colic." Al-Sha'bi said: "it will not seize their minds and carry them away." The scholars of meaning said: *ghawl* is corruption that strikes unseen; it is said: "he was struck by *ightiyal* (secret ruin)" when his affair was secretly corrupted, and from it come *al-ghul* and *al-ghaylah*, which is killing in secret.

**Nor will they be drunk from it** (*wa la hum anha yunzafun*). Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited with a kasra on the *zay* here and in Surah al-Waqi'a; Asim agreed with them in al-Waqi'a. The rest recited with a fatha on the *zay* in both places. For one who recites with a fatha, the meaning is: "it will not overpower their minds, and they will not become intoxicated." It is said: "the man was *nazafa*, so he is *manzuf* and *nazif*," when he became drunk and his mind departed. The poet said:

*So I kissed her mouth, taking hold of her horns,*
*like one drunk (nazif) drinking the cold water of al-Hashraj.* [[Al-Sihah: 1/306.]]

That is, the intoxicated one. For one who recites with a kasra, the meaning is: "their wine will not run out." It is said: "the man *anzafa*, so he is *munzaf*, when his wine has run out." Al-Hutay'a said:

*By my life, if you have been emptied or sobered,*
*how wretched were the companions you were, O family of Abjar.* [[Lisan al-Arab: 9/327.]]

**And with them are maidens restraining their gaze**, that is, restraining their eyes, lowering their eyelids, having turned their eyes away from anyone other than their husbands, so they look only at their husbands. **With wide, beautiful eyes**: the singular is *ayna'*; it is said: "a man *a'yan*, and a woman *ayna'*, and men and women *'in*."

**As if they were hidden eggs**: the plural of *baydah*. **Concealed**: hidden and protected. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said they are compared to ostrich eggs, which are sheltered (*takinnuha*) by feathers from wind and dust. [[See al-Qurtubi, Tafsir: 15/80, and Fath al-Qadir: 4/394.]] It is also said they are compared to the inner part of an egg before it is peeled, which is the meaning of Ibn Abbas's saying. The word *maknun* is masculine, and *bayd* is plural, because it refers back to the wording (lafz).

**So some of them will turn to others, questioning one another** in Paradise. **A speaker among them will say: "I had a companion in the world. He used to say, 'Are you truly among those who believe (in the Resurrection)? When we die and become dust and bones, shall we truly be recompensed?'"** Mujahid said: "he was a devil." Others said: "he was a human." Muqatil said: "they were two brothers." The rest said: "they were two partners: one was Fitrus, who was the disbeliever, and the other was Yahudha, who was the believer. They are the two whose story Allah related in Surah al-Kahf."

**He will say: "Would you like to look?"** Allah, the Exalted, said to the people of Paradise: **"Will you look down (at the Fire)?"**

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Habish related to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yazid the reciter related to us, from Jalad, from al-Hakam ibn Tahir, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from Ibn Abbas, that he recited *hal muttali'un* (with a kasra on the lam)... *fa-ttala'a* with the vowels of both lowered and the lam kasra. He said: "(meaning) raising (the verb), so he raised." Ibn Abbas said: "That is because in Paradise there are openings (kuwa) through which its people look at the Fire and its people." [[The *kuwa* is the plural of *kuwwa*, a small opening or window.]]

**So he looked down and saw him in the midst of Hell**, that is, he saw his companion in the middle of the Fire.

He said: **"By Allah, you almost ruined me! Had it not been for the grace of my Lord, I would have been among those brought (into the Fire)"** with you. The word here is: *ma aradta illa an tahlikun* ("you only wanted you to perish"), [[So in the manuscript.]] and its origin is from *al-taraddi* (ruin). **Had it not been for the grace of my Lord**: His protection and mercy, **I would have been among those brought (into the Fire)** with you.

**Are we not to die, except our first death, and are we not to be punished?** The angels will say to them: "No." It was also said that they say this by way of recounting Allah's blessing upon them, in that they will not die and will not be punished. It was said that the believer says it in order to rebuke his companion for what he used to deny.

**Indeed, this is the great triumph. For the like of this, let the workers work.**

This is what al-Dahhak said. Mujahid said: "from the true path." The scholars of meaning said: "that is, from the side of sincere counsel, blessing, and the work by which one seeks blessing." They (that is, the leaders) said: **Rather, you were not believers. We had no authority over you; rather, you were a transgressing people. So the word of our Lord has come true against us; we will surely taste (the punishment).** They mean His saying, glorified is He: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and humankind, all together." [[Surah al-Sajda: 13.]]

**Indeed, we will all surely taste the punishment.**

**So we led you astray**: that is, we misguided you, **because we were ourselves astray**, that is, wrongdoers. Allah, the Exalted, said: **Indeed, on that Day they will share in the punishment. Thus do We deal with the criminals.** **Indeed, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," they were arrogant. And they said: "Shall we abandon our gods for a mad poet?"** That refers to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family). Allah, the Exalted, replied to them: **Rather, he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers. Indeed, you will taste the painful punishment. And you will be repaid only for what you used to do.**

**Except the sincere servants of Allah. For them is a known provision**, meaning morning and evening, as in His saying: **"And for them is their provision therein, morning and evening."** [[Surah Maryam: 62.]]

**Fruits** is the plural of *fakiha*, which is any food eaten for pleasure, not for sustenance that preserves health. It is said: "So-and-so enjoys (yatafakkahu) this food." **And they will be honoured in the Gardens of Bliss, on couches facing one another. A cup will be circulated among them** (*ka's*: a vessel containing drink; it is not called a cup (*ka's*) unless it contains drink, otherwise it is merely a vessel). Al-Akhfash said: "every cup (*ka's*) in the Qur'an is wine." **From a flowing spring**: wine flowing in rivers with pure springs. It may be that *ma'in* is of the form *fa'il* from *al-ma'n*, which means speed and intensity, from *amama fi al-amr* when one enters deeply into a matter. The meaning is: wine flowing intensely and swiftly.

**White**, that is, pure, in the utmost delicacy. **Delicious to the drinkers. No harm (ghawl) is in it**, that is, no sin, according to al-Kalbi, and its parallel is: **"No idle talk is in it, nor any sinfulness."** [[Surah al-Tur: 23.]] Qatada said: "a pain in the stomach." *like one drunk (nazif) drinking the cold water of al-Hashraj.* [[Al-Sihah: 1/306.]]

That is, the intoxicated one. For one who recites with a kasra, the meaning is: "their wine will not run out." It is said: "the man *anzafa*, so he is *munzaf*, when his wine has run out." Al-Hutay'a said:

*By my life, if you have been emptied or sobered,*
*how wretched were the companions you were, O family of Abjar.* [[Lisan al-Arab: 9/327.]]

**And with them are maidens restraining their gaze**, that is, restraining their eyes, lowering their eyelids, having turned their eyes away from anyone other than their husbands, so they look only at their husbands. **With wide, beautiful eyes**: the singular is *ayna'*; it is said: "a man *a'yan*, and a woman *ayna'*, and men and women *'in*."

**Fruits** is the plural of *fakiha*, which is any food eaten for pleasure, not for sustenance that preserves health. It is said: "So-and-so enjoys (yatafakkahu) this food." **And they will be honoured in the Gardens of Bliss, on couches facing one another. A cup will be circulated among them** (*ka's*: a vessel containing drink; it is not called a cup (*ka's*) unless it contains drink, otherwise it is merely a vessel). Al-Akhfash said: "every cup (*ka's*) in the Qur'an is wine." **From a flowing spring**: wine flowing in rivers with pure springs. It may be that *ma'in* is of the form *fa'il* from *al-ma'n*, which means speed and intensity, from *amama fi al-amr* when one enters deeply into a matter. The meaning is: wine flowing intensely and swiftly.

**White**, that is, pure, in the utmost delicacy. **Delicious to the drinkers. No harm (ghawl) is in it**, that is, no sin, according to al-Kalbi, and its parallel is: **"No idle talk is in it, nor any sinfulness."** [[Surah al-Tur: 23.]] Qatada said: "a pain in the stomach." Al-Hasan said: "a headache." Mujahid said: "a disease." Ibn Kaysan said: "colic." Al-Sha'bi said: "it will not seize their minds and carry them away." It is said: "the man was *nazafa*, so he is *manzuf* and *nazif*," when he became drunk and his mind departed. The poet said:

*By my life, if you have been emptied or sobered,*
*how wretched were the companions you were, O family of Abjar.* [[Lisan al-Arab: 9/327.]]

Al-Dahhak said: about their sins. Al-Qurazi said: about all their words and deeds.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dinawari informed me, saying: Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Uqba informed us, saying: Abu Husayn ibn Numayr al-Hamdani related to us, saying:

Husayn ibn Qays al-Rahabi related to us (and he claimed that he was a truthful shaykh), saying: Ata related to us, from Abu Amr, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "The feet of the son of Adam will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is questioned about five things: about his youth, how he spent it; about his life, how he consumed it; about his wealth, from where he earned it and how he spent it; and what he did with what he knew." [87] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/35.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Saqlab related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman at Tarsus related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Khulayd related to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Yunus al-Akhtaf al-Aqtas related to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Bilal related to us, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, glorified is He, will summon one of His servants, make him stand before Him, and question him about his standing (jah) just as He questions him about his wealth." [88] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/346.]]

**What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?** That is, you do not take revenge, and they do not help one another. The guardians of the Fire say this to the disbelievers. This was the reply of Abu Jahl when he said on the day of Badr: "We are a united company that will be victorious."

Allah, the Exalted, said: **Rather, on that day they will submit.** Ibn Abbas said: "they will be humbled." Al-Hasan said: "they will be compliant." Al-Akhfash said: "they will throw down their hands" (i.e., surrender). The scholars of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "they will be yielding to what they cannot resist or avoid, like one who seeks safety in the place of conflict."

**And some of them will turn to others, questioning one another.** "They" means the leaders and the followers, "questioning one another" means disputing with one another.

They said: that is, the followers said to the leaders: **You used to come to us from the right.** That is, from the direction of the right, so that you led us astray from it. This is what al-Dahhak said. Mujahid said: "from the true path." The scholars of meaning said: "that is, from the side of sincere counsel, blessing, and the work by which one seeks blessing." The Arabs regard what comes from the right as auspicious. Some said: "that is, from strength and power," as in the verse of al-Shammakh:

*When a banner is raised for glory,*
*Gharaba meets it with the right hand.* [[Lisan al-Arab: 1/593.]]

That is, with strength. Gharaba is the name of a king of Yemen.

They (that is, the leaders) said: **Rather, you were not believers. We had no authority over you; rather, you were a transgressing people. So the word of our Lord has come true against us; we will surely taste (the punishment).** They mean His saying, glorified is He: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and humankind, all together." [[Surah al-Sajda: 13.]]

**Indeed, we will all surely taste the punishment.**

**So we led you astray**: that is, we misguided you, **because we were ourselves astray**, that is, wrongdoers. Allah, the Exalted, said: **Indeed, on that Day they will share in the punishment. Thus do We deal with the criminals.** **Indeed, when it was said to them, "There is no god but Allah," they were arrogant. And they said: "Shall we abandon our gods for a mad poet?"** That refers to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family). Allah, the Exalted, replied to them: **Rather, he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers. Indeed, you will taste the painful punishment. And you will be repaid only for what you used to do.**

**Except the sincere servants of Allah. For them is a known provision**, meaning morning and evening, as in His saying: **"And for them is their provision therein, morning and evening."** [[Surah Maryam: 62.]]

**Fruits** is the plural of *fakiha*, which is any food eaten for pleasure, not for sustenance that preserves health. It is said: "So-and-so enjoys (yatafakkahu) this food." **And they will be honoured in the Gardens of Bliss, on couches facing one another. A cup will be circulated among them** (*ka's*: a vessel containing drink; it is not called a cup (*ka's*) unless it contains drink, otherwise it is merely a vessel). Al-Akhfash said: "every cup (*ka's*) in the Qur'an is wine." **From a flowing spring**: wine flowing in rivers with pure springs. It may be that *ma'in* is of the form *fa'il* from *al-ma'n*, which means speed and intensity, from *amama fi al-amr* when one enters deeply into a matter. The meaning is: wine flowing intensely and swiftly.

**White**, that is, pure, in the utmost delicacy. **Delicious to the drinkers. No harm (ghawl) is in it**, that is, no sin, according to al-Kalbi, and its parallel is: **"No idle talk is in it, nor any sinfulness."** [[Surah al-Tur: 23.]] Qatada said: "a pain in the stomach." Al-Hasan said: "a headache." Mujahid said: "a disease." Ibn Kaysan said: "colic." Al-Sha'bi said: "it will not seize their minds and carry them away." The scholars of meaning said: *ghawl* is corruption that strikes unseen; it is said: "he was struck by *ightiyal* (secret ruin)" when his affair was secretly corrupted, and from it come *al-ghul* and *al-ghaylah*, which is killing in secret.

**Nor will they be drunk from it** (*wa la hum anha yunzafun*). Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited with a kasra on the *zay* here and in Surah al-Waqi'a; Asim agreed with them in al-Waqi'a. The rest recited with a fatha on the *zay* in both places. For one who recites with a fatha, the meaning is: "it will not overpower their minds, and they will not become intoxicated." It is said: "the man was *nazafa*, so he is *manzuf* and *nazif*," when he became drunk and his mind departed. The poet said:

*So I kissed her mouth, taking hold of her horns,*
*like one drunk (nazif) drinking the cold water of al-Hashraj.* [[Al-Sihah: 1/306.]]

That is, the intoxicated one. For one who recites with a kasra, the meaning is: "their wine will not run out." It is said: "the man *anzafa*, so he is *munzaf*, when his wine has run out." Al-Hutay'a said:

*By my life, if you have been emptied or sobered,*
*how wretched were the companions you were, O family of Abjar.* [[Lisan al-Arab: 9/327.]]

**And with them are maidens restraining their gaze**, that is, restraining their eyes, lowering their eyelids, having turned their eyes away from anyone other than their husbands, so they look only at their husbands. **With wide, beautiful eyes**: the singular is *ayna'*; it is said: "a man *a'yan*, and a woman *ayna'*, and men and women *'in*."

**As if they were hidden eggs**: the plural of *baydah*. **Concealed**: hidden and protected. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said they are compared to ostrich eggs, which are sheltered (*takinnuha*) by feathers from wind and dust. [[See al-Qurtubi, Tafsir: 15/80, and Fath al-Qadir: 4/394.]] It is also said they are compared to the inner part of an egg before it is peeled, which is the meaning of Ibn Abbas's saying. The word *maknun* is masculine, and *bayd* is plural, because it refers back to the wording (lafz).

**So some of them will turn to others, questioning one another** in Paradise. **A speaker among them will say: "I had a companion in the world. He used to say, 'Are you truly among those who believe (in the Resurrection)? When we die and become dust and bones, shall we truly be recompensed?'"** Mujahid said: "he was a devil." Others said: "he was a human." Muqatil said: "they were two brothers." The rest said: "they were two partners: one was Fitrus, who was the disbeliever, and the other was Yahudha, who was the believer. They are the two whose story Allah related in Surah al-Kahf."

**He will say: "Would you like to look?"** Allah, the Exalted, said to the people of Paradise: **"Will you look down (at the Fire)?"**

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Habish related to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yazid the reciter related to us, from Jalad, from al-Hakam ibn Tahir, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from Ibn Abbas, that he recited *hal muttali'un* (with a kasra on the lam)... *fa-ttala'a* with the vowels of both lowered and the lam kasra. He said: "(meaning) raising (the verb), so he raised." Ibn Abbas said: "That is because in Paradise there are openings (kuwa) through which its people look at the Fire and its people." [[The *kuwa* is the plural of *kuwwa*, a small opening or window.]]

**So he looked down and saw him in the midst of Hell**, that is, he saw his companion in the middle of the Fire.

He said: **"By Allah, you almost ruined me! Had it not been for the grace of my Lord, I would have been among those brought (into the Fire)"** with you. The word here is: *ma aradta illa an tahlikun* ("you only wanted you to perish"), [[So in the manuscript.]] and its origin is from *al-taraddi* (ruin). **Had it not been for the grace of my Lord**: His protection and mercy, **I would have been among those brought (into the Fire)** with you.

**Are we not to die, except our first death, and are we not to be punished?** The angels will say to them: "No." It was also said that they say this by way of recounting Allah's blessing upon them, in that they will not die and will not be punished. It was said that the believer says it in order to rebuke his companion for what he used to deny.

**Indeed, this is the great triumph. For the like of this, let the workers work.**

﴿Is that better as a welcome,﴾ meaning provision, ﴿or the tree of zaqqum?﴾ The zaqqum is the fruit of a tree whose taste is extremely repugnant. It comes from the expression "yazqumu hadha al-ta'am," used when someone eats food with great reluctance and hardship.

﴿Indeed, We made it a trial for the wrongdoers.﴾ That is, for the disbelievers. They said: "How can there be a tree in the Fire, when the Fire burns trees?" Ibn al-Zib'ara said to the chieftains of Quraysh: "Muhammad frightens us with the zaqqum, but the zaqqum in the language of Berbers and Africa means butter and dates." Abu Jahl then brought them into his house and said: "O slave-girl, zaqqimina!" She brought them butter and dates, and he said: "Eat zaqqum! This is what Muhammad promises you." So Allah, glorified is He, said:

﴿It is a tree that springs from the root of Hellfire.﴾ That is, the bottom of the Fire. Al-Hasan said: "Its root is at the bottom of Hell, and its branches rise up to its levels."

﴿Its fruit-stalks﴾ meaning its fruit, and it was called "ṭalʿ" because it emerges (ṭulūʿ). ﴿are like the heads of devils.﴾ Some scholars said: they are literally the devils themselves, and the likeness is to their ugliness, because when people describe something as having the blemish of ugliness, they say: "It is like devils," even though devils are not seen, since the ugliness of their form is imagined in the soul. This is the meaning reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Qurazi. Others said: by "devils" is meant snakes, and the Arabs call an ugly, light-bodied snake a "shaytan." The poet said:

*It plays like a Hadrami twin, as if it were a devil's coil in a barren field of khurūʿ.*

And the rajiz said:

*ʿAnjarad, when I swear, he swears too, like the shaytan of the ḥamāṭ, the one with a vein (aʿraf).*

Al-aʿraf is the one that has a vein. It was also said: it is an ugly, rough, bitter, foul-smelling tree that grows in the desert, which the Arabs call "heads of devils."

﴿Indeed, they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it.﴾ Al-mal' means filling a container with what cannot hold more. ﴿Then, indeed, they will have upon it a mixture (shawb),﴾ that is, a blend and admixture. Muqatil said: a drink ﴿of boiling water,﴾ water that is extremely hot. ﴿Then indeed their return is to the Blazing Fire.﴾ Here "thumma" is used in the sense of "qabl" (before). The implied meaning (majāz) is: "And before that, their return is indeed to the Blazing Fire," as in the poet's words:

*Indeed, whoever becomes a lord, then his father became a lord, then his grandfather had already become a lord before that.*

That is, before that, his father became a lord. It is also permissible for "thumma" to mean "wa" (and).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu ʿAli al-Muqri' told us, saying: ʿAli ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd al-Hamadani told me, saying: ʿAbbas ibn Yazid ibn Abi Ḥabib told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq told us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Maysara, from al-Minhal, from Abu ʿUbayda, from Abdullah, that he recited: "Thumma inna maqtalahum la-ila al-Jahim" (Then indeed their place of slaying is to the Blazing Fire).

﴿Indeed, they found their fathers astray,﴾ that is, they found them lost. ﴿So they were hastening upon their traces,﴾ meaning they were hurrying.

﴿And already before them most of the former peoples had gone astray.﴾ ﴿And We had already sent among them warners.﴾ That is, messengers. ﴿So see how was the end of those who were warned,﴾ ﴿except the sincere servants of Allah.﴾ ﴿And Noah had already called upon Us,﴾ its parallel is ﴿and Noah, when he called before,﴾ and it is His saying: ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "I am overpowered, so help me."﴾

﴿How excellent were the Responders!﴾ This is in the sense of glorification. ﴿And We delivered him and his family from the great distress,﴾ which is the flood. ﴿And We made his descendants the survivors,﴾

Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Saji told us, saying: Bundar told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Ghayma told us, saying: Saʿid ibn Bashir told us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from Samura, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His saying ﴿And We made his descendants the survivors﴾, he said: "Sam, Ham, and Japheth."

Sam is the father of the Arabs, Persians and Romans; Ham is the father of the black peoples from east to west; and Japheth is the father of the Turks, Gog and Magog, and what lies beyond them."

Muqatil said: The idols were seventy-two idols, of wood, iron, lead, tin, silver and gold. The chief of them was of gold, with two rubies in its eyes. They said to Abraham (peace be upon him): "Do not go out with us tomorrow to our festival." So he looked at the stars, and ﴿said, "Indeed, I am sick."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "Stricken by plague (mat'un)." al-Hasan said: "Ill." al-Dahhak said: "I will become sick," in accordance with His words, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed they will die﴾ [[Surat al-Zumar: 30.]].

It is said: "Sick" refers to what is in my neck, namely death. It is said: "Sick" refers to what I see of your ugly conditions. It is said: "Sick" refers to an ailment that befell him; and indeed he only looked at the stars, deducing from them the time of a fever that used to come upon him. The correct view is that he was not sick, because of what was related from the Prophet (peace be upon him), that he said: "Abraham told three lies, none of which was except that he was defending and disavowing thereby his religion [[In the source: two were for God's sake and one concerned his own self.]]: his saying 'Indeed, I am sick,' his saying 'Rather, the biggest of them did it,' and his saying to Sarah: 'This is my sister'" [90] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 23/85.]].

﴿So they turned their backs and departed﴾ to their festival. Then Abraham entered the idols and smashed them, and he placed the axe on the shoulder of the biggest idol. When they returned from their festival, they would enter upon their idols before returning to their homes. They entered upon them and found them broken. That is His words, glorified is He: ﴿So he turned to their gods﴾ (faragha: he turned toward them) ﴿and said, showing their weakness and impotence: "Will you not eat? What is wrong with you that you do not speak?"﴾ ﴿Then he attacked them, striking them with the right hand﴾ because it is stronger for action than the left. This is the view of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: he meant his right hand. It is said: "with the oath that he had earlier made," which is His words: ﴿And by God, I will surely plot against your idols﴾ [[Surat al-Anbiya': 57.]]. al-Farra' said: "with power."

﴿Then they came toward him﴾ toward Abraham, ﴿hastening (yazifful)﴾, meaning they rushed, according to al-Hasan. Mujahid said: "hastening like the gliding of ostriches, which is a state between walking and flying." al-Dahhak said: "running." Yahya, al-A'mash and Hamza read yuziffun with a dammed yā', and both are dialects (lughatan). Abraham said to them, in the manner of rebuke: ﴿Do you worship what you carve? And God created you and what you do?﴾ In this verse there is evidence that the acts of servants are created by God, glorified and exalted is He, since He said ﴿and what you do﴾, while attributing to them an act, which establishes that it is acquired (muktasabah) by the servants. Thus by this verse the doctrine of the Qadariyya (those who deny divine decree) and the Jabriyya (those who deny human agency) is refuted.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed God is the creator of every maker and his making" [91] [[al-Mustadrak: 1/31.]].

﴿They said: "Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire."﴾ The blazing fire: the core of the fire. Muqatil said: They built for him a wall of stone, thirty cubits long and twenty cubits wide, filled it with firewood, and lit the fire in it.

﴿They intended a scheme against him, but We made them the lowest﴾: the subdued.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 37, verse 99–106 (part 1 of 2):

Ibrahim said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord," that is, to the pleasure of my Lord, and that is the place to which he was commanded to go. Its counterpart is His saying: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord."﴾ [Surah al-Ankabut: 26]. It was also said: "I am going to my Lord" with myself and my deeds. ﴿He will guide me.﴾ ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ (abridged) That is: "My Lord, grant me a righteous son from among the righteous."

﴿So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy.﴾ ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion,﴾ that boy, ﴿he said, "O my son, indeed I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you..."﴾ (the verse). The early scholars of the Muslim scholars differed about which of his two sons Ibrahim was commanded to sacrifice, after the consensus of [the people of the specialized knowledge] that it was Ishaq (Isaac). A group said: the one sacrificed was Ishaq. Among the Companions, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib held this view; and among the later generations and their followers: Ka'b al-Ahbar, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, Masruq, 'Ikrimah, al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, 'Ata', Muqatil, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, al-Zubayri and al-Suddi.

This is the narration of 'Ikrimah and Ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Harb told us, saying: Sunayd ibn Dawud told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Layth ibn Sa'd, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "It was Ishaq."

And al-Hasan informed me, saying: 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: Radwan ibn Ahmad al-Saydalani told us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-'Utaridi told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from Hajjaj, from al-Qasim ibn Nafi', from Abu al-Tufayl, from 'Ali, who said: "The one whom Ibrahim (peace be upon him) intended to sacrifice was Ishaq."
[92] [Al-Mustadrak: 2/558 – and the narration is from Ibn 'Abbas.]

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, who said: A man boasted in the presence of Ibn Mas'ud, saying: "I am so-and-so son of so-and-so, son of the noble elders." 'Abdullah said: "That is Yusuf son of Ya'qub son of Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the friend of Allah (peace be upon them)."

And al-Husayn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Abdullah told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: al-Mubarak told us, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who said: "The one whom Allah ransomed with a great sacrifice (dhibhin 'azim) was Ishaq."

And al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ibn Habish told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-Sufi told us, saying: Abu 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn Bakkar told us, saying: Khalid ibn 'Abdullah al-Wasiti told us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "The one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice was Ishaq (peace be upon them both)."

And al-Hasan informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan ibn 'Abdullah informed us, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Abdullah told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice was Ishaq."

And al-Hasan informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid told us, saying: 'Abbas al-Duri told us, saying: Abu Salamah – meaning al-Minqari – told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi told us, from Musa, the freedman of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "When Ibrahim was shown in a dream the sacrifice of Ishaq, he travelled with him a distance of a month in a single morning until he brought him to the place of sacrifice at Mina. Then when Allah diverted the slaughter from him and commanded him to sacrifice the ram, he sacrificed it, and he travelled with him a distance of a month in a single afternoon, the valleys and mountains being folded up for him."

Sufyan narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, from his father, who said: Musa said: "O Lord, they say: 'the God of Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub.' Why do they say that?" He said: "Indeed Ibrahim never preferred anything over Me without Me choosing him over it; and Ishaq gave Me his life for the sacrifice, while he is more generous than that; and Ya'qub, whenever I increased him in trial, his good opinion of Me increased."
[93] [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 23/97.]

Hamzah al-Zayyat narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, who said: Yusuf said to the king: "Would you desire to eat with me, or would you disdain? I am, by Allah, Yusuf son of Ya'qub, the prophet of Allah, son of Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the friend of Allah (peace be upon them)?!"
[94] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/7.]

Others said: it was Isma'il. To this view went 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, Abu al-Tufayl 'Amir ibn Wathilah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Yusuf ibn Mihran, Mujahid, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi; and it is the narration of 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Abu Hamzah Nasr ibn 'Imran al-Dab'i and Yusuf ibn Majak from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The one ransomed was Isma'il, and the Jews claimed it was Ishaq, and the Jews lied."

Both views have been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ). If either of them were authentic by consensus, he would not have attributed it to another. [That is what is in the manuscript.] As for the narration reported from him (ﷺ) that the sacrificed one was Ishaq:
Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad [said] [In the manuscript: "said."] told us, saying: Ibn Mujahid told us, saying: Musa ibn Ishaq told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Shanbah told us, saying: al-Ashyab informed us, saying:
Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice was Ishaq."
[95] [Al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim, with variation: 2/557.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Lu'lu' told us, saying: al-Haytham ibn Khalaf informed us, saying:
Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I was informed, from Safwan ibn Sulaym and Zayd ibn Aslam, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), that he said: "Indeed Ishaq is the one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice."
[96]

Abu Tahir ibn Khuzaymah informed us in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, in the year three hundred and eighty-three [he read it to me]... He said: My grandfather informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Hujr told us, saying: 'Umar ibn Hafs told us, from Aban, from Anas, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ishaq will intercede after me, and he will say: 'O Lord, You have affirmed Your Prophet, and I offered myself for the sacrifice; so do not admit into the Fire anyone who has not associated anything with You.'" He said: "Then the Blessed and Exalted will say: 'By My might, I will not admit into the Fire anyone who does not associate anything with Me.'"
[97]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Nasrawayh told us, saying: Abu Hafs 'Umar ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Jawhari told us, saying: 'Isa ibn Musawwar al-Jawhari told us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam told us, from his father, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave me the choice between forgiving half of my Ummah or my intercession, and I chose my intercession, and I hoped it would be more general for my Ummah. Had it not been for what the righteous servant (al-'abd al-salih) preceded me to, my supplication would have been hastened for them. Indeed, when Allah relieved Ishaq of the distress of the sacrifice, it was said: 'O Ishaq, ask and you will be given.' He said: 'By the One in whose hand is my soul, I will hasten it before the whisper of Satan: O Allah, whoever dies without associating anything with You, forgive him and admit him into Paradise.'"
[98] [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/202; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/18, with slight variation.]

As for what was narrated from him (ﷺ) that the sacrificed one was Isma'il:
'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated from 'Ubaydullah ibn Muhammad al-'Utbi – of the descendants of 'Utbah ibn Abi Sufyan – from his father, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Sa'id told me, from al-Sunabihi, who said: We were with Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan when they mentioned the sacrificed one, whether Isma'il or Ishaq. He said: "You have come to the one who knows; I was with the Prophet (ﷺ) when a man came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, give me from what Allah has bestowed upon you, O son of the two sacrificed ones.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed." It was said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, what are the two sacrificed ones?" He said: "When 'Abd al-Muttalib dug the well of Zamzam, he vowed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that if Allah made its matter easy for him, he would sacrifice one of his sons. The arrow fell upon 'Abdullah, but his maternal uncles prevented him, saying: 'Ransom your son with a hundred camels.' So he ransomed him with a hundred camels. The second was Isma'il (peace be upon him)."
[99] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/113, with variation.]

This is what has come in the reports on this subject. As for the proof of those who say it was Ishaq from the Qur'an: Allah, glorified is He, informed about His friend Ibrahim (peace be upon him) when he separated from his people, emigrating to Syria with his wife Sarah and his nephew Lut, and he said: ﴿Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me.﴾ He supplicated and said: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ That was before he knew Hajar, and before Isma'il's mother became his. Then the account followed of His answering his supplication and giving him the good tidings of ﴿a forbearing boy,﴾ then of Ibrahim's dream that he should sacrifice that boy who had been given the good tidings of, when ﴿he reached with him [the age of] exertion.﴾ And there is in the Book of Allah no good tiding to Ibrahim of a male child except with Ishaq.
[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/190.]

Those who said it was Isma'il argued from the Qur'an with what Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that he used to say: "The one whom Allah, glorified is He, commanded Ibrahim to sacrifice from his two sons was Isma'il, and we find that in the Book of Allah, glorified is He. For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says, after finishing the story of the one sacrificed: ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous.﴾"

And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So We gave her good tidings of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Surah Hud: 71], meaning: a son, and a son's son. So He would not have commanded him to sacrifice Ishaq when the promised one from Allah, glorified and exalted is He, was in him. [That is, the promised child.] Since Allah did not mention Ishaq except after the conclusion of the account of the sacrifice, and then gave him the good tidings of Ishaq's offspring, we know that the sacrificed one was Isma'il."

Al-Qurazi said: I mentioned that to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Aziz, when he was caliph and I was with him in Syria. 'Umar said to me: "This matter, I had not considered it, and I indeed see it as you have said." Then he sent for a man who was with him in Syria, who had been a Jew, then became Muslim and his Islam was good, and who used to consider himself among the scholars of the Jews. 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Aziz asked him about that while I was with him, and he said: "Which of Ibrahim's two sons was he commanded to sacrifice?" He said: "Isma'il." Then he said: "By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful, the Jews do know that, but they envy you, the Arab folk, that your father should be the one concerning whom Allah, glorified and exalted is He, issued that command, and the virtue Allah mentioned of him for his patience in what he was commanded. So they deny that and claim it was Ishaq, because Ishaq is their father."

They also argued that the two horns of the ram were hung in the Ka'bah in the hands of the descendants of Isma'il until the House burned and the two horns burned in the days of Ibn al-Zubayr [i.e. 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam. Marginal note of the manuscript] and al-Hajjaj. al-Sha'bi said: "I saw the two horns of the ram hanging in the Ka'bah, and the two horns were an inheritance of the children of Isma'il from their father. The children of Ishaq, who are the Romans, did not contend with them over that, and they were greater, mightier and more powerful than the Arabs." This is the strongest proof that the sacrificed one was Isma'il.

al-Asma'i said: I asked Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' about whether the sacrificed one was Ishaq or Isma'il? He said to me: "O Asma', where has your intellect gone?

When was Ishaq (peace be upon him) in Mecca? Isma'il was in Mecca, and he is the one who built the House with his father Ibrahim (peace be upon them both), as Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House, and Isma'il [with him]﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 127], and the place of sacrifice in Mecca is beyond doubt."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Mundhir al-Darir say: I heard Abu Muhammad al-Zanjani al-Mu'addib say: Abu Sa'id al-Darir was asked about the sacrificed one, and he recited:

Indeed the sacrificed one, may you be guided, is Isma'il... the Book and the Revelation have spoken of that.
He was honoured by it, the one whom God singled out, our Prophet, and interpretation and exegesis came with it.
If you are his nation, do not deny him a honour that preference has singled out for him.
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/100.]

As for the account of the sacrifice, al-Suddi said with his chain: When Ibrahim the Friend (peace be upon him) separated from his people, emigrating to Syria, fleeing with his religion, as Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ he called upon Allah, glorified and exalted is He, to grant him a righteous son from Sarah, and he said: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ When the angels, the messengers sent to the overturned cities, came to him as guests and gave him the good tidings of a forbearing boy, Ibrahim said, upon being given the good tidings of him:
"Then he is indeed for Allah, a sacrifice." When the boy was born and reached with him the age of exertion, it was said: "Fulfil your vow which you vowed." This was the cause of Allah, exalted is He, commanding His messenger Ibrahim to sacrifice his son.
