Abu Hurayrah narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar, and Ibn Ishaq from his shaykhs, they said: When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was shown the sacrifice of his son, Satan said: "By Allah, if I do not tempt the family of Ibrahim at this point, I will never tempt any of them ever."

So Satan appeared to them in the form of a man, and came to the mother of the boy and said to her: "Do you know where Ibrahim has taken your son?" She said:

He took him, saying, "He is gathering firewood for us from this valley." She said, "No, by God, he has not taken him except to slaughter him." She said, "No, he is more merciful to him and loves him more than that." He said, "He claims that God has commanded him to do so." She said, "If his Lord has commanded him, then he has done well to obey his Lord, and we submit to the command of God, Mighty and Majestic."

Then Satan left her and caught up with the boy as he was walking behind his father. He said to him, "Boy, do you know where your father is going?" He said, "He is gathering firewood for our family from this valley." He said, "By God, he only wants to slaughter you." He said, "Why?" He said, "He claims that his Lord has commanded him to do so." He said, "Then let him do what his Lord has commanded him. Hearing and obedience."

When the boy refused him, he turned to Abraham and said, "Where are you going, old man?" He said, "I want this valley for a need of mine there." He said, "By God, I see that Satan has come to you in your dream and commanded you to slaughter this son of yours." Abraham recognised him and said, "Get away from me, enemy of God! By God, I will certainly carry out the command of God." [102] [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/192, the report on the manner of the action of Abraham and his son.]]

Abu al-Tufayl narrated from Ibn Abbas that when Abraham was commanded to slaughter his son, Satan appeared to him at this al-Mash'ar (the sacred site near Muzdalifah), and raced him, and Abraham outpaced him. Then he went to Jamrat al-'Aqabah, and Satan appeared to him, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he left. Then he met him at the middle pillar, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he left. Then he caught up with him at the greatest pillar, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he left. Then he proceeded by the command of God, Mighty and Majestic, in that matter.

Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said: [[The verses in full are in Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/195, the report of Abraham and his son.]]

And for Abraham, who fulfils his vow, seeking reward, and who carries the rope and the knife,
His son, whom he could not bear to be parted from, even if he saw him among a band of enemies.
O my son, I have vowed you to God, a sacrifice; so be patient, my ransom, my state.
And he tightens the bond, I will not swerve from the knife, swerving as a captive in shackles does.
He has a blade that gleams upon the flesh, sharp, curved like a crescent.
While he was stripping the garments from him, his Lord ransomed him with a lawful ram.
He said, "Take this, and release your son, for I have accepted what you both did, without speech."
Souls often recoil from a matter, yet for it there is an opening like the loosening of a hobbled camel's tether.

This is the story of the sacrifice, as God, glorified is He, said: ﴿When he reached the age of exertion with him﴾. Ibn Abbas said: this means walking with his father to the (places of) camels [[In Tafsir al-Qurtubi 15/99: Ibn Abbas said it means reaching the age of puberty; Qatadah said it means he walked with his father.]]. Al-Hasan and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it means the intellect by which one is held accountable. Al-Dahhak said: it means movement. Ibn Zayd said: [it means] striving in worship.

﴿O my son, I see in a dream﴾: I saw in a dream that I am slaughtering you, in fulfilment of a vow upon me concerning you; I was commanded to do so. For Abraham (peace be upon him) saw on the night of the Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah) as if someone was saying to him: God commands you to slaughter this son of yours. When morning came, he pondered (rawwa) in himself, that is, he reflected from morning until evening: is this command from God or from Satan? Hence the day was called Tarwiyah (the day of reflection). When evening came, he saw the same dream again, the slaughter of his son. When morning came, he knew that this command was from God. Hence the day was called 'Arafah (the day of recognition).

Muqatil said: Abraham saw this for three consecutive nights. Ata' and Muqatil said: Abraham was commanded to slaughter his son in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). When he was certain of this, he informed his son, and said to him: ﴿So consider what you see?﴾. The majority read تَرَى with a fatha on the ta. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read تُرِي with a damma on the ta and a kasra on the ra', that is: what do you indicate? It was permissible for him to consult his son about proceeding with God's command, because he wished to know his son's patience in God's command and his resolve in obedience to Him. So his son said:

﴿O my father, do what you are commanded. You will find me, God willing, among the patient.﴾

﴿When both of them submitted﴾, that is, they yielded and humbled themselves to the command of God, Glorified and Exalted, and were content with it. Ibn Mas'ud read فلما سلّما (fa-lamma sallama), meaning they entrusted (themselves). Ibn Abbas read استسلما (istaslama). Qatadah said: this one submitted his son and this one submitted himself. ﴿And he laid him down upon his forehead﴾, that is, he threw him down, placed him on his side, and turned him onto his face for the slaughter. ﴿And We called out to him﴾. The scholars of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) said: the waw (الواو, the conjunction) here is extra (muqhamah), a connective particle, and its sense is: "We called out to him," as in His saying: ﴿And they agreed to put him in the bottom of the well, and We revealed to him﴾, meaning: "We revealed to him." And His saying: ﴿And they will be from every high ground, hastening, and the promise draws near﴾. Imru' al-Qays said:

"So when we passed the courtyard of the tribe and he turned aside..."

And a poet said:
"Until, when your bellies have become infested with lice, and you have seen your sons grown up,
And you have turned the back of the shield against us, indeed the base, the weak, the treacherous one..."

He meant: "you turned" (قلبتم).

﴿O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision. Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers. Indeed, this is the clear trial﴾: the manifest test concerning that which necessitates a blessing or a calamity. For this reason, blessings are called بلاء (balaa') and trials are called بلاء, because each is named after its cause through which it leads to it, just as the causes of death are called "this very death."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 37, verse 99–106 (part 1 of 2):

Ibrahim said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord," that is, to the pleasure of my Lord, and that is the place to which he was commanded to go. Its counterpart is His saying: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord."﴾ [Surah al-Ankabut: 26]. It was also said: "I am going to my Lord" with myself and my deeds. ﴿He will guide me.﴾ ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ (abridged) That is: "My Lord, grant me a righteous son from among the righteous."

﴿So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy.﴾ ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion,﴾ that boy, ﴿he said, "O my son, indeed I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you..."﴾ (the verse). The early scholars of the Muslim scholars differed about which of his two sons Ibrahim was commanded to sacrifice, after the consensus of [the people of the specialized knowledge] that it was Ishaq (Isaac). A group said: the one sacrificed was Ishaq. Among the Companions, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib held this view; and among the later generations and their followers: Ka'b al-Ahbar, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, Masruq, 'Ikrimah, al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, 'Ata', Muqatil, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, al-Zubayri and al-Suddi.

This is the narration of 'Ikrimah and Ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Harb told us, saying: Sunayd ibn Dawud told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Layth ibn Sa'd, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "It was Ishaq."

And al-Hasan informed me, saying: 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: Radwan ibn Ahmad al-Saydalani told us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-'Utaridi told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from Hajjaj, from al-Qasim ibn Nafi', from Abu al-Tufayl, from 'Ali, who said: "The one whom Ibrahim (peace be upon him) intended to sacrifice was Ishaq."
[92] [Al-Mustadrak: 2/558 – and the narration is from Ibn 'Abbas.]

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, who said: A man boasted in the presence of Ibn Mas'ud, saying: "I am so-and-so son of so-and-so, son of the noble elders." 'Abdullah said: "That is Yusuf son of Ya'qub son of Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the friend of Allah (peace be upon them)."

And al-Husayn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Abdullah told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: al-Mubarak told us, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who said: "The one whom Allah ransomed with a great sacrifice (dhibhin 'azim) was Ishaq."

And al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ibn Habish told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-Sufi told us, saying: Abu 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn Bakkar told us, saying: Khalid ibn 'Abdullah al-Wasiti told us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "The one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice was Ishaq (peace be upon them both)."

And al-Hasan informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan ibn 'Abdullah informed us, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Abdullah told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice was Ishaq."

And al-Hasan informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid told us, saying: 'Abbas al-Duri told us, saying: Abu Salamah – meaning al-Minqari – told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi told us, from Musa, the freedman of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "When Ibrahim was shown in a dream the sacrifice of Ishaq, he travelled with him a distance of a month in a single morning until he brought him to the place of sacrifice at Mina. Then when Allah diverted the slaughter from him and commanded him to sacrifice the ram, he sacrificed it, and he travelled with him a distance of a month in a single afternoon, the valleys and mountains being folded up for him."

Sufyan narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, from his father, who said: Musa said: "O Lord, they say: 'the God of Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub.' Why do they say that?" He said: "Indeed Ibrahim never preferred anything over Me without Me choosing him over it; and Ishaq gave Me his life for the sacrifice, while he is more generous than that; and Ya'qub, whenever I increased him in trial, his good opinion of Me increased."
[93] [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 23/97.]

Hamzah al-Zayyat narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, who said: Yusuf said to the king: "Would you desire to eat with me, or would you disdain? I am, by Allah, Yusuf son of Ya'qub, the prophet of Allah, son of Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the friend of Allah (peace be upon them)?!"
[94] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/7.]

Others said: it was Isma'il. To this view went 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, Abu al-Tufayl 'Amir ibn Wathilah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Yusuf ibn Mihran, Mujahid, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi; and it is the narration of 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Abu Hamzah Nasr ibn 'Imran al-Dab'i and Yusuf ibn Majak from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The one ransomed was Isma'il, and the Jews claimed it was Ishaq, and the Jews lied."

Both views have been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ). If either of them were authentic by consensus, he would not have attributed it to another. [That is what is in the manuscript.] As for the narration reported from him (ﷺ) that the sacrificed one was Ishaq:
Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad [said] [In the manuscript: "said."] told us, saying: Ibn Mujahid told us, saying: Musa ibn Ishaq told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Shanbah told us, saying: al-Ashyab informed us, saying:
Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice was Ishaq."
[95] [Al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim, with variation: 2/557.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Lu'lu' told us, saying: al-Haytham ibn Khalaf informed us, saying:
Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I was informed, from Safwan ibn Sulaym and Zayd ibn Aslam, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), that he said: "Indeed Ishaq is the one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice."
[96]

Abu Tahir ibn Khuzaymah informed us in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, in the year three hundred and eighty-three [he read it to me]... He said: My grandfather informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Hujr told us, saying: 'Umar ibn Hafs told us, from Aban, from Anas, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ishaq will intercede after me, and he will say: 'O Lord, You have affirmed Your Prophet, and I offered myself for the sacrifice; so do not admit into the Fire anyone who has not associated anything with You.'" He said: "Then the Blessed and Exalted will say: 'By My might, I will not admit into the Fire anyone who does not associate anything with Me.'"
[97]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Nasrawayh told us, saying: Abu Hafs 'Umar ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Jawhari told us, saying: 'Isa ibn Musawwar al-Jawhari told us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam told us, from his father, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave me the choice between forgiving half of my Ummah or my intercession, and I chose my intercession, and I hoped it would be more general for my Ummah. Had it not been for what the righteous servant (al-'abd al-salih) preceded me to, my supplication would have been hastened for them. Indeed, when Allah relieved Ishaq of the distress of the sacrifice, it was said: 'O Ishaq, ask and you will be given.' He said: 'By the One in whose hand is my soul, I will hasten it before the whisper of Satan: O Allah, whoever dies without associating anything with You, forgive him and admit him into Paradise.'"
[98] [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/202; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/18, with slight variation.]

As for what was narrated from him (ﷺ) that the sacrificed one was Isma'il:
'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated from 'Ubaydullah ibn Muhammad al-'Utbi – of the descendants of 'Utbah ibn Abi Sufyan – from his father, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Sa'id told me, from al-Sunabihi, who said: We were with Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan when they mentioned the sacrificed one, whether Isma'il or Ishaq. He said: "You have come to the one who knows; I was with the Prophet (ﷺ) when a man came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, give me from what Allah has bestowed upon you, O son of the two sacrificed ones.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed." It was said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, what are the two sacrificed ones?" He said: "When 'Abd al-Muttalib dug the well of Zamzam, he vowed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that if Allah made its matter easy for him, he would sacrifice one of his sons. The arrow fell upon 'Abdullah, but his maternal uncles prevented him, saying: 'Ransom your son with a hundred camels.' So he ransomed him with a hundred camels. The second was Isma'il (peace be upon him)."
[99] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/113, with variation.]

This is what has come in the reports on this subject. As for the proof of those who say it was Ishaq from the Qur'an: Allah, glorified is He, informed about His friend Ibrahim (peace be upon him) when he separated from his people, emigrating to Syria with his wife Sarah and his nephew Lut, and he said: ﴿Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me.﴾ He supplicated and said: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ That was before he knew Hajar, and before Isma'il's mother became his. Then the account followed of His answering his supplication and giving him the good tidings of ﴿a forbearing boy,﴾ then of Ibrahim's dream that he should sacrifice that boy who had been given the good tidings of, when ﴿he reached with him [the age of] exertion.﴾ And there is in the Book of Allah no good tiding to Ibrahim of a male child except with Ishaq.
[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/190.]

Those who said it was Isma'il argued from the Qur'an with what Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that he used to say: "The one whom Allah, glorified is He, commanded Ibrahim to sacrifice from his two sons was Isma'il, and we find that in the Book of Allah, glorified is He. For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says, after finishing the story of the one sacrificed: ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous.﴾"

And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So We gave her good tidings of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Surah Hud: 71], meaning: a son, and a son's son. So He would not have commanded him to sacrifice Ishaq when the promised one from Allah, glorified and exalted is He, was in him. [That is, the promised child.] Since Allah did not mention Ishaq except after the conclusion of the account of the sacrifice, and then gave him the good tidings of Ishaq's offspring, we know that the sacrificed one was Isma'il."

Al-Qurazi said: I mentioned that to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Aziz, when he was caliph and I was with him in Syria. 'Umar said to me: "This matter, I had not considered it, and I indeed see it as you have said." Then he sent for a man who was with him in Syria, who had been a Jew, then became Muslim and his Islam was good, and who used to consider himself among the scholars of the Jews. 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Aziz asked him about that while I was with him, and he said: "Which of Ibrahim's two sons was he commanded to sacrifice?" He said: "Isma'il." Then he said: "By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful, the Jews do know that, but they envy you, the Arab folk, that your father should be the one concerning whom Allah, glorified and exalted is He, issued that command, and the virtue Allah mentioned of him for his patience in what he was commanded. So they deny that and claim it was Ishaq, because Ishaq is their father."

They also argued that the two horns of the ram were hung in the Ka'bah in the hands of the descendants of Isma'il until the House burned and the two horns burned in the days of Ibn al-Zubayr [i.e. 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam. Marginal note of the manuscript] and al-Hajjaj. al-Sha'bi said: "I saw the two horns of the ram hanging in the Ka'bah, and the two horns were an inheritance of the children of Isma'il from their father. The children of Ishaq, who are the Romans, did not contend with them over that, and they were greater, mightier and more powerful than the Arabs." This is the strongest proof that the sacrificed one was Isma'il.

al-Asma'i said: I asked Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' about whether the sacrificed one was Ishaq or Isma'il? He said to me: "O Asma', where has your intellect gone?

When was Ishaq (peace be upon him) in Mecca? Isma'il was in Mecca, and he is the one who built the House with his father Ibrahim (peace be upon them both), as Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House, and Isma'il [with him]﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 127], and the place of sacrifice in Mecca is beyond doubt."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Mundhir al-Darir say: I heard Abu Muhammad al-Zanjani al-Mu'addib say: Abu Sa'id al-Darir was asked about the sacrificed one, and he recited:

Indeed the sacrificed one, may you be guided, is Isma'il... the Book and the Revelation have spoken of that.
He was honoured by it, the one whom God singled out, our Prophet, and interpretation and exegesis came with it.
If you are his nation, do not deny him a honour that preference has singled out for him.
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/100.]

As for the account of the sacrifice, al-Suddi said with his chain: When Ibrahim the Friend (peace be upon him) separated from his people, emigrating to Syria, fleeing with his religion, as Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ he called upon Allah, glorified and exalted is He, to grant him a righteous son from Sarah, and he said: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ When the angels, the messengers sent to the overturned cities, came to him as guests and gave him the good tidings of a forbearing boy, Ibrahim said, upon being given the good tidings of him:
"Then he is indeed for Allah, a sacrifice." When the boy was born and reached with him the age of exertion, it was said: "Fulfil your vow which you vowed." This was the cause of Allah, exalted is He, commanding His messenger Ibrahim to sacrifice his son. Ibrahim then said to Ishaq: "Come, let us go and offer a sacrifice to Allah, exalted is He," and he took a knife and a rope and set off with him, until when he had gone with him between the mountains, the boy said to him: "O father, where is your sacrifice?" He said: ﴿O my son, indeed I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so see what you think.﴾ He said: ﴿O my father, do as you are commanded; you will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast.﴾

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: Whenever Ibrahim visited Hajar and Isma'il, he would be carried upon al-Buraq; he would set out from Syria, pray in Mecca, and return from Mecca and spend the night with his family in Syria. Until, when Isma'il reached with him the age of exertion and took his own self, and he hoped for him, for what he was hoping for of worshipping his Lord and magnifying His sanctities, he was shown in a dream that he should sacrifice him. When he was commanded to do so, he said to his son: "O my son, take the rope and the knife, then let us go to this valley to gather wood." When Ibrahim was alone with his son in the valley of [Thabir], he informed him of what he had been commanded, as Allah, exalted is He, mentioned. They said:

Then his son, whom he intended to sacrifice, said: "O father, tighten my bonds so that I do not thrash about, and keep your garments away from me so that no blood from me splashes upon them, lest my reward be diminished and my mother see it and grieve; and sharpen your two blades, and hasten the passing of the knife over my throat, so that it may be easier for me in death, for death is severe. And when you come to my mother, convey my greetings of peace to her; and if you see fit to return my shirt to my mother, then do so, for perhaps it will console her for me."

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him: "Excellent helper are you, my son, in the matter of Allah's command."

Ibrahim did what his son had instructed him, then he turned to him, kissing him, while he had bound him and was weeping, and the son was weeping until the tears pooled beneath his cheek. Then he placed the knife upon his throat, but the knife did not cut. al-Suddi said: Allah placed a plate of copper upon his throat. They said: Then the son said at that point: "O father, lay me down on my face upon my forehead, for when you look at my face you will have mercy on me, and a tenderness will overcome you that stands between you and the command of Allah; and I will not look at the blade, so I will not panic." Ibrahim did so, and placed the knife upon his nape, and the knife turned over, and it was called out: "O Ibrahim, enough! You have indeed fulfilled the vision. This is your sacrifice as a ransom for your son, so slaughter it instead of him." Ibrahim looked, and there he saw Jibril with a ram, white-black and horned. Jibril said "Allahu akbar", and the ram said "Allahu akbar", Ibrahim said "Allahu akbar", and his son said "Allahu akbar". Ibrahim took the ram and brought it to the place of sacrifice at Mina and sacrificed it.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it was the beginning of Islam, and the head of the ram was hung by its horns in the spout of the Ka'bah."

al-Suddi said: When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) took the ram, he released his son, and he bent over him, kissing him and saying: "O my son, you have been given to me." Then he returned to Sarah and informed her of the news. Sarah grew distressed and said: "O Ibrahim, you wanted to sacrifice my son and did not tell me?" [101].

Abu Hurayrah narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar, and Ibn Ishaq from his shaykhs, they said: When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was shown the sacrifice of his son, Satan said: "By Allah, if I do not tempt the family of Ibrahim at this point, I will never tempt any of them ever."

So Satan appeared to them in the form of a man, and came to the mother of the boy and said to her: "Do you know where Ibrahim has taken your son?" She said:

He took him, saying, "He is gathering firewood for us from this valley." She said, "No, by God, he has not taken him except to slaughter him." She said, "No, he is more merciful to him and loves him more than that." He said, "He claims that God has commanded him to do so." She said, "If his Lord has commanded him, then he has done well to obey his Lord, and we submit to the command of God, Mighty and Majestic."

Then Satan left her and caught up with the boy as he was walking behind his father. He said to him, "Boy, do you know where your father is going?" He said, "He is gathering firewood for our family from this valley." He said, "By God, he only wants to slaughter you." He said, "Why?" He said, "He claims that his Lord has commanded him to do so." He said, "Then let him do what his Lord has commanded him. Hearing and obedience."

When the boy refused him, he turned to Abraham and said, "Where are you going, old man?" He said, "I want this valley for a need of mine there." He said, "By God, I see that Satan has come to you in your dream and commanded you to slaughter this son of yours." Abraham recognised him and said, "Get away from me, enemy of God! By God, I will certainly carry out the command of God." [102] [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/192, the report on the manner of the action of Abraham and his son.]]

Abu al-Tufayl narrated from Ibn Abbas that when Abraham was commanded to slaughter his son, Satan appeared to him at this al-Mash'ar (the sacred site near Muzdalifah), and raced him, and Abraham outpaced him. Then he went to Jamrat al-'Aqabah, and Satan appeared to him, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he left. Then he met him at the middle pillar, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he left. Then he caught up with him at the greatest pillar, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he left. Then he proceeded by the command of God, Mighty and Majestic, in that matter.

Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said: [[The verses in full are in Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/195, the report of Abraham and his son.]]

And for Abraham, who fulfils his vow, seeking reward, and who carries the rope and the knife,
His son, whom he could not bear to be parted from, even if he saw him among a band of enemies.
O my son, I have vowed you to God, a sacrifice; so be patient, my ransom, my state.
And he tightens the bond, I will not swerve from the knife, swerving as a captive in shackles does.
He has a blade that gleams upon the flesh, sharp, curved like a crescent.
While he was stripping the garments from him, his Lord ransomed him with a lawful ram.
He said, "Take this, and release your son, for I have accepted what you both did, without speech."
Souls often recoil from a matter, yet for it there is an opening like the loosening of a hobbled camel's tether.

This is the story of the sacrifice, as God, glorified is He, said: ﴿When he reached the age of exertion with him﴾. Ibn Abbas said: this means walking with his father to the (places of) camels [[In Tafsir al-Qurtubi 15/99: Ibn Abbas said it means reaching the age of puberty; Qatadah said it means he walked with his father.]]. Al-Hasan and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it means the intellect by which one is held accountable. Al-Dahhak said: it means movement. Ibn Zayd said: [it means] striving in worship.

﴿O my son, I see in a dream﴾: I saw in a dream that I am slaughtering you, in fulfilment of a vow upon me concerning you; I was commanded to do so. For Abraham (peace be upon him) saw on the night of the Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah) as if someone was saying to him: God commands you to slaughter this son of yours. When morning came, he pondered (rawwa) in himself, that is, he reflected from morning until evening: is this command from God or from Satan? Hence the day was called Tarwiyah (the day of reflection). When evening came, he saw the same dream again, the slaughter of his son. When morning came, he knew that this command was from God. Hence the day was called 'Arafah (the day of recognition).

Muqatil said: Abraham saw this for three consecutive nights. Ata' and Muqatil said: Abraham was commanded to slaughter his son in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). When he was certain of this, he informed his son, and said to him: ﴿So consider what you see?﴾. The majority read تَرَى with a fatha on the ta. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read تُرِي with a damma on the ta and a kasra on the ra', that is: what do you indicate? It was permissible for him to consult his son about proceeding with God's command, because he wished to know his son's patience in God's command and his resolve in obedience to Him. So his son said:

﴿O my father, do what you are commanded. You will find me, God willing, among the patient.﴾

﴿When both of them submitted﴾, that is, they yielded and humbled themselves to the command of God, Glorified and Exalted, and were content with it. Ibn Mas'ud read فلما سلّما (fa-lamma sallama), meaning they entrusted (themselves). Ibn Abbas read استسلما (istaslama). Qatadah said: this one submitted his son and this one submitted himself. ﴿And he laid him down upon his forehead﴾, that is, he threw him down, placed him on his side, and turned him onto his face for the slaughter. ﴿And We called out to him﴾. The scholars of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) said: the waw (الواو, the conjunction) here is extra (muqhamah), a connective particle, and its sense is: "We called out to him," as in His saying: ﴿And they agreed to put him in the bottom of the well, and We revealed to him﴾, meaning: "We revealed to him." And His saying: ﴿And they will be from every high ground, hastening, and the promise draws near﴾. Imru' al-Qays said:

"So when we passed the courtyard of the tribe and he turned aside..."

And a poet said:
"Until, when your bellies have become infested with lice, and you have seen your sons grown up,
And you have turned the back of the shield against us, indeed the base, the weak, the treacherous one..."

He meant: "you turned" (قلبتم).

﴿O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision. Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers. Indeed, this is the clear trial﴾: the manifest test concerning that which necessitates a blessing or a calamity. For this reason, blessings are called بلاء (balaa') and trials are called بلاء, because each is named after its cause through which it leads to it, just as the causes of death are called "this very death."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 37, verse 99–106 (part 1 of 2):

Ibrahim said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord," that is, to the pleasure of my Lord, and that is the place to which he was commanded to go. Its counterpart is His saying: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord."﴾ [Surah al-Ankabut: 26]. It was also said: "I am going to my Lord" with myself and my deeds. ﴿He will guide me.﴾ ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ (abridged) That is: "My Lord, grant me a righteous son from among the righteous."

﴿So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy.﴾ ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion,﴾ that boy, ﴿he said, "O my son, indeed I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you..."﴾ (the verse). The early scholars of the Muslim scholars differed about which of his two sons Ibrahim was commanded to sacrifice, after the consensus of [the people of the specialized knowledge] that it was Ishaq (Isaac). A group said: the one sacrificed was Ishaq. Among the Companions, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib held this view; and among the later generations and their followers: Ka'b al-Ahbar, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, Masruq, 'Ikrimah, al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, 'Ata', Muqatil, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, al-Zubayri and al-Suddi.

This is the narration of 'Ikrimah and Ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Harb told us, saying: Sunayd ibn Dawud told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Layth ibn Sa'd, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "It was Ishaq."

And al-Hasan informed me, saying: 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: Radwan ibn Ahmad al-Saydalani told us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-'Utaridi told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from Hajjaj, from al-Qasim ibn Nafi', from Abu al-Tufayl, from 'Ali, who said: "The one whom Ibrahim (peace be upon him) intended to sacrifice was Ishaq."
[92] [Al-Mustadrak: 2/558 – and the narration is from Ibn 'Abbas.]

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, who said: A man boasted in the presence of Ibn Mas'ud, saying: "I am so-and-so son of so-and-so, son of the noble elders." 'Abdullah said: "That is Yusuf son of Ya'qub son of Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the friend of Allah (peace be upon them)."

And al-Husayn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Abdullah told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: al-Mubarak told us, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who said: "The one whom Allah ransomed with a great sacrifice (dhibhin 'azim) was Ishaq."

And al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ibn Habish told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-Sufi told us, saying: Abu 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn Bakkar told us, saying: Khalid ibn 'Abdullah al-Wasiti told us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "The one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice was Ishaq (peace be upon them both)."

And al-Hasan informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan ibn 'Abdullah informed us, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Abdullah told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice was Ishaq."

And al-Hasan informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid told us, saying: 'Abbas al-Duri told us, saying: Abu Salamah – meaning al-Minqari – told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi told us, from Musa, the freedman of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "When Ibrahim was shown in a dream the sacrifice of Ishaq, he travelled with him a distance of a month in a single morning until he brought him to the place of sacrifice at Mina. Then when Allah diverted the slaughter from him and commanded him to sacrifice the ram, he sacrificed it, and he travelled with him a distance of a month in a single afternoon, the valleys and mountains being folded up for him."

Sufyan narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, from his father, who said: Musa said: "O Lord, they say: 'the God of Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub.' Why do they say that?" He said: "Indeed Ibrahim never preferred anything over Me without Me choosing him over it; and Ishaq gave Me his life for the sacrifice, while he is more generous than that; and Ya'qub, whenever I increased him in trial, his good opinion of Me increased."
[93] [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 23/97.]

Hamzah al-Zayyat narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, who said: Yusuf said to the king: "Would you desire to eat with me, or would you disdain? I am, by Allah, Yusuf son of Ya'qub, the prophet of Allah, son of Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the friend of Allah (peace be upon them)?!"
[94] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/7.]

Others said: it was Isma'il. To this view went 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, Abu al-Tufayl 'Amir ibn Wathilah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Yusuf ibn Mihran, Mujahid, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi; and it is the narration of 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Abu Hamzah Nasr ibn 'Imran al-Dab'i and Yusuf ibn Majak from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The one ransomed was Isma'il, and the Jews claimed it was Ishaq, and the Jews lied."

Both views have been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ). If either of them were authentic by consensus, he would not have attributed it to another. [That is what is in the manuscript.] As for the narration reported from him (ﷺ) that the sacrificed one was Ishaq:
Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad [said] [In the manuscript: "said."] told us, saying: Ibn Mujahid told us, saying: Musa ibn Ishaq told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Shanbah told us, saying: al-Ashyab informed us, saying:
Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice was Ishaq."
[95] [Al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim, with variation: 2/557.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Lu'lu' told us, saying: al-Haytham ibn Khalaf informed us, saying:
Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I was informed, from Safwan ibn Sulaym and Zayd ibn Aslam, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), that he said: "Indeed Ishaq is the one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice."
[96]

Abu Tahir ibn Khuzaymah informed us in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, in the year three hundred and eighty-three [he read it to me]... He said: My grandfather informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Hujr told us, saying: 'Umar ibn Hafs told us, from Aban, from Anas, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ishaq will intercede after me, and he will say: 'O Lord, You have affirmed Your Prophet, and I offered myself for the sacrifice; so do not admit into the Fire anyone who has not associated anything with You.'" He said: "Then the Blessed and Exalted will say: 'By My might, I will not admit into the Fire anyone who does not associate anything with Me.'"
[97]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Nasrawayh told us, saying: Abu Hafs 'Umar ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Jawhari told us, saying: 'Isa ibn Musawwar al-Jawhari told us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam told us, from his father, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave me the choice between forgiving half of my Ummah or my intercession, and I chose my intercession, and I hoped it would be more general for my Ummah. Had it not been for what the righteous servant (al-'abd al-salih) preceded me to, my supplication would have been hastened for them. Indeed, when Allah relieved Ishaq of the distress of the sacrifice, it was said: 'O Ishaq, ask and you will be given.' He said: 'By the One in whose hand is my soul, I will hasten it before the whisper of Satan: O Allah, whoever dies without associating anything with You, forgive him and admit him into Paradise.'"
[98] [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/202; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/18, with slight variation.]

As for what was narrated from him (ﷺ) that the sacrificed one was Isma'il:
'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated from 'Ubaydullah ibn Muhammad al-'Utbi – of the descendants of 'Utbah ibn Abi Sufyan – from his father, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Sa'id told me, from al-Sunabihi, who said: We were with Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan when they mentioned the sacrificed one, whether Isma'il or Ishaq. He said: "You have come to the one who knows; I was with the Prophet (ﷺ) when a man came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, give me from what Allah has bestowed upon you, O son of the two sacrificed ones.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed." It was said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, what are the two sacrificed ones?" He said: "When 'Abd al-Muttalib dug the well of Zamzam, he vowed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that if Allah made its matter easy for him, he would sacrifice one of his sons. The arrow fell upon 'Abdullah, but his maternal uncles prevented him, saying: 'Ransom your son with a hundred camels.' So he ransomed him with a hundred camels. The second was Isma'il (peace be upon him)."
[99] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/113, with variation.]

This is what has come in the reports on this subject. As for the proof of those who say it was Ishaq from the Qur'an: Allah, glorified is He, informed about His friend Ibrahim (peace be upon him) when he separated from his people, emigrating to Syria with his wife Sarah and his nephew Lut, and he said: ﴿Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me.﴾ He supplicated and said: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ That was before he knew Hajar, and before Isma'il's mother became his. Then the account followed of His answering his supplication and giving him the good tidings of ﴿a forbearing boy,﴾ then of Ibrahim's dream that he should sacrifice that boy who had been given the good tidings of, when ﴿he reached with him [the age of] exertion.﴾ And there is in the Book of Allah no good tiding to Ibrahim of a male child except with Ishaq.
[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/190.]

Those who said it was Isma'il argued from the Qur'an with what Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that he used to say: "The one whom Allah, glorified is He, commanded Ibrahim to sacrifice from his two sons was Isma'il, and we find that in the Book of Allah, glorified is He. For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says, after finishing the story of the one sacrificed: ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous.﴾"

And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So We gave her good tidings of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Surah Hud: 71], meaning: a son, and a son's son. So He would not have commanded him to sacrifice Ishaq when the promised one from Allah, glorified and exalted is He, was in him. [That is, the promised child.] Since Allah did not mention Ishaq except after the conclusion of the account of the sacrifice, and then gave him the good tidings of Ishaq's offspring, we know that the sacrificed one was Isma'il."

Al-Qurazi said: I mentioned that to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Aziz, when he was caliph and I was with him in Syria. 'Umar said to me: "This matter, I had not considered it, and I indeed see it as you have said." Then he sent for a man who was with him in Syria, who had been a Jew, then became Muslim and his Islam was good, and who used to consider himself among the scholars of the Jews. 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Aziz asked him about that while I was with him, and he said: "Which of Ibrahim's two sons was he commanded to sacrifice?" He said: "Isma'il." Then he said: "By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful, the Jews do know that, but they envy you, the Arab folk, that your father should be the one concerning whom Allah, glorified and exalted is He, issued that command, and the virtue Allah mentioned of him for his patience in what he was commanded. So they deny that and claim it was Ishaq, because Ishaq is their father."

They also argued that the two horns of the ram were hung in the Ka'bah in the hands of the descendants of Isma'il until the House burned and the two horns burned in the days of Ibn al-Zubayr [i.e. 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam. Marginal note of the manuscript] and al-Hajjaj. al-Sha'bi said: "I saw the two horns of the ram hanging in the Ka'bah, and the two horns were an inheritance of the children of Isma'il from their father. The children of Ishaq, who are the Romans, did not contend with them over that, and they were greater, mightier and more powerful than the Arabs." This is the strongest proof that the sacrificed one was Isma'il.

al-Asma'i said: I asked Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' about whether the sacrificed one was Ishaq or Isma'il? He said to me: "O Asma', where has your intellect gone?

When was Ishaq (peace be upon him) in Mecca? Isma'il was in Mecca, and he is the one who built the House with his father Ibrahim (peace be upon them both), as Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House, and Isma'il [with him]﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 127], and the place of sacrifice in Mecca is beyond doubt."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Mundhir al-Darir say: I heard Abu Muhammad al-Zanjani al-Mu'addib say: Abu Sa'id al-Darir was asked about the sacrificed one, and he recited:

Indeed the sacrificed one, may you be guided, is Isma'il... the Book and the Revelation have spoken of that.
He was honoured by it, the one whom God singled out, our Prophet, and interpretation and exegesis came with it.
If you are his nation, do not deny him a honour that preference has singled out for him.
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/100.]

As for the account of the sacrifice, al-Suddi said with his chain: When Ibrahim the Friend (peace be upon him) separated from his people, emigrating to Syria, fleeing with his religion, as Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ he called upon Allah, glorified and exalted is He, to grant him a righteous son from Sarah, and he said: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ When the angels, the messengers sent to the overturned cities, came to him as guests and gave him the good tidings of a forbearing boy, Ibrahim said, upon being given the good tidings of him:
"Then he is indeed for Allah, a sacrifice." When the boy was born and reached with him the age of exertion, it was said: "Fulfil your vow which you vowed." This was the cause of Allah, exalted is He, commanding His messenger Ibrahim to sacrifice his son. Ibrahim then said to Ishaq: "Come, let us go and offer a sacrifice to Allah, exalted is He," and he took a knife and a rope and set off with him, until when he had gone with him between the mountains, the boy said to him: "O father, where is your sacrifice?" He said: ﴿O my son, indeed I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so see what you think.﴾ He said: ﴿O my father, do as you are commanded; you will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast.﴾

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: Whenever Ibrahim visited Hajar and Isma'il, he would be carried upon al-Buraq; he would set out from Syria, pray in Mecca, and return from Mecca and spend the night with his family in Syria. Until, when Isma'il reached with him the age of exertion and took his own self, and he hoped for him, for what he was hoping for of worshipping his Lord and magnifying His sanctities, he was shown in a dream that he should sacrifice him. When he was commanded to do so, he said to his son: "O my son, take the rope and the knife, then let us go to this valley to gather wood." When Ibrahim was alone with his son in the valley of [Thabir], he informed him of what he had been commanded, as Allah, exalted is He, mentioned. They said:

Then his son, whom he intended to sacrifice, said: "O father, tighten my bonds so that I do not thrash about, and keep your garments away from me so that no blood from me splashes upon them, lest my reward be diminished and my mother see it and grieve; and sharpen your two blades, and hasten the passing of the knife over my throat, so that it may be easier for me in death, for death is severe. And when you come to my mother, convey my greetings of peace to her; and if you see fit to return my shirt to my mother, then do so, for perhaps it will console her for me."

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him: "Excellent helper are you, my son, in the matter of Allah's command."

Ibrahim did what his son had instructed him, then he turned to him, kissing him, while he had bound him and was weeping, and the son was weeping until the tears pooled beneath his cheek. Then he placed the knife upon his throat, but the knife did not cut. al-Suddi said: Allah placed a plate of copper upon his throat. They said: Then the son said at that point: "O father, lay me down on my face upon my forehead, for when you look at my face you will have mercy on me, and a tenderness will overcome you that stands between you and the command of Allah; and I will not look at the blade, so I will not panic." Ibrahim did so, and placed the knife upon his nape, and the knife turned over, and it was called out: "O Ibrahim, enough! You have indeed fulfilled the vision. This is your sacrifice as a ransom for your son, so slaughter it instead of him." Ibrahim looked, and there he saw Jibril with a ram, white-black and horned. Jibril said "Allahu akbar", and the ram said "Allahu akbar", Ibrahim said "Allahu akbar", and his son said "Allahu akbar". Ibrahim took the ram and brought it to the place of sacrifice at Mina and sacrificed it.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it was the beginning of Islam, and the head of the ram was hung by its horns in the spout of the Ka'bah."

al-Suddi said: When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) took the ram, he released his son, and he bent over him, kissing him and saying: "O my son, you have been given to me." Then he returned to Sarah and informed her of the news. Sarah grew distressed and said: "O Ibrahim, you wanted to sacrifice my son and did not tell me?" [101].

Abu Hurayrah narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar, and Ibn Ishaq from his shaykhs, they said: When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was shown the sacrifice of his son, Satan said: "By Allah, if I do not tempt the family of Ibrahim at this point, I will never tempt any of them ever."

So Satan appeared to them in the form of a man, and came to the mother of the boy and said to her: "Do you know where Ibrahim has taken your son?" She said:

He took him, saying, "He is gathering firewood for us from this valley." She said, "No, by God, he has not taken him except to slaughter him." She said, "No, he is more merciful to him and loves him more than that." He said, "He claims that God has commanded him to do so." She said, "If his Lord has commanded him, then he has done well to obey his Lord, and we submit to the command of God, Mighty and Majestic."

Then Satan left her and caught up with the boy as he was walking behind his father. He said to him, "Boy, do you know where your father is going?" He said, "He is gathering firewood for our family from this valley." He said, "By God, he only wants to slaughter you." He said, "Why?" He said, "He claims that his Lord has commanded him to do so." He said, "Then let him do what his Lord has commanded him. Hearing and obedience."

When the boy refused him, he turned to Abraham and said, "Where are you going, old man?" He said, "I want this valley for a need of mine there." He said, "By God, I see that Satan has come to you in your dream and commanded you to slaughter this son of yours." Abraham recognised him and said, "Get away from me, enemy of God! By God, I will certainly carry out the command of God." [102] [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/192, the report on the manner of the action of Abraham and his son.]]

Abu al-Tufayl narrated from Ibn Abbas that when Abraham was commanded to slaughter his son, Satan appeared to him at this al-Mash'ar (the sacred site near Muzdalifah), and raced him, and Abraham outpaced him. Then he went to Jamrat al-'Aqabah, and Satan appeared to him, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he left. Then he met him at the middle pillar, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he left. Then he caught up with him at the greatest pillar, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he left. Then he proceeded by the command of God, Mighty and Majestic, in that matter.

Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said: [[The verses in full are in Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/195, the report of Abraham and his son.]]

And for Abraham, who fulfils his vow, seeking reward, and who carries the rope and the knife,
His son, whom he could not bear to be parted from, even if he saw him among a band of enemies.
O my son, I have vowed you to God, a sacrifice; so be patient, my ransom, my state.
And he tightens the bond, I will not swerve from the knife, swerving as a captive in shackles does.
He has a blade that gleams upon the flesh, sharp, curved like a crescent.
While he was stripping the garments from him, his Lord ransomed him with a lawful ram.
He said, "Take this, and release your son, for I have accepted what you both did, without speech."
Souls often recoil from a matter, yet for it there is an opening like the loosening of a hobbled camel's tether.

This is the story of the sacrifice, as God, glorified is He, said: ﴿When he reached the age of exertion with him﴾. Ibn Abbas said: this means walking with his father to the (places of) camels [[In Tafsir al-Qurtubi 15/99: Ibn Abbas said it means reaching the age of puberty; Qatadah said it means he walked with his father.]]. Al-Hasan and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it means the intellect by which one is held accountable. Al-Dahhak said: it means movement. Ibn Zayd said: [it means] striving in worship.

﴿O my son, I see in a dream﴾: I saw in a dream that I am slaughtering you, in fulfilment of a vow upon me concerning you; I was commanded to do so. For Abraham (peace be upon him) saw on the night of the Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah) as if someone was saying to him: God commands you to slaughter this son of yours. When morning came, he pondered (rawwa) in himself, that is, he reflected from morning until evening: is this command from God or from Satan? Hence the day was called Tarwiyah (the day of reflection). When evening came, he saw the same dream again, the slaughter of his son. When morning came, he knew that this command was from God. Hence the day was called 'Arafah (the day of recognition).

Muqatil said: Abraham saw this for three consecutive nights. Ata' and Muqatil said: Abraham was commanded to slaughter his son in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). When he was certain of this, he informed his son, and said to him: ﴿So consider what you see?﴾. The majority read تَرَى with a fatha on the ta. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read تُرِي with a damma on the ta and a kasra on the ra', that is: what do you indicate? It was permissible for him to consult his son about proceeding with God's command, because he wished to know his son's patience in God's command and his resolve in obedience to Him. So his son said:

﴿O my father, do what you are commanded. You will find me, God willing, among the patient.﴾

﴿When both of them submitted﴾, that is, they yielded and humbled themselves to the command of God, Glorified and Exalted, and were content with it. Ibn Mas'ud read فلما سلّما (fa-lamma sallama), meaning they entrusted (themselves). Ibn Abbas read استسلما (istaslama). Qatadah said: this one submitted his son and this one submitted himself. ﴿And he laid him down upon his forehead﴾, that is, he threw him down, placed him on his side, and turned him onto his face for the slaughter. ﴿And We called out to him﴾. The scholars of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) said: the waw (الواو, the conjunction) here is extra (muqhamah), a connective particle, and its sense is: "We called out to him," as in His saying: ﴿And they agreed to put him in the bottom of the well, and We revealed to him﴾, meaning: "We revealed to him." And His saying: ﴿And they will be from every high ground, hastening, and the promise draws near﴾. Imru' al-Qays said:

"So when we passed the courtyard of the tribe and he turned aside..."

And a poet said:
"Until, when your bellies have become infested with lice, and you have seen your sons grown up,
And you have turned the back of the shield against us, indeed the base, the weak, the treacherous one..."

He meant: "you turned" (قلبتم).

﴿O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision. Indeed, thus do We reward the good-doers. Indeed, this is the clear trial﴾: the manifest test concerning that which necessitates a blessing or a calamity. For this reason, blessings are called بلاء (balaa') and trials are called بلاء, because each is named after its cause through which it leads to it, just as the causes of death are called "this very death."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 37, verse 99–106 (part 1 of 2):

Ibrahim said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord," that is, to the pleasure of my Lord, and that is the place to which he was commanded to go. Its counterpart is His saying: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord."﴾ [Surah al-Ankabut: 26]. It was also said: "I am going to my Lord" with myself and my deeds. ﴿He will guide me.﴾ ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ (abridged) That is: "My Lord, grant me a righteous son from among the righteous."

﴿So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy.﴾ ﴿And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion,﴾ that boy, ﴿he said, "O my son, indeed I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you..."﴾ (the verse). The early scholars of the Muslim scholars differed about which of his two sons Ibrahim was commanded to sacrifice, after the consensus of [the people of the specialized knowledge] that it was Ishaq (Isaac). A group said: the one sacrificed was Ishaq. Among the Companions, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib held this view; and among the later generations and their followers: Ka'b al-Ahbar, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, Masruq, 'Ikrimah, al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, 'Ata', Muqatil, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, al-Zubayri and al-Suddi.

This is the narration of 'Ikrimah and Ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas. al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Harb told us, saying: Sunayd ibn Dawud told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Layth ibn Sa'd, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "It was Ishaq."

And al-Hasan informed me, saying: 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: Radwan ibn Ahmad al-Saydalani told us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-'Utaridi told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from Hajjaj, from al-Qasim ibn Nafi', from Abu al-Tufayl, from 'Ali, who said: "The one whom Ibrahim (peace be upon him) intended to sacrifice was Ishaq."
[92] [Al-Mustadrak: 2/558 – and the narration is from Ibn 'Abbas.]

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, who said: A man boasted in the presence of Ibn Mas'ud, saying: "I am so-and-so son of so-and-so, son of the noble elders." 'Abdullah said: "That is Yusuf son of Ya'qub son of Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the friend of Allah (peace be upon them)."

And al-Husayn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Abdullah told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: al-Mubarak told us, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who said: "The one whom Allah ransomed with a great sacrifice (dhibhin 'azim) was Ishaq."

And al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ibn Habish told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-Sufi told us, saying: Abu 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn Bakkar told us, saying: Khalid ibn 'Abdullah al-Wasiti told us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "The one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice was Ishaq (peace be upon them both)."

And al-Hasan informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan ibn 'Abdullah informed us, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Abdullah told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice was Ishaq."

And al-Hasan informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid told us, saying: 'Abbas al-Duri told us, saying: Abu Salamah – meaning al-Minqari – told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi told us, from Musa, the freedman of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "When Ibrahim was shown in a dream the sacrifice of Ishaq, he travelled with him a distance of a month in a single morning until he brought him to the place of sacrifice at Mina. Then when Allah diverted the slaughter from him and commanded him to sacrifice the ram, he sacrificed it, and he travelled with him a distance of a month in a single afternoon, the valleys and mountains being folded up for him."

Sufyan narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, from his father, who said: Musa said: "O Lord, they say: 'the God of Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub.' Why do they say that?" He said: "Indeed Ibrahim never preferred anything over Me without Me choosing him over it; and Ishaq gave Me his life for the sacrifice, while he is more generous than that; and Ya'qub, whenever I increased him in trial, his good opinion of Me increased."
[93] [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 23/97.]

Hamzah al-Zayyat narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, who said: Yusuf said to the king: "Would you desire to eat with me, or would you disdain? I am, by Allah, Yusuf son of Ya'qub, the prophet of Allah, son of Ishaq, the sacrificed one of Allah, son of Ibrahim, the friend of Allah (peace be upon them)?!"
[94] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/7.]

Others said: it was Isma'il. To this view went 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, Abu al-Tufayl 'Amir ibn Wathilah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Yusuf ibn Mihran, Mujahid, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi; and it is the narration of 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Abu Hamzah Nasr ibn 'Imran al-Dab'i and Yusuf ibn Majak from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The one ransomed was Isma'il, and the Jews claimed it was Ishaq, and the Jews lied."

Both views have been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ). If either of them were authentic by consensus, he would not have attributed it to another. [That is what is in the manuscript.] As for the narration reported from him (ﷺ) that the sacrificed one was Ishaq:
Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and 'Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad [said] [In the manuscript: "said."] told us, saying: Ibn Mujahid told us, saying: Musa ibn Ishaq told us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Shanbah told us, saying: al-Ashyab informed us, saying:
Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice was Ishaq."
[95] [Al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim, with variation: 2/557.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Lu'lu' told us, saying: al-Haytham ibn Khalaf informed us, saying:
Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I was informed, from Safwan ibn Sulaym and Zayd ibn Aslam, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), that he said: "Indeed Ishaq is the one whom Ibrahim intended to sacrifice."
[96]

Abu Tahir ibn Khuzaymah informed us in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, in the year three hundred and eighty-three [he read it to me]... He said: My grandfather informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Hujr told us, saying: 'Umar ibn Hafs told us, from Aban, from Anas, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ishaq will intercede after me, and he will say: 'O Lord, You have affirmed Your Prophet, and I offered myself for the sacrifice; so do not admit into the Fire anyone who has not associated anything with You.'" He said: "Then the Blessed and Exalted will say: 'By My might, I will not admit into the Fire anyone who does not associate anything with Me.'"
[97]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Nasrawayh told us, saying: Abu Hafs 'Umar ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Jawhari told us, saying: 'Isa ibn Musawwar al-Jawhari told us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam told us, from his father, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave me the choice between forgiving half of my Ummah or my intercession, and I chose my intercession, and I hoped it would be more general for my Ummah. Had it not been for what the righteous servant (al-'abd al-salih) preceded me to, my supplication would have been hastened for them. Indeed, when Allah relieved Ishaq of the distress of the sacrifice, it was said: 'O Ishaq, ask and you will be given.' He said: 'By the One in whose hand is my soul, I will hasten it before the whisper of Satan: O Allah, whoever dies without associating anything with You, forgive him and admit him into Paradise.'"
[98] [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/202; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/18, with slight variation.]

As for what was narrated from him (ﷺ) that the sacrificed one was Isma'il:
'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated from 'Ubaydullah ibn Muhammad al-'Utbi – of the descendants of 'Utbah ibn Abi Sufyan – from his father, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Sa'id told me, from al-Sunabihi, who said: We were with Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan when they mentioned the sacrificed one, whether Isma'il or Ishaq. He said: "You have come to the one who knows; I was with the Prophet (ﷺ) when a man came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, give me from what Allah has bestowed upon you, O son of the two sacrificed ones.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed." It was said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, what are the two sacrificed ones?" He said: "When 'Abd al-Muttalib dug the well of Zamzam, he vowed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that if Allah made its matter easy for him, he would sacrifice one of his sons. The arrow fell upon 'Abdullah, but his maternal uncles prevented him, saying: 'Ransom your son with a hundred camels.' So he ransomed him with a hundred camels. The second was Isma'il (peace be upon him)."
[99] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/113, with variation.]

This is what has come in the reports on this subject. As for the proof of those who say it was Ishaq from the Qur'an: Allah, glorified is He, informed about His friend Ibrahim (peace be upon him) when he separated from his people, emigrating to Syria with his wife Sarah and his nephew Lut, and he said: ﴿Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me.﴾ He supplicated and said: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ That was before he knew Hajar, and before Isma'il's mother became his. Then the account followed of His answering his supplication and giving him the good tidings of ﴿a forbearing boy,﴾ then of Ibrahim's dream that he should sacrifice that boy who had been given the good tidings of, when ﴿he reached with him [the age of] exertion.﴾ And there is in the Book of Allah no good tiding to Ibrahim of a male child except with Ishaq.
[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/190.]

Those who said it was Isma'il argued from the Qur'an with what Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that he used to say: "The one whom Allah, glorified is He, commanded Ibrahim to sacrifice from his two sons was Isma'il, and we find that in the Book of Allah, glorified is He. For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says, after finishing the story of the one sacrificed: ﴿And We gave him good tidings of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous.﴾"

And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So We gave her good tidings of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Surah Hud: 71], meaning: a son, and a son's son. So He would not have commanded him to sacrifice Ishaq when the promised one from Allah, glorified and exalted is He, was in him. [That is, the promised child.] Since Allah did not mention Ishaq except after the conclusion of the account of the sacrifice, and then gave him the good tidings of Ishaq's offspring, we know that the sacrificed one was Isma'il."

Al-Qurazi said: I mentioned that to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Aziz, when he was caliph and I was with him in Syria. 'Umar said to me: "This matter, I had not considered it, and I indeed see it as you have said." Then he sent for a man who was with him in Syria, who had been a Jew, then became Muslim and his Islam was good, and who used to consider himself among the scholars of the Jews. 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Aziz asked him about that while I was with him, and he said: "Which of Ibrahim's two sons was he commanded to sacrifice?" He said: "Isma'il." Then he said: "By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful, the Jews do know that, but they envy you, the Arab folk, that your father should be the one concerning whom Allah, glorified and exalted is He, issued that command, and the virtue Allah mentioned of him for his patience in what he was commanded. So they deny that and claim it was Ishaq, because Ishaq is their father."

They also argued that the two horns of the ram were hung in the Ka'bah in the hands of the descendants of Isma'il until the House burned and the two horns burned in the days of Ibn al-Zubayr [i.e. 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam. Marginal note of the manuscript] and al-Hajjaj. al-Sha'bi said: "I saw the two horns of the ram hanging in the Ka'bah, and the two horns were an inheritance of the children of Isma'il from their father. The children of Ishaq, who are the Romans, did not contend with them over that, and they were greater, mightier and more powerful than the Arabs." This is the strongest proof that the sacrificed one was Isma'il.

al-Asma'i said: I asked Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' about whether the sacrificed one was Ishaq or Isma'il? He said to me: "O Asma', where has your intellect gone?

When was Ishaq (peace be upon him) in Mecca? Isma'il was in Mecca, and he is the one who built the House with his father Ibrahim (peace be upon them both), as Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House, and Isma'il [with him]﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 127], and the place of sacrifice in Mecca is beyond doubt."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Mundhir al-Darir say: I heard Abu Muhammad al-Zanjani al-Mu'addib say: Abu Sa'id al-Darir was asked about the sacrificed one, and he recited:

Indeed the sacrificed one, may you be guided, is Isma'il... the Book and the Revelation have spoken of that.
He was honoured by it, the one whom God singled out, our Prophet, and interpretation and exegesis came with it.
If you are his nation, do not deny him a honour that preference has singled out for him.
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/100.]

As for the account of the sacrifice, al-Suddi said with his chain: When Ibrahim the Friend (peace be upon him) separated from his people, emigrating to Syria, fleeing with his religion, as Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ he called upon Allah, glorified and exalted is He, to grant him a righteous son from Sarah, and he said: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ When the angels, the messengers sent to the overturned cities, came to him as guests and gave him the good tidings of a forbearing boy, Ibrahim said, upon being given the good tidings of him:
"Then he is indeed for Allah, a sacrifice." When the boy was born and reached with him the age of exertion, it was said: "Fulfil your vow which you vowed." This was the cause of Allah, exalted is He, commanding His messenger Ibrahim to sacrifice his son. Ibrahim then said to Ishaq: "Come, let us go and offer a sacrifice to Allah, exalted is He," and he took a knife and a rope and set off with him, until when he had gone with him between the mountains, the boy said to him: "O father, where is your sacrifice?" He said: ﴿O my son, indeed I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so see what you think.﴾ He said: ﴿O my father, do as you are commanded; you will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast.﴾

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: Whenever Ibrahim visited Hajar and Isma'il, he would be carried upon al-Buraq; he would set out from Syria, pray in Mecca, and return from Mecca and spend the night with his family in Syria. Until, when Isma'il reached with him the age of exertion and took his own self, and he hoped for him, for what he was hoping for of worshipping his Lord and magnifying His sanctities, he was shown in a dream that he should sacrifice him. When he was commanded to do so, he said to his son: "O my son, take the rope and the knife, then let us go to this valley to gather wood." When Ibrahim was alone with his son in the valley of [Thabir], he informed him of what he had been commanded, as Allah, exalted is He, mentioned. They said:

Then his son, whom he intended to sacrifice, said: "O father, tighten my bonds so that I do not thrash about, and keep your garments away from me so that no blood from me splashes upon them, lest my reward be diminished and my mother see it and grieve; and sharpen your two blades, and hasten the passing of the knife over my throat, so that it may be easier for me in death, for death is severe. And when you come to my mother, convey my greetings of peace to her; and if you see fit to return my shirt to my mother, then do so, for perhaps it will console her for me."

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said to him: "Excellent helper are you, my son, in the matter of Allah's command."

Ibrahim did what his son had instructed him, then he turned to him, kissing him, while he had bound him and was weeping, and the son was weeping until the tears pooled beneath his cheek. Then he placed the knife upon his throat, but the knife did not cut. al-Suddi said: Allah placed a plate of copper upon his throat. They said: Then the son said at that point: "O father, lay me down on my face upon my forehead, for when you look at my face you will have mercy on me, and a tenderness will overcome you that stands between you and the command of Allah; and I will not look at the blade, so I will not panic." Ibrahim did so, and placed the knife upon his nape, and the knife turned over, and it was called out: "O Ibrahim, enough! You have indeed fulfilled the vision. This is your sacrifice as a ransom for your son, so slaughter it instead of him." Ibrahim looked, and there he saw Jibril with a ram, white-black and horned. Jibril said "Allahu akbar", and the ram said "Allahu akbar", Ibrahim said "Allahu akbar", and his son said "Allahu akbar". Ibrahim took the ram and brought it to the place of sacrifice at Mina and sacrificed it.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it was the beginning of Islam, and the head of the ram was hung by its horns in the spout of the Ka'bah."

al-Suddi said: When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) took the ram, he released his son, and he bent over him, kissing him and saying: "O my son, you have been given to me." Then he returned to Sarah and informed her of the news. Sarah grew distressed and said: "O Ibrahim, you wanted to sacrifice my son and did not tell me?" [101].

Abu Hurayrah narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar, and Ibn Ishaq from his shaykhs, they said: When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was shown the sacrifice of his son, Satan said: "By Allah, if I do not tempt the family of Ibrahim at this point, I will never tempt any of them ever."

So Satan appeared to them in the form of a man, and came to the mother of the boy and said to her: "Do you know where Ibrahim has taken your son?" She said:

He took him, saying, "He is gathering firewood for us from this valley." She said, "No, by God, he has not taken him except to slaughter him." She said, "No, he is more merciful to him and loves him more than that." He said, "He claims that God has commanded him to do so." She said, "If his Lord has commanded him, then he has done well to obey his Lord, and we submit to the command of God, Mighty and Majestic."

Then Satan left her and caught up with the boy as he was walking behind his father. He said to him, "Boy, do you know where your father is going?" He said, "He is gathering firewood for our family from this valley." He said, "By God, he only wants to slaughter you." He said, "Why?" He said, "He claims that his Lord has commanded him to do so." He said, "Then let him do what his Lord has commanded him. Hearing and obedience."

When the boy refused him, he turned to Abraham and said, "Where are you going, old man?" He said, "I want this valley for a need of mine there." He said, "By God, I see that Satan has come to you in your dream and commanded you to slaughter this son of yours." Abraham recognised him and said, "Get away from me, enemy of God! By God, I will certainly carry out the command of God." [102] [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/192, the report on the manner of the action of Abraham and his son.]]

Abu al-Tufayl narrated from Ibn Abbas that when Abraham was commanded to slaughter his son, Satan appeared to him at this al-Mash'ar (the sacred site near Muzdalifah), and raced him, and Abraham outpaced him. Then he went to Jamrat al-'Aqabah, and Satan appeared to him, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he left. Then he met him at the middle pillar, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he left. Then he caught up with him at the greatest pillar, and he threw seven pebbles at him until he left. Then he proceeded by the command of God, Mighty and Majestic, in that matter.

Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said: [[The verses in full are in Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/195, the report of Abraham and his son.]]

And for Abraham, who fulfils his vow, seeking reward, and who carries the rope and the knife,
His son, whom he could not bear to be parted from, even if he saw him among a band of enemies.
O my son, I have vowed you to God, a sacrifice; so be patient, my ransom, my state.
And he tightens the bond, I will not swerve from the knife, swerving as a captive in shackles does.
He has a blade that gleams upon the flesh, sharp, curved like a crescent.
While he was stripping the garments from him, his Lord ransomed him with a lawful ram.
He said, "Take this, and release your son, for I have accepted what you both did, without speech."
Souls often recoil from a matter, yet for it there is an opening like the loosening of a hobbled camel's tether.

This is the story of the sacrifice, as God, glorified is He, said: ﴿When he reached the age of exertion with him﴾. Ibn Abbas said: this means walking with his father to the (places of) camels [[In Tafsir al-Qurtubi 15/99: Ibn Abbas said it means reaching the age of puberty; Qatadah said it means he walked with his father.]]. Al-Hasan and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it means the intellect by which one is held accountable. Al-Dahhak said: it means movement. Ibn Zayd said: [it means] striving in worship.
