And indeed Ilyas (Elias) was among the messengers (﴿وَإِنَّ إِلْيَاسَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾). Abu Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim ibn al-Mu'hil informed us, saying: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm related to us, saying: Bakkar ibn Qutayba related to us, saying: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi related to us, saying: Qays ibn Abi Ishaq related to us, from Ubayya ibn Rabi'a, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Ilyas is Idris, and Israel is Ya'qub." Ikrima also held this view, and he said: "It is in the codex of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud): ﴿وَإِنَّ إِدْرِيسَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾." Abdullah and Ikrima alone held this opinion.

Others said: he was a prophet from among the prophets of the Children of Israel. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He was the paternal cousin of al-Yasa' (Elisha)." Ibn Ishaq said: "He is Ilyas ibn Yasin ibn al-'Izar ibn Harun ibn 'Imran." Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar and the scholars of narratives also said: When God, glorified is He, took the soul of the prophet Hizqil (Ezekiel), the offences among the Children of Israel grew great, corruption and polytheism appeared among them, they forgot the covenant of God, they set up idols and worshipped them besides God. So God sent to them Ilyas (peace be upon him) as a prophet. The prophets from the Children of Israel after Musa (peace be upon him) had been following the Torah and were sent to them to renew what they had forgotten of it. The Children of Israel at that time were scattered in the land of al-Sham, and there were many kings among them. The reason for this was that Yusha' ibn Nun, when he conquered the land of al-Sham after Musa and took possession of it, settled the Children of Israel there and divided it among them. He assigned to one tribe of them Ba'labakk and its surroundings, and they were the tribe of Ilyas, and Ilyas was from among them. So God sent him to them as a prophet. At that time over them was a king called [Ajab] [[The author vocalised it in 'Ara'is al-Majalis (pp. 192–199) as Lajab.]], who had gone astray and led his people astray, and compelled them to worship idols. He and his people worshipped an idol called Ba'l, which was twenty cubits tall and had four faces.

He said: Ilyas began to call them to God, glorified is He, but they, in all of this, would not listen to him at all, except for the king of Ba'labakk, who believed in him and affirmed him. Ilyas would support his affair, strengthen him and guide him. Ajab had a wife called Azbil [[The author vocalised it in the same source as Arbil.]], and he would appoint her over his subjects whenever he was absent from them on a raid or otherwise. She would appear before people as her husband did, ride as he rode, and sit in the seat of judgment, judging between people. She was a killer of prophets.

He said: She had a scribe, a wise man of faith who concealed his faith from her. This scribe had rescued from her hand three hundred prophets whom she intended to kill, each one of them, when they were sent, in addition to those before them, whose numbers were many. She was unchaste by nature, and there was no one on the face of the earth more shameless than her. Moreover, she had married seven kings of the Children of Israel and killed them all by assassination. She lived so long that it was said she bore seventy children.

He said: Ajab had a neighbour from the Children of Israel, a righteous man called Mazdaki, who had a garden from which he lived, and he devoted himself to cultivating and beautifying it. The garden was beside the palace of the king and his wife, and they would look out over that garden, taking their leisure in it, eating, drinking and resting there. Ajab, despite all this, treated him well, but his wife Azbil envied him for that garden, and she schemed to seize it from him when she heard people frequently mentioning the garden and marvelling at its beauty, saying: "How fitting it would be for this garden to belong to the people of this palace!" and marvelling at the king and his wife, asking how they had not taken it from its owner. The wife of the king kept scheming against the righteous servant Mazdaki, hoping to kill him and take his garden, while the king kept forbidding her from that, so she could find no way against him.

Then it happened that the king set out on a distant journey and his absence was prolonged. His wife Azbil seized the opportunity to plot against Mazdaki, while he was heedless of what she intended for him, devoted to the worship of his Lord and to improving his livelihood. Azbil gathered a group of people and ordered them to testify against Mazdaki that he had reviled her husband Ajab. They agreed to her request to bear witness against him.

Among the judgments of that time was that whoever reviled the king was to be killed, once the proof had been established against him. So she summoned Mazdaki and said to him: "It has reached me that you insulted the king and disparaged him." Mazdaki denied this. The woman said: "There are witnesses against you." She produced the witnesses, who testified falsely against him in the presence of the people, so she ordered Mazdaki to be killed. He was killed and she seized his garden by force. Thus God became angry with them for killing the righteous servant.

When the king returned from his journey, she told him the news. He said to her: "You have not done right, nor have you been successful. I do not think we will prosper after this, ever. We were rich without his garden; we used to take our leisure in it. He has been our neighbour and under our protection for a long time, so we treated him well and withheld harm from him, because of his due right over us. You have ended his neighbourliness with the worst treatment. Nothing has moved you to this audacity against him except your foolishness, your bad judgment and your lack of reflection on the consequences." She said: "I was only angry on your behalf, and I judged by your judgment." He said to her: "Does your forbearance not encompass it, and does your great station not urge you to pardon one man, so that you protect his neighbourhood?" She said: "What has happened has happened."

God, exalted is He, then sent Ilyas (peace be upon him) to Ajab the king and his people, and commanded him to inform them that God, glorified is He, had become angry for His friend when they killed him among them unjustly, and that He had sworn by Himself that if they two did not repent of their deed and did not return the garden to the heirs of Mazdaki, He would destroy them both—meaning Ajab and his wife—inside the garden in the worst condition, by shedding their blood, then leave them as two corpses lying there until their bones were stripped of their flesh, and they would enjoy it only briefly.

He said: Ilyas came and informed him of what God, exalted is He, had revealed to him concerning him, his wife and the garden. When the king heard that, his anger against him intensified, and then he said to him: "O Ilyas, by God, I see nothing in what you call to except falsehood. By God, I see that so-and-so and so-and-so (he named kings among them) who worshipped idols were only in the same state as we are, eating, drinking and enjoying themselves, possessing without diminishing their worldly life or their affair, which you claim is false. We see no superiority for you over us or over them."

He said: The king resolved to torture Ilyas and kill him. When Ilyas heard that and sensed the evil, he withdrew from him and left, and went to the highest mountain peaks. The king returned to the worship of Ba'l. Ilyas climbed the most difficult and loftiest mountain, and entered a cave in it. It is said that he remained there for seven years, homeless and fleeing, fearful, taking refuge in ravines and caves, eating from the plants of the earth and the fruit of trees. They, in their search for him, had placed watchers upon him, awaiting news of him and striving to seize him, while God, glorified and exalted is He, concealed him and warded off harm from him. When seven years had passed, God, exalted is He, permitted his appearance before them and the healing of his anger against them. God, glorified is He, afflicted a son of Ajab—he was his dearest child, the most precious to him, and the most like him—with an illness, so that he became gravely ill until he despaired of him. So he called upon his idol Ba'l—they had been seduced by Ba'l and magnified him, to the point that they had appointed four hundred attendants for him and assigned them to him as his trustees. The devil would enter the belly of the idol and speak with all kinds of speech, while the four hundred listened attentively to what the devil said, and the devil would whisper to them a law of misguidance, which they would write down for the people, and they would act upon it. They called them "the prophets."

When the son of the king's illness intensified, the king asked them to intercede for him with Ba'l and seek for his son, from him, recovery and well-being. They called upon him [[From 'Ara'is al-Majalis; in the manuscript: "fa-da'awhum" (they called them).]], but he did not respond to them. God, by His power, prevented the devil from entering the idol, so he could neither enter its belly nor speak. They strove greatly in supplicating to him, but he only grew more lifeless. When this went on too long for them, they said to Ajab: "In the land of al-Sham there are other gods, equal in greatness to your god. Send the prophets to them so that they may intercede for you with them, perhaps they will intercede for you with your god Ba'l, for he is angry with you. Had he not been angry with you, he would have answered you and healed your son."

Ajab said: "And for what reason is he angry with me, when I have obeyed him and sought his pleasure since I was born, never once displeasing him?" They said: "For the reason that you did not kill Ilyas; you neglected him until he escaped unharmed, and he disbelieves in your god and worships another. That is what has made him angry with you." Ajab said: "And how can I kill Ilyas today, when I am preoccupied from seeking him by my son's pain? Ilyas has no place where he may be sought or known, so that if my son were healed, I would devote myself to seeking him, and I would have no concern or occupation other than him, until I seize him and kill him, and thus relieve my god of him and please him."

He said: Then he sent his four hundred prophets to intercede with the gods [[From 'Ara'is al-Majalis; in the manuscript: "al-Hawn".]] that were in al-Sham, and to ask them to intercede with the idol of the king so that it would heal his son. They set out until, when they were opposite the mountain in which Ilyas was, God, glorified is He, revealed to Ilyas that he should descend from the mountain, confront them, stop them and speak to them, and He said to him: "Do not fear, for I will turn their evil away from you and cast terror into their hearts." So Ilyas came down from the mountain, and when he met them he stopped them. When they stood still, he said to them: "God, glorified is He, has sent me to you and to those behind you. So listen, O people, to the message of your Lord, that you may convey it to your master. Return to him and say to him: 'God says to you: Do you not know, O Ajab, that I am God, there is no god but I (﴿إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنَا﴾), the God of the Children of Israel, who created them, provided for them, gave them life and caused them to die? Has your ignorance and lack of knowledge led you to associate others with Me, and to seek healing for your son from other than Me, from those who possess nothing for themselves except what I will? I have sworn by My name that I will indeed enrage you concerning your son, and I will cause him to die at this very moment, until you know that no one possesses anything for him besides Me.'"

When he had said this to them, they returned, filled with terror of him. When they came to the king, they told him that and informed him that Ilyas had come down upon them. He was a tall, lean man, emaciated, dried out, with his hair fallen out and his skin peeling. He wore a garment of hair and a cloak which he had fastened on his chest with thorns. "He stopped us, and when he came near us, awe and terror were cast into our hearts, our tongues were cut off, and we, in this great number, while he was alone, could not speak to him, answer him, or even fill our eyes with him, until we returned to you." They related to him the words of Ilyas. Ajab said: "Life is of no benefit as long as Ilyas is alive! What prevented you from seizing him when you met him, binding him, and bringing him to me, when you know that he is my pursuer and my enemy?" They said: "We have told you what prevented us from him, from speaking to him and from seizing him." Ajab said: "Then Ilyas can only be overcome by cunning and deception."

So he chose fifty men from his people, who had strength and courage, and gave them his instructions, ordering them to scheme against him and to take care of him [[From 'Ara'is al-Majalis; in the manuscript: "lahu" (for him).]], and to make him hope that they, and those behind them, had believed in him, so that he would trust them and be deceived by them, and they would then enable them to take hold of him and bring him to their king. They set out until they climbed that mountain in which Ilyas (peace be upon him) was. Then they dispersed in it, calling out to him at the top of their voices and saying: "O prophet of God, show yourself to us and reveal yourself, for we have believed in you and affirmed you. Ajab and all our people have become our kings, and you are secure for yourself, and all the Children of Israel send you greetings and say: 'You have conveyed the message of your Lord to us, and we have come to know what you said, and we have believed in you, and we have answered your call to what you invited us to. So come to us, for you are our prophet and the messenger of our Lord. Remain among us and judge among us, for we submit to what you command us and refrain from what you forbid us, and it is not fitting for you to stay away from us, given our faith and obedience. So rescue us and return to us.'" All of this was from them, deceit and treachery.

When Ilyas heard their words, they affected his heart, he hoped for their faith, and he feared God. He was apprehensive of His anger if he did not show himself and answer them after what he had heard from them. When he resolved to show himself to them, he reconsidered and said: "If only I had called upon God, glorified and exalted is He, and asked Him to make me know what is in their souls and to inform me of the reality of their affair." God, glorified is He, had granted him success and inspired him to pause, to supplicate and to be cautious. So he said: "O God, if they are truthful in what they say, then permit me to show myself to them; but if they are liars, then suffice me against them and strike them with a fire that will burn them."

He had not finished his words before they were pelted with fire from above them, all of them.

He said: News reached Ajab and his people, and he did not refrain from his intent to harm, and he schemed again concerning Ilyas. He appointed another group equal in number to those, stronger than them and more capable of cunning and opinion. They came, dispersing, until they penetrated [into] those mountains, and they began calling out: "O prophet of God, we seek refuge in God and in you from the wrath of God and His assaults. We are not like those who came to you before us. Those were a faction that hypocritically opposed us and went against us, and they came to you to plot against you without our opinion or knowledge. That is because they envied us and envied you, and they went out to you secretly. Had we known about them, we would have killed them and spared you their trouble. Now your Lord has sufficed you against their affair, destroyed them for the evil of their intentions, and taken vengeance on them on your behalf." When Ilyas heard their words, he called upon God with his first supplication, and fire rained down upon them, and they were burned to the last man.

Throughout all this, the king's son was in severe affliction from his illness, as God, glorified and exalted is He, had promised through the tongue of His prophet Ilyas. He would not be given a decree to die, nor would his punishment be lightened for him. When the king heard of the destruction of his companions a second time, his anger increased upon anger, and he wished to go out in search of Ilyas himself, but his son's illness preoccupied him and prevented him. So he sent to Ilyas the believing scribe, who was the scribe of his wife, hoping that Ilyas would feel at ease with him and come down with him. He showed the scribe that he did not intend any harm to Ilyas, and he only showed him this because he had become aware of his faith, and that the king, despite knowing of his faith, had overlooked it because of his trustworthiness, capability, wisdom, soundness of judgment and insight into affairs. When he dispatched him toward Ilyas, he sent with him a group of his companions, and he instructed them, without the scribe, that they should bind Ilyas and bring him to him if he wished to hold back from them; but if he came with the scribe, trusting in him and at ease because of his standing, they were not to frighten or alarm him. Then he showed the scribe repentance and said to him: "It is time for me to repent and take warning. Afflictions have befallen us from the burning of our companions, and the affliction in which my son is. I know that this is due to Ilyas's supplication, and I am not safe from him calling down a curse on all of us who remain, so that we perish by his supplication. So go to him for us and inform him that we have repented and turned back, and that nothing will set us right in our repentance, nor in our seeking the pleasure of our Lord and the removal of our idols, except that Ilyas be among us, commanding us and forbidding us, and informing us of what pleases our Lord."

He said: He ordered his people to abandon the idols, and he said to him: "Inform Ilyas that we have cast off the gods we used to worship, and we have postponed their affair until Ilyas comes down to us, so that he may be the one who burns them and destroys them." That was a trick on the king's part. So the scribe and the group set off until they reached the mountain in which Ilyas was. Then he called out to him, and Ilyas recognised his voice, his soul yearned for him and he felt at ease with him, for he had been longing to meet him.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 37, verses 123–138 (part 2 of 2):

He said: God, glorified and exalted, revealed to Ilyas (Elijah): "Go down to your righteous brother, meet him and renew the covenant with him." So he went down to him, greeted him, shook his hand, and said to him: "What is the news?" The believer said: "This tyrant, the oppressor, and his people have sent me to you." Then he recounted to him what they had said. Then he said to him: "I fear that if I return to him without you with me, he will kill me. So command me to do whatever you wish, and I will do it and go to him. Or, if you wish, I will devote myself to you and remain with you, and leave him. Or, if you wish, I will fight him with you. Or, if you wish, send me to him with whatever you love, and I will convey your message. Or, if you wish, call upon your Lord, that He may grant us a way out and a means of escape from our affair."

He said: God revealed to Ilyas: "Everything that has come to you from them is deceit and falsehood, meant to bring about your defeat. As for Ajab, if his messengers inform him that you have met this man but did not bring him to him, he will suspect him and realise that he has colluded (dahana)[[From ʿArāʾis al-majālis; the manuscript reads: kāhin.]] concerning your matter. He will not feel secure that he will kill him. So go with him, for your going with him will be his excuse and his innocence before Ajab. I will occupy Ajab and his son, and I will multiply the affliction upon his son until he has no concern other than it. Then I will cause him to die in the worst condition. When he dies, return from him and do not stay."

He said: So he went with them until they arrived at him. God intensified the pain upon his son, and death began to choke him. So God occupied Ajab and his companions with that, away from Ilyas, and Ilyas returned safely to his place. When Ajab's son died, and they finished with his affairs, and his grief lessened, he turned his attention to Ilyas and asked about him the secretary who had brought him. He said: "I have no knowledge of him, for the death of your son and the grief over him occupied me from him. I did not think that you had not already secured him." So Ajab turned away from him and left him, because of the grief over his son that was upon him.

When the matter lengthened for Ilyas, he grew weary of staying in the mountains and remaining there, and longed for inhabited places and people. He came down from the mountain and set off until he alighted at the house of a woman from the Children of Israel, who was the mother of Yunus ibn Matta Dhu l-Nun (Jonah). He hid himself with her for six months, while Yunus ibn Matta was then an infant nursing. The mother of Yunus served him with her own hands, comforted him with what she had, and withheld from him no honour she was able to give.

He said: Then Ilyas grew weary of the narrowness of houses, having become accustomed to the spaciousness of the mountains and their trees, so he loved to return to the mountains. He went out and returned to his place. The mother of Yunus grieved at his parting, and his absence distressed her. Not long after, her son died when he was weaned, and her calamity over him was great. So she went out seeking Ilyas, and she continued to climb the mountains and wander through them until she came upon him and found him. She said to him: "I have been struck by a calamity after you, in the death of my son. My calamity over him is great, and my trial in his loss is severe. I have no child other than him. So have mercy on me and call upon your Lord, mighty in majesty, to bring my son back to life and mend my calamity. I have left him laid out and have not buried him, and I have concealed his place." Ilyas said to her: "This is not what I was commanded. I am only a servant under command, acting as my Lord commands me, and He has not commanded me in this." The woman grieved and pleaded humbly, so God inclined Ilyas's heart towards her, and he said to her: "When did your son die?" She said: "Seven days ago."

So Ilyas went with her and they travelled for another seven days until they reached her house, and he found her son Yunus ibn Matta dead for fourteen days. He performed ablution, prayed, and supplicated, and God restored Yunus ibn Matta to life by the supplication of Ilyas. When he lived and sat up, Ilyas sprang up, departed, left him, and returned to the place where he had been.

When the disobedience of his people lengthened, Ilyas was distressed and his affliction overwhelmed him. He said: God, glorified and exalted, revealed to him after seven years, while he was fearful and exhausted: "O Ilyas, what is this sorrow and grief you are in? Am I not your trustee over My revelation, My proof on My earth, and My chosen one from among My creation? So ask Me and I will give you, for I am the One of vast mercy and great bounty." He said:
"Cause me to die, so that I may join my forefathers, for I have grown weary of the Children of Israel, and they have grown weary of me. I have come to hate them for Your sake, and they have come to hate me." God, glorified and exalted, revealed to him: "O Ilyas, this is not the day when I will leave the earth and its people bereft of you. Its stability and its righteousness depend upon you and those like you, though you are few. But ask Me, and I will give you."

Ilyas said: "If You will not cause me to die, O my God, then give me vengeance upon the Children of Israel." God, glorified and exalted, said: "What is it you wish Me to give you, O Ilyas?" He said: "Empower me over the treasuries of heaven for seven years, so that no cloud forms over them except by my supplication, and no rain falls upon them for seven years except by my intercession, for nothing else will humble them." God, glorified and exalted, said: "O Ilyas, I am more merciful to My creation than that, even though they are wrongdoers." He said: "Then six years." He said: "I am more merciful to My creation than that, even though they are wrongdoers." He said: "Then five years." He said: "I am more merciful to My creation than that, even though they are wrongdoers. But I will give you your vengeance for three years: I will place the treasuries of rain in your hand, so no cloud forms over them except by your supplication, and no drop falls upon them except by your intercession." Ilyas said: "Then by what shall I live?" He said: "I will subject to you a kind of bird that will carry your food and drink to you from the fertile lands and from the land that has not been afflicted with drought."

Ilyas said: "I am content."

He said: So God withheld the rain from them until livestock, beasts, insects and trees perished, and the people suffered severe hardship. Ilyas remained in his state, hiding from his people, and his provision was placed for him wherever he was. His people knew of this, so whenever they smelled the scent of bread in a house, they said: "Ilyas has entered this place!" They searched for him, and the people of that house suffered something on account of it.

Ibn Abbas said: The Children of Israel were struck by drought for three years. Ilyas passed by an old woman and said to her: "Do you have any food?" She said: "Yes, some flour and a little oil." He said: So he called for them, invoked blessing upon them, and touched them until they filled her sack with flour and her jars with oil. When the Children of Israel [saw][[The phrase "raʾā Banū Isrāʾīl" is from ʿArāʾis al-majālis; the manuscript reads: raʾawhu.]] this with her, they said: "From where do you have this?" She said: "A man passed by me of such and such a condition." She described him by his description, and they recognised him and said: "That is Ilyas!" They sought him and found him, but he fled from them.

Then he took refuge one night in the house of a woman from the Children of Israel who had a son called al-Yasa' ibn Akhtub, and he had an affliction. She sheltered Ilyas and concealed his matter. He prayed for the boy, who was healed of the affliction he had. Al-Yasa' followed Ilyas, believed in him, affirmed him, and remained with him. He would go wherever Ilyas went. Ilyas had become old and advanced in years, while al-Yasa' was a young man.

Then God, glorified and exalted, revealed to Ilyas: "You have destroyed many creatures who had not disobeyed except the Children of Israel: beasts, animals, birds, insects and trees. You are withholding the rain from the Children of Israel."

They claim, and God knows best, that Ilyas said: "My Lord, let me be the one who prays for them, and brings them relief from the affliction that has befallen them, so that perhaps they will return and abandon what they are upon of worshipping other than You." It was said to him: "Yes."

So Ilyas came to the Children of Israel and said to them: "You have perished from hunger and hardship, and the beasts, animals, birds, insects and trees have perished because of your sins. You are upon falsehood and delusion. If you wish to know that, then go out with your idols [that][[In the manuscript: dhālika.]]. If they answer you, then it is as you say. If they do not do so, you will know that you are upon falsehood, and you will give it up, and I will pray to God and He will relieve you of the affliction you are in."

They said: "You have been just."

So they went out with their idols and called upon them, but they did not answer them, and the affliction they were in was not lifted from them. Then they said to Ilyas, peace be upon him: "O Ilyas, we have perished, so pray to God for us." Ilyas prayed for them, and al-Yasa' was with him, that relief be granted them from what they were in, and that they be given rain. A cloud like a shield appeared over the sea, while they watched. It came towards them and spread across the horizons. Then God, exalted be He, sent down rain upon them, relieved them, and their lands were revived. But when God lifted the harm from them, they broke the covenant, did not desist from their disbelief, did not give up their error, and remained as they had been. When Ilyas saw this, he prayed to his Lord, mighty and majestic, that He would relieve him of them. It was said to him, as they claim: "Look to such and such a day, then go out on it to such and such a place. Whatever comes to you, mount it and do not be frightened."

So Ilyas went out with al-Yasa' ibn Akhtub, until when he was at the place he had been commanded, a horse of fire came and stood before him. Ilyas leapt upon it, and the horse carried him away. Al-Yasa' called out to him: "O Ilyas, what do you command me?" He threw his cloak down to him from the highest air, and that was a sign of his succession to him over the Children of Israel. That was the last time he was seen. God, glorified and exalted, raised Ilyas from among them, cut off from him the pleasure of food and drink, and clothed him with feathers. So he was human and angelic, earthly and heavenly.

God, glorified and exalted, empowered against Ajab the king and his people enemies of theirs, who came upon them from where they did not perceive, until they overtook them. They killed Ajab their king and his wife Azbil in an orchard belonging to Mudhakki (?). Their corpses remained lying in that garden until their flesh decayed and their bones crumbled.

God, glorified and exalted, bestowed prophethood upon al-Yasa' by His grace and sent him as a messenger to the Children of Israel. He revealed to him and strengthened him with the same things with which He had strengthened His servant Ilyas. The Children of Israel believed in him, honoured him, and submitted to his command. God's judgment among them remained in force until al-Yasa' parted from them.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Jadawi told us, from Damrah, from al-Sudi ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad, who said: Ilyas and al-Khadir, peace be upon them both, fast the month of Ramadan in Jerusalem, and they attend the pilgrimage season every year.

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me, saying: Ibn Majah told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ayyub told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad told us, saying: Yasar told us, saying: Bishr ibn Mansur told us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Basri told me, saying: al-Ala' al-Bajali told me, from Zayd, the client of Awn al-Tufawi, from a man from the people of Ascalon who used to walk in Jordan around midday. He saw a man and said: "O servant of God, who are you?" He did not speak to me. I said: "O servant of God, who are you?" He said: "I am Ilyas." A trembling came over me, and I said: "Pray to God to lift from me what I feel, until I understand your speech and comprehend it from you." He prayed for me with eight supplications: "O Most Kind, O Most Merciful, O Most Compassionate, O Bestower, O Living, O Self-Subsisting," and two supplications in Syriac which I did not understand.

He said: God lifted from me what I had been feeling. He placed his palm between my shoulders, and I found its coolness between my hands. He said:
I said to him: "Is revelation still sent to you today?" He said: "Since God, glorified and exalted, sent Muhammad as a messenger, He does not reveal to me." I said to him: "How many prophets are alive today?" He said: "Four: two on the earth and two in heaven. In heaven are Jesus and Idris, and on the earth are Ilyas and al-Khadir." I said: "How many abdal (substitutes, a class of saints) are there?" He said: "Sixty men: fifty of them from the Arish of Egypt to the bank of the Euphrates, a man at al-Masisiyya, two men at Ascalon, and seven in the rest of the lands. Whenever God takes one away, He brings another. Through them the people are protected, and through them rain falls." I said: "Where is al-Khadir?" He said: "In the islands of the sea." I said: "Do you meet him?" He said: "Yes." I said: "Where?" He said: "At the pilgrimage season." I said: "What passes between you two?" He said: "He takes from my hair, and I take from his hair."

He said: That was when war was taking place between Marwan ibn al-Hakam and the people of Syria. I said: "What do you say about Marwan ibn al-Hakam?" He said: "What do you want with him? He is a tyrant, arrogant towards God, glorified and exalted: the killer, the killed, and the witness are in the Fire." He said: I said: "I have participated and did not thrust with a spear, nor shoot with an arrow, nor strike with a sword. I ask God, mighty and majestic, forgiveness for that position, and I will never return to the like of it."

He said: "You have done well. Be like this."

He said: While he and I were sitting, two loaves were placed before him, whiter than snow. He and I ate one loaf and part of another. Then he lifted them, and I did not see anyone place them or anyone lift them. He had a she-camel grazing in the valley of the Jordan. He raised his head towards her but did not call her, and she came and knelt before him, and he mounted her. I said: "I wish to accompany you." He said: "You are not able to keep my company." I said: "I am alone; I have no wife and no dependants." He said:
"Marry, and beware of the four kinds of women: beware of the rebellious (nashiz), the one who seeks khul' (divorce by ransom), the one who invokes mutual curses (mula'ana), and the one who is mubarriza[[In ʿArāʾis al-majālis: al-mubarzza.]], and marry whichever women you wish." He said: I said: "I love to meet you." He said: "When you see me, you have met me." Then he said: "I intend to seclude myself in retreat in Jerusalem during the blessed month of God, Ramadan."[103]

He said: Then a tree came between me and him. By God, I do not know how he departed. That is the saying of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿And indeed Ilyas was among the messengers. When he said to his people: "Will you not be mindful of God? Will you call upon Ba'l and forsake the best of creators, God, your Lord and the Lord of your earliest forefathers?"﴾ Ba'l was the name of an idol they worshipped, and for that reason their city was named Baalbek. Mujahid, Ikrimah and al-Sudi said: Ba'l means "lord" in the dialect of the people of Yemen. This is the transmission of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abbas said: I asked a Bedouin who said to another: "Whose ba'l is this she-camel?" meaning her owner. Al-Farra' said: it is in the dialect of Hudhayl.

﴿And you forsake the best of creators﴾, so that you do not worship Him. ﴿God, your Lord and the Lord of your earliest forefathers.﴾ Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf and Ya'qub recited (Allah rabbakum wa-rabba) with the ha' and the two bas in the accusative as a substitution (badal), which is the choice of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim and the transmission of Hafs from Asim. The others recited them in the nominative as a new sentence (isti'naf).

﴿But they denied him, so they will surely be brought to punishment and to the Fire, except the sincere servants of God among his people, for they will be saved from the Fire. And We left for him among later generations: ﴿Peace be upon Ilyasin﴾.﴾ Ibn Muhays and Shayba recited "Salam ala Ilyasin" with continuous connection (mawsulan).

Ibn Amir, Nafi' and Ya'qub recited ﴿Al Yasin﴾ with the long vowel (mad). The rest recited ﴿Il Yasin﴾ with a separated alif and short vowel. Whoever recites ﴿Al Yasin﴾ with the mad, is said by some to have meant "the family of Muhammad." It was also said that he meant Ilyas, and this fits the context of the verse better. Whoever recites ﴿Il Yasin﴾ — it was said that it is a dialect form of Ilyas, like Isma'il and Isma'in, and Mika'il and Mika'in. Al-Farra' said: it is a plural, meaning Ilyas and his followers among the believers, like their saying "al-Ash'aruna" and "al-Makiyyuna." Al-Kisa'i said: the Arabs make the singular dual or plural, as in the saying of the poet:

"Qadani min nasr al-Khubaybayni qadi"

and it is actually Abu Khubayb, Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr.

Another poet said:

"Jaza'ani al-Zahdamani jaza'a su'in"

and it is actually Zahdam.

In the reading of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) it is: ﴿And indeed Idris was among the messengers, and peace be upon Idrasin﴾.

﴿Thus do We reward the good-doers. Indeed he was of Our believing servants. And indeed Lut was among the messengers, when We saved him and his family, all of them, except an old woman who was among those who remained behind. Then We destroyed the others. And indeed you pass by them in the morning﴾ — i.e., by their traces and their dwellings — ﴿and at night.﴾ — the time of morning — "and at night" also you pass by. Here the speech is complete. Then He said: ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾ — so that you may take heed?

The Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 37, verses 123–138 (part 1 of 2):

And indeed Ilyas (Elias) was among the messengers (﴿وَإِنَّ إِلْيَاسَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾). Abu Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim ibn al-Mu'hil informed us, saying: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm related to us, saying: Bakkar ibn Qutayba related to us, saying: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi related to us, saying: Qays ibn Abi Ishaq related to us, from Ubayya ibn Rabi'a, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Ilyas is Idris, and Israel is Ya'qub." Ikrima also held this view, and he said: "It is in the codex of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud): ﴿وَإِنَّ إِدْرِيسَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾." Abdullah and Ikrima alone held this opinion.

Others said: he was a prophet from among the prophets of the Children of Israel. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He was the paternal cousin of al-Yasa' (Elisha)." Ibn Ishaq said: "He is Ilyas ibn Yasin ibn al-'Izar ibn Harun ibn 'Imran." Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar and the scholars of narratives also said: When God, glorified is He, took the soul of the prophet Hizqil (Ezekiel), the offences among the Children of Israel grew great, corruption and polytheism appeared among them, they forgot the covenant of God, they set up idols and worshipped them besides God. So God sent to them Ilyas (peace be upon him) as a prophet. The prophets from the Children of Israel after Musa (peace be upon him) had been following the Torah and were sent to them to renew what they had forgotten of it. The Children of Israel at that time were scattered in the land of al-Sham, and there were many kings among them. The reason for this was that Yusha' ibn Nun, when he conquered the land of al-Sham after Musa and took possession of it, settled the Children of Israel there and divided it among them. He assigned to one tribe of them Ba'labakk and its surroundings, and they were the tribe of Ilyas, and Ilyas was from among them. So God sent him to them as a prophet. At that time over them was a king called [Ajab] [[The author vocalised it in 'Ara'is al-Majalis (pp. 192–199) as Lajab.]], who had gone astray and led his people astray, and compelled them to worship idols. He and his people worshipped an idol called Ba'l, which was twenty cubits tall and had four faces.

He said: Ilyas began to call them to God, glorified is He, but they, in all of this, would not listen to him at all, except for the king of Ba'labakk, who believed in him and affirmed him. Ilyas would support his affair, strengthen him and guide him. Ajab had a wife called Azbil [[The author vocalised it in the same source as Arbil.]], and he would appoint her over his subjects whenever he was absent from them on a raid or otherwise. She would appear before people as her husband did, ride as he rode, and sit in the seat of judgment, judging between people. She was a killer of prophets.

He said: She had a scribe, a wise man of faith who concealed his faith from her. This scribe had rescued from her hand three hundred prophets whom she intended to kill, each one of them, when they were sent, in addition to those before them, whose numbers were many. She was unchaste by nature, and there was no one on the face of the earth more shameless than her. Moreover, she had married seven kings of the Children of Israel and killed them all by assassination. She lived so long that it was said she bore seventy children.

He said: Ajab had a neighbour from the Children of Israel, a righteous man called Mazdaki, who had a garden from which he lived, and he devoted himself to cultivating and beautifying it. The garden was beside the palace of the king and his wife, and they would look out over that garden, taking their leisure in it, eating, drinking and resting there. Ajab, despite all this, treated him well, but his wife Azbil envied him for that garden, and she schemed to seize it from him when she heard people frequently mentioning the garden and marvelling at its beauty, saying: "How fitting it would be for this garden to belong to the people of this palace!" and marvelling at the king and his wife, asking how they had not taken it from its owner. The wife of the king kept scheming against the righteous servant Mazdaki, hoping to kill him and take his garden, while the king kept forbidding her from that, so she could find no way against him.

Then it happened that the king set out on a distant journey and his absence was prolonged. His wife Azbil seized the opportunity to plot against Mazdaki, while he was heedless of what she intended for him, devoted to the worship of his Lord and to improving his livelihood. Azbil gathered a group of people and ordered them to testify against Mazdaki that he had reviled her husband Ajab. They agreed to her request to bear witness against him.

Among the judgments of that time was that whoever reviled the king was to be killed, once the proof had been established against him. So she summoned Mazdaki and said to him: "It has reached me that you insulted the king and disparaged him." Mazdaki denied this. The woman said: "There are witnesses against you." She produced the witnesses, who testified falsely against him in the presence of the people, so she ordered Mazdaki to be killed. He was killed and she seized his garden by force. Thus God became angry with them for killing the righteous servant.

When the king returned from his journey, she told him the news. He said to her: "You have not done right, nor have you been successful. I do not think we will prosper after this, ever. We were rich without his garden; we used to take our leisure in it. He has been our neighbour and under our protection for a long time, so we treated him well and withheld harm from him, because of his due right over us. You have ended his neighbourliness with the worst treatment. Nothing has moved you to this audacity against him except your foolishness, your bad judgment and your lack of reflection on the consequences." She said: "I was only angry on your behalf, and I judged by your judgment." He said to her: "Does your forbearance not encompass it, and does your great station not urge you to pardon one man, so that you protect his neighbourhood?" She said: "What has happened has happened."

God, exalted is He, then sent Ilyas (peace be upon him) to Ajab the king and his people, and commanded him to inform them that God, glorified is He, had become angry for His friend when they killed him among them unjustly, and that He had sworn by Himself that if they two did not repent of their deed and did not return the garden to the heirs of Mazdaki, He would destroy them both—meaning Ajab and his wife—inside the garden in the worst condition, by shedding their blood, then leave them as two corpses lying there until their bones were stripped of their flesh, and they would enjoy it only briefly.

He said: Ilyas came and informed him of what God, exalted is He, had revealed to him concerning him, his wife and the garden. When the king heard that, his anger against him intensified, and then he said to him: "O Ilyas, by God, I see nothing in what you call to except falsehood. By God, I see that so-and-so and so-and-so (he named kings among them) who worshipped idols were only in the same state as we are, eating, drinking and enjoying themselves, possessing without diminishing their worldly life or their affair, which you claim is false. We see no superiority for you over us or over them."

He said: The king resolved to torture Ilyas and kill him. When Ilyas heard that and sensed the evil, he withdrew from him and left, and went to the highest mountain peaks. The king returned to the worship of Ba'l. Ilyas climbed the most difficult and loftiest mountain, and entered a cave in it. It is said that he remained there for seven years, homeless and fleeing, fearful, taking refuge in ravines and caves, eating from the plants of the earth and the fruit of trees. They, in their search for him, had placed watchers upon him, awaiting news of him and striving to seize him, while God, glorified and exalted is He, concealed him and warded off harm from him. When seven years had passed, God, exalted is He, permitted his appearance before them and the healing of his anger against them. God, glorified is He, afflicted a son of Ajab—he was his dearest child, the most precious to him, and the most like him—with an illness, so that he became gravely ill until he despaired of him. So he called upon his idol Ba'l—they had been seduced by Ba'l and magnified him, to the point that they had appointed four hundred attendants for him and assigned them to him as his trustees. The devil would enter the belly of the idol and speak with all kinds of speech, while the four hundred listened attentively to what the devil said, and the devil would whisper to them a law of misguidance, which they would write down for the people, and they would act upon it. They called them "the prophets."

When the son of the king's illness intensified, the king asked them to intercede for him with Ba'l and seek for his son, from him, recovery and well-being. They called upon him [[From 'Ara'is al-Majalis; in the manuscript: "fa-da'awhum" (they called them).]], but he did not respond to them. God, by His power, prevented the devil from entering the idol, so he could neither enter its belly nor speak. They strove greatly in supplicating to him, but he only grew more lifeless. When this went on too long for them, they said to Ajab: "In the land of al-Sham there are other gods, equal in greatness to your god. Send the prophets to them so that they may intercede for you with them, perhaps they will intercede for you with your god Ba'l, for he is angry with you. Had he not been angry with you, he would have answered you and healed your son."

Ajab said: "And for what reason is he angry with me, when I have obeyed him and sought his pleasure since I was born, never once displeasing him?" They said: "For the reason that you did not kill Ilyas; you neglected him until he escaped unharmed, and he disbelieves in your god and worships another. That is what has made him angry with you." Ajab said: "And how can I kill Ilyas today, when I am preoccupied from seeking him by my son's pain? Ilyas has no place where he may be sought or known, so that if my son were healed, I would devote myself to seeking him, and I would have no concern or occupation other than him, until I seize him and kill him, and thus relieve my god of him and please him."

He said: Then he sent his four hundred prophets to intercede with the gods [[From 'Ara'is al-Majalis; in the manuscript: "al-Hawn".]] that were in al-Sham, and to ask them to intercede with the idol of the king so that it would heal his son. They set out until, when they were opposite the mountain in which Ilyas was, God, glorified is He, revealed to Ilyas that he should descend from the mountain, confront them, stop them and speak to them, and He said to him: "Do not fear, for I will turn their evil away from you and cast terror into their hearts." So Ilyas came down from the mountain, and when he met them he stopped them. When they stood still, he said to them: "God, glorified is He, has sent me to you and to those behind you. So listen, O people, to the message of your Lord, that you may convey it to your master. Return to him and say to him: 'God says to you: Do you not know, O Ajab, that I am God, there is no god but I (﴿إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنَا﴾), the God of the Children of Israel, who created them, provided for them, gave them life and caused them to die? Has your ignorance and lack of knowledge led you to associate others with Me, and to seek healing for your son from other than Me, from those who possess nothing for themselves except what I will? I have sworn by My name that I will indeed enrage you concerning your son, and I will cause him to die at this very moment, until you know that no one possesses anything for him besides Me.'"

When he had said this to them, they returned, filled with terror of him. When they came to the king, they told him that and informed him that Ilyas had come down upon them. He was a tall, lean man, emaciated, dried out, with his hair fallen out and his skin peeling. He wore a garment of hair and a cloak which he had fastened on his chest with thorns. "He stopped us, and when he came near us, awe and terror were cast into our hearts, our tongues were cut off, and we, in this great number, while he was alone, could not speak to him, answer him, or even fill our eyes with him, until we returned to you." They related to him the words of Ilyas. Ajab said: "Life is of no benefit as long as Ilyas is alive! What prevented you from seizing him when you met him, binding him, and bringing him to me, when you know that he is my pursuer and my enemy?" They said: "We have told you what prevented us from him, from speaking to him and from seizing him." Ajab said: "Then Ilyas can only be overcome by cunning and deception."

So he chose fifty men from his people, who had strength and courage, and gave them his instructions, ordering them to scheme against him and to take care of him [[From 'Ara'is al-Majalis; in the manuscript: "lahu" (for him).]], and to make him hope that they, and those behind them, had believed in him, so that he would trust them and be deceived by them, and they would then enable them to take hold of him and bring him to their king. They set out until they climbed that mountain in which Ilyas (peace be upon him) was. Then they dispersed in it, calling out to him at the top of their voices and saying: "O prophet of God, show yourself to us and reveal yourself, for we have believed in you and affirmed you. Ajab and all our people have become our kings, and you are secure for yourself, and all the Children of Israel send you greetings and say: 'You have conveyed the message of your Lord to us, and we have come to know what you said, and we have believed in you, and we have answered your call to what you invited us to. So come to us, for you are our prophet and the messenger of our Lord. Remain among us and judge among us, for we submit to what you command us and refrain from what you forbid us, and it is not fitting for you to stay away from us, given our faith and obedience. So rescue us and return to us.'" All of this was from them, deceit and treachery.

When Ilyas heard their words, they affected his heart, he hoped for their faith, and he feared God. He was apprehensive of His anger if he did not show himself and answer them after what he had heard from them. When he resolved to show himself to them, he reconsidered and said: "If only I had called upon God, glorified and exalted is He, and asked Him to make me know what is in their souls and to inform me of the reality of their affair." God, glorified is He, had granted him success and inspired him to pause, to supplicate and to be cautious. So he said: "O God, if they are truthful in what they say, then permit me to show myself to them; but if they are liars, then suffice me against them and strike them with a fire that will burn them."

He had not finished his words before they were pelted with fire from above them, all of them.

He said: News reached Ajab and his people, and he did not refrain from his intent to harm, and he schemed again concerning Ilyas. He appointed another group equal in number to those, stronger than them and more capable of cunning and opinion. They came, dispersing, until they penetrated [into] those mountains, and they began calling out: "O prophet of God, we seek refuge in God and in you from the wrath of God and His assaults. We are not like those who came to you before us. Those were a faction that hypocritically opposed us and went against us, and they came to you to plot against you without our opinion or knowledge. That is because they envied us and envied you, and they went out to you secretly. Had we known about them, we would have killed them and spared you their trouble. Now your Lord has sufficed you against their affair, destroyed them for the evil of their intentions, and taken vengeance on them on your behalf." When Ilyas heard their words, he called upon God with his first supplication, and fire rained down upon them, and they were burned to the last man.

Throughout all this, the king's son was in severe affliction from his illness, as God, glorified and exalted is He, had promised through the tongue of His prophet Ilyas. He would not be given a decree to die, nor would his punishment be lightened for him. When the king heard of the destruction of his companions a second time, his anger increased upon anger, and he wished to go out in search of Ilyas himself, but his son's illness preoccupied him and prevented him. So he sent to Ilyas the believing scribe, who was the scribe of his wife, hoping that Ilyas would feel at ease with him and come down with him. He showed the scribe that he did not intend any harm to Ilyas, and he only showed him this because he had become aware of his faith, and that the king, despite knowing of his faith, had overlooked it because of his trustworthiness, capability, wisdom, soundness of judgment and insight into affairs. When he dispatched him toward Ilyas, he sent with him a group of his companions, and he instructed them, without the scribe, that they should bind Ilyas and bring him to him if he wished to hold back from them; but if he came with the scribe, trusting in him and at ease because of his standing, they were not to frighten or alarm him. Then he showed the scribe repentance and said to him: "It is time for me to repent and take warning. Afflictions have befallen us from the burning of our companions, and the affliction in which my son is. I know that this is due to Ilyas's supplication, and I am not safe from him calling down a curse on all of us who remain, so that we perish by his supplication. So go to him for us and inform him that we have repented and turned back, and that nothing will set us right in our repentance, nor in our seeking the pleasure of our Lord and the removal of our idols, except that Ilyas be among us, commanding us and forbidding us, and informing us of what pleases our Lord."

He said: He ordered his people to abandon the idols, and he said to him: "Inform Ilyas that we have cast off the gods we used to worship, and we have postponed their affair until Ilyas comes down to us, so that he may be the one who burns them and destroys them." That was a trick on the king's part. So the scribe and the group set off until they reached the mountain in which Ilyas was. Then he called out to him, and Ilyas recognised his voice, his soul yearned for him and he felt at ease with him, for he had been longing to meet him.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 37, verses 123–138 (part 2 of 2):

He said: God, glorified and exalted, revealed to Ilyas (Elijah): "Go down to your righteous brother, meet him and renew the covenant with him." So he went down to him, greeted him, shook his hand, and said to him: "What is the news?" The believer said: "This tyrant, the oppressor, and his people have sent me to you." Then he recounted to him what they had said. Then he said to him: "I fear that if I return to him without you with me, he will kill me. So command me to do whatever you wish, and I will do it and go to him. Or, if you wish, I will devote myself to you and remain with you, and leave him. Or, if you wish, I will fight him with you. Or, if you wish, send me to him with whatever you love, and I will convey your message. Or, if you wish, call upon your Lord, that He may grant us a way out and a means of escape from our affair."

He said: God revealed to Ilyas: "Everything that has come to you from them is deceit and falsehood, meant to bring about your defeat. As for Ajab, if his messengers inform him that you have met this man but did not bring him to him, he will suspect him and realise that he has colluded (dahana)[[From ʿArāʾis al-majālis; the manuscript reads: kāhin.]] concerning your matter. He will not feel secure that he will kill him. So go with him, for your going with him will be his excuse and his innocence before Ajab. I will occupy Ajab and his son, and I will multiply the affliction upon his son until he has no concern other than it. Then I will cause him to die in the worst condition. When he dies, return from him and do not stay."

He said: So he went with them until they arrived at him. God intensified the pain upon his son, and death began to choke him. So God occupied Ajab and his companions with that, away from Ilyas, and Ilyas returned safely to his place. When Ajab's son died, and they finished with his affairs, and his grief lessened, he turned his attention to Ilyas and asked about him the secretary who had brought him. He said: "I have no knowledge of him, for the death of your son and the grief over him occupied me from him. I did not think that you had not already secured him." So Ajab turned away from him and left him, because of the grief over his son that was upon him.

When the matter lengthened for Ilyas, he grew weary of staying in the mountains and remaining there, and longed for inhabited places and people. He came down from the mountain and set off until he alighted at the house of a woman from the Children of Israel, who was the mother of Yunus ibn Matta Dhu l-Nun (Jonah). He hid himself with her for six months, while Yunus ibn Matta was then an infant nursing. The mother of Yunus served him with her own hands, comforted him with what she had, and withheld from him no honour she was able to give.

He said: Then Ilyas grew weary of the narrowness of houses, having become accustomed to the spaciousness of the mountains and their trees, so he loved to return to the mountains. He went out and returned to his place. The mother of Yunus grieved at his parting, and his absence distressed her. Not long after, her son died when he was weaned, and her calamity over him was great. So she went out seeking Ilyas, and she continued to climb the mountains and wander through them until she came upon him and found him. She said to him: "I have been struck by a calamity after you, in the death of my son. My calamity over him is great, and my trial in his loss is severe. I have no child other than him. So have mercy on me and call upon your Lord, mighty in majesty, to bring my son back to life and mend my calamity. I have left him laid out and have not buried him, and I have concealed his place." Ilyas said to her: "This is not what I was commanded. I am only a servant under command, acting as my Lord commands me, and He has not commanded me in this." The woman grieved and pleaded humbly, so God inclined Ilyas's heart towards her, and he said to her: "When did your son die?" She said: "Seven days ago."

So Ilyas went with her and they travelled for another seven days until they reached her house, and he found her son Yunus ibn Matta dead for fourteen days. He performed ablution, prayed, and supplicated, and God restored Yunus ibn Matta to life by the supplication of Ilyas. When he lived and sat up, Ilyas sprang up, departed, left him, and returned to the place where he had been.

When the disobedience of his people lengthened, Ilyas was distressed and his affliction overwhelmed him. He said: God, glorified and exalted, revealed to him after seven years, while he was fearful and exhausted: "O Ilyas, what is this sorrow and grief you are in? Am I not your trustee over My revelation, My proof on My earth, and My chosen one from among My creation? So ask Me and I will give you, for I am the One of vast mercy and great bounty." He said:
"Cause me to die, so that I may join my forefathers, for I have grown weary of the Children of Israel, and they have grown weary of me. I have come to hate them for Your sake, and they have come to hate me." God, glorified and exalted, revealed to him: "O Ilyas, this is not the day when I will leave the earth and its people bereft of you. Its stability and its righteousness depend upon you and those like you, though you are few. But ask Me, and I will give you."

Ilyas said: "If You will not cause me to die, O my God, then give me vengeance upon the Children of Israel." God, glorified and exalted, said: "What is it you wish Me to give you, O Ilyas?" He said: "Empower me over the treasuries of heaven for seven years, so that no cloud forms over them except by my supplication, and no rain falls upon them for seven years except by my intercession, for nothing else will humble them." God, glorified and exalted, said: "O Ilyas, I am more merciful to My creation than that, even though they are wrongdoers." He said: "Then six years." He said: "I am more merciful to My creation than that, even though they are wrongdoers." He said: "Then five years." He said: "I am more merciful to My creation than that, even though they are wrongdoers. But I will give you your vengeance for three years: I will place the treasuries of rain in your hand, so no cloud forms over them except by your supplication, and no drop falls upon them except by your intercession." Ilyas said: "Then by what shall I live?" He said: "I will subject to you a kind of bird that will carry your food and drink to you from the fertile lands and from the land that has not been afflicted with drought."

Ilyas said: "I am content."

He said: So God withheld the rain from them until livestock, beasts, insects and trees perished, and the people suffered severe hardship. Ilyas remained in his state, hiding from his people, and his provision was placed for him wherever he was. His people knew of this, so whenever they smelled the scent of bread in a house, they said: "Ilyas has entered this place!" They searched for him, and the people of that house suffered something on account of it.

Ibn Abbas said: The Children of Israel were struck by drought for three years. Ilyas passed by an old woman and said to her: "Do you have any food?" She said: "Yes, some flour and a little oil." He said: So he called for them, invoked blessing upon them, and touched them until they filled her sack with flour and her jars with oil. When the Children of Israel [saw][[The phrase "raʾā Banū Isrāʾīl" is from ʿArāʾis al-majālis; the manuscript reads: raʾawhu.]] this with her, they said: "From where do you have this?" She said: "A man passed by me of such and such a condition." She described him by his description, and they recognised him and said: "That is Ilyas!" They sought him and found him, but he fled from them.

Then he took refuge one night in the house of a woman from the Children of Israel who had a son called al-Yasa' ibn Akhtub, and he had an affliction. She sheltered Ilyas and concealed his matter. He prayed for the boy, who was healed of the affliction he had. Al-Yasa' followed Ilyas, believed in him, affirmed him, and remained with him. He would go wherever Ilyas went. Ilyas had become old and advanced in years, while al-Yasa' was a young man.

Then God, glorified and exalted, revealed to Ilyas: "You have destroyed many creatures who had not disobeyed except the Children of Israel: beasts, animals, birds, insects and trees. You are withholding the rain from the Children of Israel."

They claim, and God knows best, that Ilyas said: "My Lord, let me be the one who prays for them, and brings them relief from the affliction that has befallen them, so that perhaps they will return and abandon what they are upon of worshipping other than You." It was said to him: "Yes."

So Ilyas came to the Children of Israel and said to them: "You have perished from hunger and hardship, and the beasts, animals, birds, insects and trees have perished because of your sins. You are upon falsehood and delusion. If you wish to know that, then go out with your idols [that][[In the manuscript: dhālika.]]. If they answer you, then it is as you say. If they do not do so, you will know that you are upon falsehood, and you will give it up, and I will pray to God and He will relieve you of the affliction you are in."

They said: "You have been just."

So they went out with their idols and called upon them, but they did not answer them, and the affliction they were in was not lifted from them. Then they said to Ilyas, peace be upon him: "O Ilyas, we have perished, so pray to God for us." Ilyas prayed for them, and al-Yasa' was with him, that relief be granted them from what they were in, and that they be given rain. A cloud like a shield appeared over the sea, while they watched. It came towards them and spread across the horizons. Then God, exalted be He, sent down rain upon them, relieved them, and their lands were revived. But when God lifted the harm from them, they broke the covenant, did not desist from their disbelief, did not give up their error, and remained as they had been. When Ilyas saw this, he prayed to his Lord, mighty and majestic, that He would relieve him of them. It was said to him, as they claim: "Look to such and such a day, then go out on it to such and such a place. Whatever comes to you, mount it and do not be frightened."

So Ilyas went out with al-Yasa' ibn Akhtub, until when he was at the place he had been commanded, a horse of fire came and stood before him. Ilyas leapt upon it, and the horse carried him away. Al-Yasa' called out to him: "O Ilyas, what do you command me?" He threw his cloak down to him from the highest air, and that was a sign of his succession to him over the Children of Israel. That was the last time he was seen. God, glorified and exalted, raised Ilyas from among them, cut off from him the pleasure of food and drink, and clothed him with feathers. So he was human and angelic, earthly and heavenly.

God, glorified and exalted, empowered against Ajab the king and his people enemies of theirs, who came upon them from where they did not perceive, until they overtook them. They killed Ajab their king and his wife Azbil in an orchard belonging to Mudhakki (?). Their corpses remained lying in that garden until their flesh decayed and their bones crumbled.

God, glorified and exalted, bestowed prophethood upon al-Yasa' by His grace and sent him as a messenger to the Children of Israel. He revealed to him and strengthened him with the same things with which He had strengthened His servant Ilyas. The Children of Israel believed in him, honoured him, and submitted to his command. God's judgment among them remained in force until al-Yasa' parted from them.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Jadawi told us, from Damrah, from al-Sudi ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad, who said: Ilyas and al-Khadir, peace be upon them both, fast the month of Ramadan in Jerusalem, and they attend the pilgrimage season every year.

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me, saying: Ibn Majah told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ayyub told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad told us, saying: Yasar told us, saying: Bishr ibn Mansur told us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Basri told me, saying: al-Ala' al-Bajali told me, from Zayd, the client of Awn al-Tufawi, from a man from the people of Ascalon who used to walk in Jordan around midday. He saw a man and said: "O servant of God, who are you?" He did not speak to me. I said: "O servant of God, who are you?" He said: "I am Ilyas." A trembling came over me, and I said: "Pray to God to lift from me what I feel, until I understand your speech and comprehend it from you." He prayed for me with eight supplications: "O Most Kind, O Most Merciful, O Most Compassionate, O Bestower, O Living, O Self-Subsisting," and two supplications in Syriac which I did not understand.

He said: God lifted from me what I had been feeling. He placed his palm between my shoulders, and I found its coolness between my hands. He said:
I said to him: "Is revelation still sent to you today?" He said: "Since God, glorified and exalted, sent Muhammad as a messenger, He does not reveal to me." I said to him: "How many prophets are alive today?" He said: "Four: two on the earth and two in heaven. In heaven are Jesus and Idris, and on the earth are Ilyas and al-Khadir." I said: "How many abdal (substitutes, a class of saints) are there?" He said: "Sixty men: fifty of them from the Arish of Egypt to the bank of the Euphrates, a man at al-Masisiyya, two men at Ascalon, and seven in the rest of the lands. Whenever God takes one away, He brings another. Through them the people are protected, and through them rain falls." I said: "Where is al-Khadir?" He said: "In the islands of the sea." I said: "Do you meet him?" He said: "Yes." I said: "Where?" He said: "At the pilgrimage season." I said: "What passes between you two?" He said: "He takes from my hair, and I take from his hair."

He said: That was when war was taking place between Marwan ibn al-Hakam and the people of Syria. I said: "What do you say about Marwan ibn al-Hakam?" He said: "What do you want with him? He is a tyrant, arrogant towards God, glorified and exalted: the killer, the killed, and the witness are in the Fire." He said: I said: "I have participated and did not thrust with a spear, nor shoot with an arrow, nor strike with a sword. I ask God, mighty and majestic, forgiveness for that position, and I will never return to the like of it."

He said: "You have done well. Be like this."

He said: While he and I were sitting, two loaves were placed before him, whiter than snow. He and I ate one loaf and part of another. Then he lifted them, and I did not see anyone place them or anyone lift them. He had a she-camel grazing in the valley of the Jordan. He raised his head towards her but did not call her, and she came and knelt before him, and he mounted her. I said: "I wish to accompany you." He said: "You are not able to keep my company." I said: "I am alone; I have no wife and no dependants." He said:
"Marry, and beware of the four kinds of women: beware of the rebellious (nashiz), the one who seeks khul' (divorce by ransom), the one who invokes mutual curses (mula'ana), and the one who is mubarriza[[In ʿArāʾis al-majālis: al-mubarzza.]], and marry whichever women you wish." He said: I said: "I love to meet you." He said: "When you see me, you have met me." Then he said: "I intend to seclude myself in retreat in Jerusalem during the blessed month of God, Ramadan."[103]

He said: Then a tree came between me and him. By God, I do not know how he departed. That is the saying of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿And indeed Ilyas was among the messengers. When he said to his people: "Will you not be mindful of God? Will you call upon Ba'l and forsake the best of creators, God, your Lord and the Lord of your earliest forefathers?"﴾ Ba'l was the name of an idol they worshipped, and for that reason their city was named Baalbek. Mujahid, Ikrimah and al-Sudi said: Ba'l means "lord" in the dialect of the people of Yemen. This is the transmission of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abbas said: I asked a Bedouin who said to another: "Whose ba'l is this she-camel?" meaning her owner. Al-Farra' said: it is in the dialect of Hudhayl.

﴿And you forsake the best of creators﴾, so that you do not worship Him. ﴿God, your Lord and the Lord of your earliest forefathers.﴾ Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf and Ya'qub recited (Allah rabbakum wa-rabba) with the ha' and the two bas in the accusative as a substitution (badal), which is the choice of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim and the transmission of Hafs from Asim. The others recited them in the nominative as a new sentence (isti'naf).

﴿But they denied him, so they will surely be brought to punishment and to the Fire, except the sincere servants of God among his people, for they will be saved from the Fire. And We left for him among later generations: ﴿Peace be upon Ilyasin﴾.﴾ Ibn Muhays and Shayba recited "Salam ala Ilyasin" with continuous connection (mawsulan).

Ibn Amir, Nafi' and Ya'qub recited ﴿Al Yasin﴾ with the long vowel (mad). The rest recited ﴿Il Yasin﴾ with a separated alif and short vowel. Whoever recites ﴿Al Yasin﴾ with the mad, is said by some to have meant "the family of Muhammad." It was also said that he meant Ilyas, and this fits the context of the verse better. Whoever recites ﴿Il Yasin﴾ — it was said that it is a dialect form of Ilyas, like Isma'il and Isma'in, and Mika'il and Mika'in. Al-Farra' said: it is a plural, meaning Ilyas and his followers among the believers, like their saying "al-Ash'aruna" and "al-Makiyyuna." Al-Kisa'i said: the Arabs make the singular dual or plural, as in the saying of the poet:

"Qadani min nasr al-Khubaybayni qadi"

and it is actually Abu Khubayb, Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr.

Another poet said:

"Jaza'ani al-Zahdamani jaza'a su'in"

and it is actually Zahdam.

In the reading of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) it is: ﴿And indeed Idris was among the messengers, and peace be upon Idrasin﴾.

﴿Thus do We reward the good-doers. Indeed he was of Our believing servants. And indeed Lut was among the messengers, when We saved him and his family, all of them, except an old woman who was among those who remained behind. Then We destroyed the others. And indeed you pass by them in the morning﴾ — i.e., by their traces and their dwellings — ﴿and at night.﴾ — the time of morning — "and at night" also you pass by. Here the speech is complete. Then He said: ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾ — so that you may take heed?

And indeed Jonah was among the messengers. ﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾ (Ibn Abbas and Wahb said: Jonah had promised his people the punishment. When the punishment was delayed from them, he left them in anger and set out for the sea, boarded a ship, and the ship was held fast. The sailors said: "There is a runaway slave here from his master. This is the custom of a ship: if there is a runaway aboard, it does not sail." So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah. They said: "Shall we not throw him into the water?" They cast lots a second and a third time, and the lot fell on Jonah. He said: "I am the runaway," and he threw himself into the water. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿and he drew lots﴾: he cast lots. Al-musahama is the casting of arrows by way of lottery.) ﴿So he was among the losers﴾: those defeated by lot, those cast down, those overcome.

﴿Then the great fish swallowed him﴾: it swallowed him, and Allah revealed to him that He had made his belly a prison and had not made him its food. ﴿And he was blameworthy﴾: at fault, having done what deserved blame.

﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify Allah﴾: those who declare Allah free of imperfection and remember Him before that, in times of ease. Ibn Abbas said: those who pray. Muqatil said: those who are righteous and obedient before disobedience. Wahb said: those who worship. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means his words, ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers﴾ (Qur'an 21:87). Al-Hasan said: he had no prayer in the belly of the fish, but he had sent ahead good deeds. ﴿He would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾: the belly of the fish would have been his grave until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Then We cast him onto the open shore﴾: We threw him. Al-Kalbi said: it means the face of the earth. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: the surface of the earth. Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: the open deserts of the earth. Al-Akhfash said: the open space. Al-Farra' said: the wide earth. Al-Suddi said: the shore. The root of al-'ara' is land empty of trees and plants, and from it is said of one who is stripped bare: "naked." The poet said:

[He left the heads ... on the open ground ... became a barrier for the good, the 'abaq]

[The text is as it stands in the manuscript.]

﴿While he was sick﴾: ailing, like a featherless young bird. They differed about how long Jonah remained in the belly of the fish. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: three days. Ata': seven days. Al-Dahhak: twenty days. Al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and Muqatil ibn Sulayman: forty days.

﴿And We caused to grow over him﴾: over him, meaning for him; it was also said: near him, as in the saying of Allah, ﴿they have a claim against me﴾, meaning with me. ﴿A gourd plant﴾: Ibn Mas'ud said: it means the pumpkin. Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Muqatil said: it is any plant that spreads and stretches over the surface of the earth, does not survive the winter, and has no stalk, such as cucumber, watermelon, pumpkin and colocynth. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is anything that grows and then dies within the same year. It was also said: the word is from the form yaf'il, from "qatana bil-makan," meaning he stayed in a place, a temporary stay, not a permanent one. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: he would shade himself under the plant, and a wild goat would come to him and he would drink from its milk.

﴿And We sent him﴾: it may be that this refers to his sending after his confinement in the belly of the fish, the sense of the verse being "and We had sent him." It may also be that it refers to what came after, or that he was sent to another people. ﴿To a hundred thousand or more﴾: Ibn Abbas said: the meaning is "or more," and he cited the poet:

[When the war grew fierce among us ... we considered Riyah or Rizam]

Meaning "and Rizam." Muqatil said: rather, "they increase." They differed about the amount of the increase over one hundred thousand. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: twenty thousand. Al-Hasan and al-Rabi': some thirty-odd thousand. Ibn Hayyan: seventy thousand. ﴿So they believed﴾ when they saw the punishment, ﴿and We let them enjoy for a time﴾: until the end of their terms.

﴿So ask them﴾: ask, O Muhammad, the people of Makkah. ﴿Has your Lord daughters while they have sons?﴾ This is because the Juhaynah and the Banu Salamah ibn Abd al-Dar claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah. ﴿Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?﴾: present, having witnessed Our creating them. Its parallel is His words, ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾ (Qur'an 43:19).

﴿Is it not that they say out of their own falsehood: "Allah has begotten"? And indeed they are liars.﴾ Ibn Kathir's readers: the majority read the hamza of ﴿asṭafā﴾ with a cut (qat' al-hamza), because it is an interrogative alif placed before the alif of connection; the alif of connection was dropped and the interrogative alif remained open as it is, like the words ﴿astakbarta﴾ (Qur'an 38:75), ﴿astaghfarta﴾ (Qur'an 63:6), ﴿adhhabtum﴾ (Qur'an 46:20), and similar forms.
