Abu Ja'far and Nafi', in some transmissions, read ﴿al-kadhibūna, iṣṭafā﴾ with connection, as a report and narration of the words of the polytheists. Its sense is: "they say Allah has begotten, and they say He chose daughters over sons." Then the address returns to the second person: ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge? Will you not then remember? Or do you have a clear authority?﴾: a manifest proof that Allah has offspring. ﴿So bring your Book, if you are truthful.﴾

﴿And they made between Him and the jinn a kinship﴾: they made the angels the daughters of Allah, and the angels were called jinn because they are hidden from sight. This is the view of Mujahid and Qatadah. Ibn Abbas said: they said of a tribe among the angels, called the jinn, among whom is Iblis, that they are the daughters of Allah. Al-Kalbi said: they said (may Allah curse them): "Rather, He married among the jinn, and the angels came from them," exalted is Allah far above that, a great exaltation. Al-Hasan said: they associated Satan with Allah in worship, and that is the kinship they devised.

﴿And the jinn know that they will surely be brought forward﴾: meaning the speakers of this saying, to the Fire.

﴿Glory be to Allah above what they describe, except the chosen servants of Allah﴾: for they are saved from the Fire. ﴿Indeed you, and what you worship﴾: meaning the idols, ﴿are not able to lead astray against Him﴾, meaning with that, ﴿except one who is to burn in Hell﴾, that is, except one who, in Allah's knowledge and will, will enter the Fire.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: al-Firyabi narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, from Umar ibn Dharr, who said: We came to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, and qadar was mentioned in his presence. Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said: "If Allah had willed that He not be disobeyed, He would not have created Iblis, who is the head of sin. In that is knowledge from the Book of Allah. Whoever is ignorant of it is ignorant, and whoever knows it knows it." Then he recited, ﴿Indeed you, and what you worship, are not able to lead astray against Him, except one who is to burn in Hell.﴾ And this verse has distinguished between people.

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: al-Firyabi narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Musa al-Ansari narrated to us, saying: Anas ibn Iyad narrated to us, saying: Abu Suhayl Nafi' ibn Malik ibn Abi Amir narrated to me, saying: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said to me (from his mouth to my ear): "What do you say about those who say there is no qadar?" He said: "I think they should be asked to repent; if they repent, well, otherwise their necks should be struck." Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said: "That is the ruling concerning them. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾" [106] [Al-Adhkar of al-Nawawi: 299, no. 889.]

[Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: al-Hasan al-Mukhallidi, the reciter, informed us, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ahmad, from Abu [Uthman] al-Basri, from Abu Khalifah [al-Jumahi, from] Abd al-Mu'min, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq [from Abd al-Samad], from Salih ibn Musafir, who said: I recited Surat al-Saffat to Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, and when I reached its end I stopped. He said: "Why? Recite." I said: "I have finished." He said: "I did as I did with Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, and Abu Abd al-Rahman said: 'Ali said this to me as well, and said: Say: ﴿I have proclaimed to you the proclamation of the messengers﴾, and ﴿you will surely be questioned about the great news﴾.'" And indeed Jonah was among the messengers. ﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾ (Ibn Abbas and Wahb said: Jonah had promised his people the punishment. When the punishment was delayed from them, he left them in anger and set out for the sea, boarded a ship, and the ship was held fast. The sailors said: "There is a runaway slave here from his master. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿and he drew lots﴾: he cast lots. ﴿Then the great fish swallowed him﴾: it swallowed him, and Allah revealed to him that He had made his belly a prison and had not made him its food. ﴿And he was blameworthy﴾: at fault, having done what deserved blame.

﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify Allah﴾: those who declare Allah free of imperfection and remember Him before that, in times of ease. Ibn Abbas said: those who pray. Muqatil said: those who are righteous and obedient before disobedience. Wahb said: those who worship. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means his words, ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers﴾ (Qur'an 21:87). ﴿Then We cast him onto the open shore﴾: We threw him. Al-Kalbi said: it means the face of the earth. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: the surface of the earth. Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: the open deserts of the earth. Al-Akhfash said: the open space. Al-Farra' said: the wide earth. Al-Suddi said: the shore. The root of al-'ara' is land empty of trees and plants, and from it is said of one who is stripped bare: "naked." The poet said:

[He left the heads ... on the open ground ... became a barrier for the good, the 'abaq]

[The text is as it stands in the manuscript.]

﴿While he was sick﴾: ailing, like a featherless young bird. They differed about how long Jonah remained in the belly of the fish. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: three days. Ata': seven days. Al-Dahhak: twenty days. Al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and Muqatil ibn Sulayman: forty days.

﴿And We caused to grow over him﴾: over him, meaning for him; it was also said: near him, as in the saying of Allah, ﴿they have a claim against me﴾, meaning with me. ﴿A gourd plant﴾: Ibn Mas'ud said: it means the pumpkin. Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Muqatil said: it is any plant that spreads and stretches over the surface of the earth, does not survive the winter, and has no stalk, such as cucumber, watermelon, pumpkin and colocynth. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is anything that grows and then dies within the same year. It was also said: the word is from the form yaf'il, from "qatana bil-makan," meaning he stayed in a place, a temporary stay, not a permanent one. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: he would shade himself under the plant, and a wild goat would come to him and he would drink from its milk.

﴿And We sent him﴾: it may be that this refers to his sending after his confinement in the belly of the fish, the sense of the verse being "and We had sent him." It may also be that it refers to what came after, or that he was sent to another people. ﴿To a hundred thousand or more﴾: Ibn Abbas said: the meaning is "or more," and he cited the poet:

[When the war grew fierce among us ... we considered Riyah or Rizam]

Meaning "and Rizam." Muqatil said: rather, "they increase." They differed about the amount of the increase over one hundred thousand. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: twenty thousand. Al-Hasan and al-Rabi': some thirty-odd thousand. Ibn Hayyan: seventy thousand. ﴿So they believed﴾ when they saw the punishment, ﴿and We let them enjoy for a time﴾: until the end of their terms.

﴿So ask them﴾: ask, O Muhammad, the people of Makkah. ﴿Has your Lord daughters while they have sons?﴾ This is because the Juhaynah and the Banu Salamah ibn Abd al-Dar claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah. ﴿Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?﴾: present, having witnessed Our creating them. Its parallel is His words, ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾ (Qur'an 43:19).

﴿Is it not that they say out of their own falsehood: "Allah has begotten"? And indeed they are liars.﴾ Ibn Kathir's readers: the majority read the hamza of ﴿asṭafā﴾ with a cut (qat' al-hamza), because it is an interrogative alif placed before the alif of connection; the alif of connection was dropped and the interrogative alif remained open as it is, like the words ﴿astakbarta﴾ (Qur'an 38:75), ﴿astaghfarta﴾ (Qur'an 63:6), ﴿adhhabtum﴾ (Qur'an 46:20), and similar forms.

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: al-Firyabi narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Musa al-Ansari narrated to us, saying: Anas ibn Iyad narrated to us, saying: Abu Suhayl Nafi' ibn Malik ibn Abi Amir narrated to me, saying: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said to me (from his mouth to my ear): "What do you say about those who say there is no qadar?" And peace be upon the messengers. And praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾" [106] [Al-Adhkar of al-Nawawi: 299, no. 889.]

[Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: al-Hasan al-Mukhallidi, the reciter, informed us, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ahmad, from Abu [Uthman] al-Basri, from Abu Khalifah [al-Jumahi, from] Abd al-Mu'min, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq [from Abd al-Samad], from Salih ibn Musafir, who said: I recited Surat al-Saffat to Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, and when I reached its end I stopped. He said: "Why? Recite." I said: "I have finished." He said: "I did as I did with Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, and Abu Abd al-Rahman said: 'Ali said this to me as well, and said: Say: ﴿I have proclaimed to you the proclamation of the messengers﴾, and ﴿you will surely be questioned about the great news﴾.'" And indeed Jonah was among the messengers. ﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾ (Ibn Abbas and Wahb said: Jonah had promised his people the punishment. When the punishment was delayed from them, he left them in anger and set out for the sea, boarded a ship, and the ship was held fast. The sailors said: "There is a runaway slave here from his master. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿and he drew lots﴾: he cast lots. ﴿Then the great fish swallowed him﴾: it swallowed him, and Allah revealed to him that He had made his belly a prison and had not made him its food. ﴿And he was blameworthy﴾: at fault, having done what deserved blame.

﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify Allah﴾: those who declare Allah free of imperfection and remember Him before that, in times of ease. Ibn Abbas said: those who pray. Muqatil said: those who are righteous and obedient before disobedience. Wahb said: those who worship. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means his words, ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers﴾ (Qur'an 21:87). ﴿Then We cast him onto the open shore﴾: We threw him. Al-Kalbi said: it means the face of the earth. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: the surface of the earth. Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: the open deserts of the earth. Al-Akhfash said: the open space. Al-Farra' said: the wide earth. Al-Suddi said: the shore. The root of al-'ara' is land empty of trees and plants, and from it is said of one who is stripped bare: "naked." The poet said:

[He left the heads ... on the open ground ... became a barrier for the good, the 'abaq]

[The text is as it stands in the manuscript.]

﴿While he was sick﴾: ailing, like a featherless young bird. They differed about how long Jonah remained in the belly of the fish. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: three days. Ata': seven days. Al-Dahhak: twenty days. Al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and Muqatil ibn Sulayman: forty days.

﴿And We caused to grow over him﴾: over him, meaning for him; it was also said: near him, as in the saying of Allah, ﴿they have a claim against me﴾, meaning with me. ﴿A gourd plant﴾: Ibn Mas'ud said: it means the pumpkin. Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Muqatil said: it is any plant that spreads and stretches over the surface of the earth, does not survive the winter, and has no stalk, such as cucumber, watermelon, pumpkin and colocynth. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is anything that grows and then dies within the same year. It was also said: the word is from the form yaf'il, from "qatana bil-makan," meaning he stayed in a place, a temporary stay, not a permanent one. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: he would shade himself under the plant, and a wild goat would come to him and he would drink from its milk.

﴿And We sent him﴾: it may be that this refers to his sending after his confinement in the belly of the fish, the sense of the verse being "and We had sent him." It may also be that it refers to what came after, or that he was sent to another people. ﴿To a hundred thousand or more﴾: Ibn Abbas said: the meaning is "or more," and he cited the poet:

[When the war grew fierce among us ... we considered Riyah or Rizam]

Meaning "and Rizam." Muqatil said: rather, "they increase." They differed about the amount of the increase over one hundred thousand. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: twenty thousand. Al-Hasan and al-Rabi': some thirty-odd thousand. Ibn Hayyan: seventy thousand. ﴿So they believed﴾ when they saw the punishment, ﴿and We let them enjoy for a time﴾: until the end of their terms.

﴿So ask them﴾: ask, O Muhammad, the people of Makkah. ﴿Has your Lord daughters while they have sons?﴾ This is because the Juhaynah and the Banu Salamah ibn Abd al-Dar claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah. ﴿Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?﴾: present, having witnessed Our creating them. Its parallel is His words, ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾ (Qur'an 43:19).

﴿Is it not that they say out of their own falsehood: "Allah has begotten"? And indeed they are liars.﴾ Ibn Kathir's readers: the majority read the hamza of ﴿asṭafā﴾ with a cut (qat' al-hamza), because it is an interrogative alif placed before the alif of connection; the alif of connection was dropped and the interrogative alif remained open as it is, like the words ﴿astakbarta﴾ (Qur'an 38:75), ﴿astaghfarta﴾ (Qur'an 63:6), ﴿adhhabtum﴾ (Qur'an 46:20), and similar forms.

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: al-Firyabi narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Musa al-Ansari narrated to us, saying: Anas ibn Iyad narrated to us, saying: Abu Suhayl Nafi' ibn Malik ibn Abi Amir narrated to me, saying: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said to me (from his mouth to my ear): "What do you say about those who say there is no qadar?" And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: al-Firyabi narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Musa al-Ansari narrated to us, saying: Anas ibn Iyad narrated to us, saying: Abu Suhayl Nafi' ibn Malik ibn Abi Amir narrated to me, saying: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said to me (from his mouth to my ear): "What do you say about those who say there is no qadar?" By Allah, even if there were only this one verse, it would suffice: ﴿Indeed you, and what you worship, are not able to lead astray against Him, except one who is to burn in Hell.﴾"

﴿There is none of us but has a known station﴾: meaning, except one who has a specific place in worship. Ibn Abbas said: there is not a span of space in the heavens but that an angel is upon it, either praying or glorifying Allah. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "Except that he has a known station in which he worships Allah, such as fear and hope, love and contentment." Al-Suddi said: it means nearness and witnessing.

﴿And indeed we are those who stand in rows﴾ in prayer, ﴿and indeed we are those who glorify﴾.

﴿And indeed they were about to say﴾, meaning the people of Makkah, ﴿if only we had a reminder from the former peoples﴾: a book like their books, ﴿we would have been the chosen servants of Allah.﴾ ﴿But they disbelieved in it﴾: there is an ellipsis here; its sense is: when that Book came to them, they disbelieved in it. And indeed Jonah was among the messengers. ﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾ (Ibn Abbas and Wahb said: Jonah had promised his people the punishment. When the punishment was delayed from them, he left them in anger and set out for the sea, boarded a ship, and the ship was held fast. The sailors said: "There is a runaway slave here from his master. This is the custom of a ship: if there is a runaway aboard, it does not sail." So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah. They said: "Shall we not throw him into the water?" They cast lots a second and a third time, and the lot fell on Jonah. He said: "I am the runaway," and he threw himself into the water. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿and he drew lots﴾: he cast lots. Al-musahama is the casting of arrows by way of lottery.) ﴿So he was among the losers﴾: those defeated by lot, those cast down, those overcome.

﴿Then the great fish swallowed him﴾: it swallowed him, and Allah revealed to him that He had made his belly a prison and had not made him its food. ﴿And he was blameworthy﴾: at fault, having done what deserved blame.

﴿Had he not been one of those who glorify Allah﴾: those who declare Allah free of imperfection and remember Him before that, in times of ease. Ibn Abbas said: those who pray. Muqatil said: those who are righteous and obedient before disobedience. Wahb said: those who worship. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means his words, ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers﴾ (Qur'an 21:87). Al-Hasan said: he had no prayer in the belly of the fish, but he had sent ahead good deeds. ﴿He would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected﴾: the belly of the fish would have been his grave until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Then We cast him onto the open shore﴾: We threw him. Al-Kalbi said: it means the face of the earth. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: the surface of the earth. Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: the open deserts of the earth. Al-Akhfash said: the open space. Al-Farra' said: the wide earth. Al-Suddi said: the shore. The root of al-'ara' is land empty of trees and plants, and from it is said of one who is stripped bare: "naked." The poet said:

[He left the heads ... on the open ground ... became a barrier for the good, the 'abaq]

[The text is as it stands in the manuscript.]

﴿While he was sick﴾: ailing, like a featherless young bird. They differed about how long Jonah remained in the belly of the fish. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: three days. Ata': seven days. Al-Dahhak: twenty days. Al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and Muqatil ibn Sulayman: forty days.

﴿And We caused to grow over him﴾: over him, meaning for him; it was also said: near him, as in the saying of Allah, ﴿they have a claim against me﴾, meaning with me. ﴿A gourd plant﴾: Ibn Mas'ud said: it means the pumpkin. Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Muqatil said: it is any plant that spreads and stretches over the surface of the earth, does not survive the winter, and has no stalk, such as cucumber, watermelon, pumpkin and colocynth. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is anything that grows and then dies within the same year. It was also said: the word is from the form yaf'il, from "qatana bil-makan," meaning he stayed in a place, a temporary stay, not a permanent one. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: he would shade himself under the plant, and a wild goat would come to him and he would drink from its milk.

﴿And We sent him﴾: it may be that this refers to his sending after his confinement in the belly of the fish, the sense of the verse being "and We had sent him." It may also be that it refers to what came after, or that he was sent to another people. ﴿To a hundred thousand or more﴾: Ibn Abbas said: the meaning is "or more," and he cited the poet:

[When the war grew fierce among us ... we considered Riyah or Rizam]

Meaning "and Rizam." Muqatil said: rather, "they increase." They differed about the amount of the increase over one hundred thousand. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: twenty thousand. Al-Hasan and al-Rabi': some thirty-odd thousand. Ibn Hayyan: seventy thousand. ﴿So they believed﴾ when they saw the punishment, ﴿and We let them enjoy for a time﴾: until the end of their terms.

﴿So ask them﴾: ask, O Muhammad, the people of Makkah. ﴿Has your Lord daughters while they have sons?﴾ This is because the Juhaynah and the Banu Salamah ibn Abd al-Dar claimed that the angels are the daughters of Allah. ﴿Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?﴾: present, having witnessed Our creating them. Its parallel is His words, ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾ (Qur'an 43:19).

﴿Is it not that they say out of their own falsehood: "Allah has begotten"? And indeed they are liars.﴾ Ibn Kathir's readers: the majority read the hamza of ﴿asṭafā﴾ with a cut (qat' al-hamza), because it is an interrogative alif placed before the alif of connection; the alif of connection was dropped and the interrogative alif remained open as it is, like the words ﴿astakbarta﴾ (Qur'an 38:75), ﴿astaghfarta﴾ (Qur'an 63:6), ﴿adhhabtum﴾ (Qur'an 46:20), and similar forms.

Abu Ja'far and Nafi', in some transmissions, read ﴿al-kadhibūna, iṣṭafā﴾ with connection, as a report and narration of the words of the polytheists. Its sense is: "they say Allah has begotten, and they say He chose daughters over sons." Then the address returns to the second person: ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge? Will you not then remember? Or do you have a clear authority?﴾: a manifest proof that Allah has offspring. ﴿So bring your Book, if you are truthful.﴾

﴿And they made between Him and the jinn a kinship﴾: they made the angels the daughters of Allah, and the angels were called jinn because they are hidden from sight. This is the view of Mujahid and Qatadah. Ibn Abbas said: they said of a tribe among the angels, called the jinn, among whom is Iblis, that they are the daughters of Allah. Al-Kalbi said: they said (may Allah curse them): "Rather, He married among the jinn, and the angels came from them," exalted is Allah far above that, a great exaltation. Al-Hasan said: they associated Satan with Allah in worship, and that is the kinship they devised.

﴿And the jinn know that they will surely be brought forward﴾: meaning the speakers of this saying, to the Fire.

﴿Glory be to Allah above what they describe, except the chosen servants of Allah﴾: for they are saved from the Fire. ﴿Indeed you, and what you worship﴾: meaning the idols, ﴿are not able to lead astray against Him﴾, meaning with that, ﴿except one who is to burn in Hell﴾, that is, except one who, in Allah's knowledge and will, will enter the Fire.
